title: feat(post): work offsets ride the stream as a 1-based index; the post writes the word
body:
Slice 1 of 3 for #931: the post crate and scripts. Stacked on #945 (#934, Sinumerik G505/G506). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Effort: high.

**This changes the post interface** (what every script receives as `PARAM WorkOffset`), so it waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.

## What changed

- **The stream carries the index.** `dump` writes `PARAM WorkOffset` as the setup's 1-based offset number (`G55` -> `2`). App still hands the word and still caps at 6; slice 2 makes the `Dump` field an index.
- **New `workOffsetIndex` manifest flag** (`crates/post/src/post/work_offset.rs`, on the `coolantModes` pattern). It is read once at load with `workOffsetMax` (6 when unstated):
  - A flagged script receives the number. The engine refuses an offset above its maximum by setup name.
  - An unflagged (user) script receives the word `G54`..`G59` for 1-6, exactly as before. Any offset above 6 is refused by setup name, and an unflagged script cannot raise its own maximum.
  - The legacy words `G54`..`G59` in a stream still read as 1-6. Any other value (`G53`, 0, 2.5, `G54.1 P3`) is refused by setup name before a script sees it.
  - `work_offset::work_offsets(cps)` returns the maximum and the `workOffsetName(n)` names for slice 2's display. It never feeds the stream.
- **All 11 shipped scripts** declare the flag, `workOffsetMax` and `workOffsetName`, and map the index to their own word. No `slotOf` / `frameWord` / `frameOf` word parsing remains:
  - The Fanuc-family probe register reads `wcsIndex - 1`.
  - Sinumerik's `$P_UIFR[n]` uses the number directly.
  - Heidenhain maps offset n to preset row n.
- **Declared maxima:**
  - Tormach mill and Tormach lathe: **9** (`G59.1`..`G59.3`, cited to the LinuxCNC G-code reference: "G54-G59.3 Select Coordinate System (1 - 9)" and its G10 L2 table).
  - Every other dialect: **6**. Haas G154, Fanuc/Mazak/Doosan G54.1 P and further Sinumerik/Heidenhain frames or rows were not verified against a public manual, so none is written. Reasons and sources are in `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-post.md`.
- **Docs.** `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents the 1-based `WorkOffset` beside the probe's 0-based `SetWorkOffset` (triage point 4). `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describes the flag, the maximum and the name function.

## Tests

- New `crates/post/tests/work_offset_index.rs` (9 tests). Every shipped script runs on recorded streams at offsets 1, 6, 7, its maximum and one past it, checking the word it writes or the refusal by setup name. It also covers:
  - a recorded generator toolpath (`face_square_40x40.cl`) through Fanuc and Tormach;
  - legacy word streams posting byte-identically to their index;
  - invalid values;
  - an unflagged user script at 1-6 and at 7, and one that tries to raise its maximum;
  - a flagged script without a maximum or names;
  - the dump writing the index;
  - each script's name table.
- `sinumerik_work_offsets::sinumerik_refuses_a_work_offset_that_names_no_settable_frame` now expects the engine's refusal of `G53` (the engine refuses it before the script runs).
- Gate (local, worktree target, sccache), on head `2fe7afb7`:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 75 passed, 0 failed.
  - 63 app suites, 431 passed, 0 failed. They cover every app suite that posts through the shipped scripts: conformance, golden_cl, posting, arc_planes, cli, the probe_* suites, sinumerik_*, heidenhain_*, fanuc_post, doosan_dnm_post, carvera_*, tormach_*, the lathe_post* suites, plasma_*, inverted_*, comment_escape, one_wcs, setups, setup_wcs, setup_defines_wcs, rotated_wcs, setup_mounts_post, setup_post_options, per_op_files, program_comments, smoothing, after_op, coolant*, post_unit_word, regression_models, wear_comp, control_comp and lathe_spindle_law. There are no separate mazak or haas suites; those scripts are covered by conformance, fanuc_post and the inverted_* suites.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- 400-line law: the new manifest reading lives in its own module, `work_offset.rs`. `engine.rs` (511 -> 530 lines) and `js.rs` (409 -> 415) were already over 400 and grew only by the hook-up.

**Goldens:** no golden file changed. Offsets 1-6 post the same words as before.

**Not exercised:** the GUI and MCP (unchanged in this slice), a real control, and offsets above 6 end to end through app (app still caps at 6 until slice 2).

Changelog: Posts receive the work offset as a 1-based number and write their own word; the Tormach mill and lathe posts accept work offsets 7-9 (G59.1-G59.3), and a post that cannot express an offset refuses it by setup name (#931, slice 1)

Refs #931

title: feat(tools): .camtools carries the tool body; "Import tool holders" toggle
body:
## What changed

- **Format (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs`)**: a `.camtools` tool's `definition` may carry `body`, the same `ToolBodyDto` a `.camproj` tool stores (a drawn holder profile, a placed mesh, or a lathe holder). The key is additive: `camcraft-tools/1` stays, files without it read unchanged, and older builds ignore it. Export writes the body of every tool that has one. On read, a body is checked the way the project loader checks one: `ToolBodyDto::to_body` re-derives it and `tool_body::fits` must accept it. If either refuses, the whole file is refused and the tool is named. The clean-room note stays as it was.
- **Command (`commands/tool_import.rs`)**: `ImportTools::with_holders(world, library, holders)` is still one undoable command. `ImportTools::new` is the same call with holders on. With holders on, each body is checked again at command creation. With holders off, every tool lands bare (holder cylinder only). The duplicate and rename rules are unchanged. The body counts toward "identical" only when one lands: a bare library tool matches the document's tool on its record alone, as before, and a tool that lands with a body must match the body too, otherwise it arrives as "Name (2)". `ImportReport` gains `holders` and `holders_left_out`, and both appear on the status line.
- **UI (Tool library page)**: an "Import tool holders" checkbox next to Import library, ticked by default. It is passed to the command as its `holders` parameter and remembered per user in the prefs file (`importToolHolders`, written only when off), the same way as #877. It is not project state and not on the history.
- **MCP**: `import_tool_library` takes an optional `holders` boolean (default true). The schema and description are updated, and the reply adds `holders` and `holders_left_out`. The script verb `cam.importTools(path)` keeps its arity (holders on).
- **Process**: the `import_tool_library` line in the camcraft-mcp skill is updated, so `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 16 -> 17. Other open process PRs also claim 17-20; whichever merges later takes the next number when it merges main.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/889-camtools-holder-body.md`.

## How tested (local, macOS, debug, sccache; fork synced at v0.18.0)

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/tool_library_holders.rs` (new, 5 tests):
  - `export_import_with_holders_is_byte_stable` covers a drawn BT30 ER20 body and a mesh body; export -> import -> export gives identical bytes and the bodies are bit-identical.
  - `holders_off_lands_every_tool_bare_and_undo_restores`
  - `a_malformed_or_ill_fitting_body_refuses_the_file_by_name` covers a non-body, a bad outline, a mesh with no placement, and flutes running into the holder; nothing is applied and nothing goes on the history.
  - `a_file_without_bodies_imports_as_before_and_the_skip_reads_bodies_only_when_one_lands`
  - `mcp_import_tool_library_takes_the_holders_flag` covers the schema, off, the default on, the round trip over MCP, and refusal of a non-boolean.
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs`: `the_tool_holder_import_choice_survives_a_restart`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/tool_library_import.rs`: `the_toggle_stands_on_the_page_ticked_and_is_remembered_per_user` (AccessKit CheckBox role and toggled state, prefs written, not dirty) and `unticked_imports_bare_ticked_takes_the_holder_and_undo_restores`.

Suites, all green:

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| tool_library | 13 |
| tool_library_holders | 5 |
| view_prefs | 7 |
| holder_library | 11 |
| tool_body | 12 |
| tool_body_bands | 13 |
| tool_body_judged | 8 |
| tool_body_view | 7 |
| project_roundtrip | 71 |
| mcp | 13 |
| camcraft-ui lib, `--test-threads=1` | 533 passed, 5 ignored |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. No snapshot PNGs changed.

## Not exercised

- The real file dialog and click-through in a live window.
- The holder count is shown after the import (status line and MCP reply), not before it, because the toggle stands on the page before any file is picked. The decision file explains this.
- The drawn cutter outline (`ToolCutter`) and a holder-library entry name are not carried; see the decision file.

Changelog: Tool library files (.camtools) carry each tool's holder body; the Tool library page's "Import tool holders" toggle (and MCP `import_tool_library` `holders`) chooses whether an import takes them (#889)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at v0.18.0

Fixes #889

title: fix(thread): a matched thread mill verifies clean - the gouge laws read its major circle
body:
#1071: a Thread op's helix runs the thread depth H = 0.5413 x pitch past the declared hole, which is the thread's minor circle (what CAD draws of a tapped hole), by design (`machining2d::thread_mill`). The verify read that hole as a wall the cutter must keep `r` from, so every matched thread mill was blocked.

That covered the stock source too, which the issue thought was unaffected: the same thread from `SrcRef::Stock` had 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs. `mill2d_c` never asserted the warnings, so no thread mill could post from any source.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 16; branched on upstream main 23c62044.

## What changed

Three laws convicted a matched thread, and each is fixed narrowly.

- **Law (b), the rim.** The Thread arm now moves each declared hole's rim out to the major circle (declared radius + H), after the region is built (`material_source::major_rims`). This covers every source and the area-controlled region. A loop that is the hole's minor rim (ours, or the model's own for a through hole) gives way to it; every other wall stays.
- **The containment solid law.** It read the model's minor wall, and the face the hole opens through, as part to keep. A new `sim::verify::thread_bore` (and `solid_hits_threaded`) excuses a hit only when both of these hold:
  - the facet is the thread's own material: the minor wall (near-vertical, every vertex on the declared circle within max(2 % r, 0.1 mm)), or a facet with a vertex on that circle lying wholly at or above the hole's entry (the mouth);
  - the swept cutter stays inside the major cylinder: the farther tip end's radius plus the atom's radius is at most the major radius plus the allowance.

  Floors, walls of another radius, other holes and any cut past the major circle still convict. `solid_hits` is unchanged: it calls the threaded form with no bores.
- **Law (a), crossings.** The retract runs the ride backwards at feed. The reversed arcs put their chord joints a last bit off their twins, and `proper_cross` excused a touch only at an exactly zero orientation. So each shared joint, and each collinear overlap, read as a crossing.

  Now chords that only touch (an endpoint within 1 nm of the other chord's line) are no crossing. A real crossing keeps every endpoint off the other line. This is the one change that reaches every operation's verify, so the whole batch tier was run (below). A parallel-only guard was tried first: it removed 5 of the 21 pairs, and the rest were the joint touches.
- Two functions now take eight arguments (`SolidIndex::hits`, `contain_into`). They carry `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` with a reason, as ten others in `sim` already do.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1071-thread-mill-rim.md`.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/thread_mill_rim.rs` (a 6 mm Tap-form thread mill, pitch 1, model-sourced unless named):
  - `a_matched_thread_mill_in_air_verifies_clean`: the issue's cavity fixture (#1073's block). Before the fix: 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs.
  - `a_matched_thread_mill_in_a_drilled_hole_verifies_clean`: a block with a real r 5 blind hole, 96-gon. Before the fix: the gouges came back from the solid law at the wall and the mouth.
  - `a_stock_sourced_thread_mill_verifies_clean_too`.
  - `a_thread_whose_major_circle_reaches_a_wall_convicts`: the major circle is 0.24 mm into the cavity wall; the minor circle is clear of it.
  - `a_thread_declared_wider_than_the_models_hole_convicts`: the model drilled r 4.5, declared r 5.
  - `a_thread_taken_below_the_models_hole_floor_convicts`: floor declared at Z 9, model floor at Z 10.
- `crates/sim/tests/crossing_retrace.rs`:
  - `a_helix_run_back_over_its_own_trace_is_no_crossing`: three ride/retrace shapes, all-pairs and bucketed. It fails with the touch guard removed, which was checked.
  - `a_real_crossing_still_reads_as_one_at_any_angle`: 90 degrees down to 0.001 rad.

Gates:
- `cargo xtask gate batch` on c770b35c (18.3 min): every test suite green.
  - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim (with `crossing_buckets`), motion (slow suites included), app (`center_cut_multiaxis` included), ui.
  - clippy failed only on the two eight-argument functions. With the `#[allow]` (head commit), `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- On the head, both pinning suites were rerun: green.
- No snapshot PNG touched.

## Not exercised

- No posted thread program was run on a machine or simulator.
- The thread flanks are not modelled: the whole minor-to-major annulus is read as removable (#986 owns the form).
- A tilted-frame (indexed) thread uses the same code path, but no test pins it.
- #1073's `coarse_rims::a_thread_mill_reads_the_same_near_the_bound_as_at_full_fidelity` lives on that open PR. When both land it can tighten to `== Vec::new()`, as #1071 asks.

Changelog: Thread milling: a thread mill matched to its hole verifies clean and can be posted. The gouge checks now read the thread's major circle, and the retract is no longer read as a crossing (#1071)

Effort: high (the issue's label). Not escalated.

Fixes #1071

title: fix(verify): the rapid law reads the stock's top under the rapid, not its highest point
body:
**Stacked on #1077.** Until #1077 merges, this diff also shows #1077's commits. Merge #1077 first. Branched from #1077's head `c6c658db` with `origin/main` (`23c62044`) merged in.

## What changed

Law (d) (#96, `RapidInStock`) caps every column at `stock_top_z`, the stock's highest point. On a stepped "from model" or carried stock, a Bore's entry dive to just above the low part was convicted as if the boss stood there too, and the post was blocked for a legal program.

- **`crates/sim/src/verify/stock_top.rs` (new): `verify::acquit_by_stock_top`.** It works like `acquit_by_prior`: it re-reads the convictions the column law gave **upright vertical rapids down**, in column modes only (radial, revolved and rotary are excluded), and it can only **remove** a conviction. A dive is acquitted only when every band of the tool stack ends above the highest vertex of every stock or part facet whose plan comes within that band's disc:
  - the flute at its full radius (no `- gouge_tol`, no ball lift), from the tip;
  - the shank, from the flute's top;
  - the holder, from the shank's top.

  On a closed mesh this is an exact upper bound on the material in the disc, and slopes read high. It fails closed: a non-finite stack number, or a flute disc that meets no facet, leaves the conviction standing.
- **Closed-shell gate (review fix, `crates/sim/src/verify/stock_top_shell.rs`).** The bound holds only on a closed surface, so a solid that fails this gate keeps the conviction. To pass, a solid must:
  - be non-empty, with every vertex finite;
  - have no facet that is degenerate in 3-D;
  - use every undirected edge (endpoints matched exactly) in **exactly two facets, once in each direction**;
  - form one edge-connected shell;
  - have a positive signed volume.

  Open shells, non-manifold or duplicated edges, inside-out or split solids all keep the conviction. The check runs once per solid per operation, in O(F) with an edge hash map, never per rapid. It does not test self-intersection: the ray argument behind the bound holds for any closed surface, self-intersecting or not (see the decision file).
- **`crates/app/src/operation/stock_top_law.rs` (new)** is the wiring. The solids are #1077's `judged_stock` (the setup's or carried stock, or the stock itself for a stock-sourced Bore/Thread) plus the op's own material. With no judged stock (the op's region stood in for it), every conviction stands. It is called at both `VerifyContext` sites in `generate.rs` (+6 lines net), before `acquit_by_prior`. The 3+2 site passes the plane's local facets.
- The column law itself (`rapids.rs`, `Rest::surface_before`) is unchanged, so lateral rapids, the posed and radial readings and the solid law keep their verdicts. Thread's descent is a vertical rapid and goes through the same re-reading.

## Readings

The reproduction uses **stock only**. The casting is set as from-model stock and then deleted from the tree (the stock keeps its copy), because a casting left in the tree is judged as a part by the program verdict. That is the reviewer's second refusal, filed as #1094. The casting is solid to Z 20 over a 16 mm hole, with a boss to Z 30 at x 18..28. Before the fix, the part-sourced Bore's dive to Z 22 gave `[RapidInStock { at: 0 }]`. I confirmed this again after the fix by disabling the wiring: the pin fails. After the fix it is silent and the program posts, for the part-sourced and the stock-sourced Bore alike.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/stepped_stock_rapid.rs` (new suite, 4 tests, each run for a part-sourced and a stock-sourced Bore):
  - `a_dive_over_the_low_part_of_a_stepped_stock_passes_and_posts`
  - `the_same_dive_with_the_boss_under_it_is_convicted`: convicted, and the post is blocked by the rapid law.
  - `a_boss_reaching_into_the_tool_footprint_is_convicted`: the boss edge is 1.5 mm beside the dive's centre, under the 4 mm rim.
  - `an_open_stock_mesh_proves_nothing_and_the_dive_stays_convicted`: the review's case (the boss over the hole without its top facets) is convicted and the post is blocked. It fails with the gate off.
- `sim::verify::stock_top::tests` (12 tests): the low step of a closed single-shell stepped stock is acquitted; a boss over the dive, or under the rim only, stands; a holder band over the boss on a stubby tool stands; a part under the dive counts; an open shell, a non-manifold or duplicated edge, a degenerate facet, an inside-out or split solid, an empty solid and a non-finite vertex all keep the conviction; posed and lateral dives and the radial, revolved and rotary modes are never re-read.

## How tested

All green:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test stepped_stock_rapid --test ladder_entry_height --test operations --test golden_cl` | 4 / 4 / 117 (6 ignored) / 25 passed (`drill_rplane` 8, `top_stock` 4 at the first head) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --lib verify` | 23 passed |
| sim `vertical_rapids` / `sideways_rapids` / `posed_rapids` / `radial_rapids` | 16 / 3 / 5 / 15 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` | green on `6440858b`: 4 steps (sim 14 s, motion 9 s, app 808 s, ui 130 s), 0 failed, 16.1 min wall |

No goldens moved, and the existing rapid-law pins (`ladder_entry_height`, the #96 pins) are unchanged.

## Not exercised

- No end-to-end test of a 3+2 (tilted) Bore on a stepped stock, and none of Thread. Both go through the same sim reading, which is unit-pinned.
- No test of a carried stock with a boss. Its facets are the judged stock, so it goes through the same path.
- Imported meshes with T-junctions or vertices that are not welded bit for bit are not closed by this rule, so they keep the flat-cap verdict. That is a refusal, never a pass.
- Lateral rapids over a stepped stock still read the flat cap. They over-report and hide nothing (#1095).
- A model that is neither the op's source nor inside the stock (a second part poking up through a low step) is not among the solids. The flat cap did not read it there either.

Decision: `docs/decisions/1091-rapid-law-local-top.md`.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: The rapid-in-stock law reads the stock's top under a vertical dive instead of its highest point, so a legal entry dive over the low part of a stepped (from-model or carried) stock no longer blocks the post. A dive into the boss, or with the boss under the tool's rim or stack, is still refused.

Fixes #1091

title: fix(verify): a from-model stock's source is judged unless the user marks it raw stock only
body:
## What changed

**The default verdict is unchanged.** If the user does nothing, every non-fixture model is still judged as the part, exactly as before. A casting copied into a "from model" stock and left in the tree leaves the gouge verdict only when the user ticks **"The source model is raw stock only (not judged as the part)"** on the stock page (shown for a from-model stock).

The first push of this PR guessed which model was the part. The review reproduced a real 5 mm gouge posting with an empty gate (a stock made from the part itself, plus an unrelated model an op touches, live or suppressed). That guess is removed. The rule is now explicit:

- `SetStockSourceOnly` (new, `crates/app/src/commands/stock_source_only.rs`): one undoable step on the active setup's stock. It is refused by name when the stock is not made from a model. It writes `schema::StockSourceOnly { source }` on the stock entity.
- MCP `set_raw_stock_only { on }` (`crates/app/src/mcp/setup_tools.rs`) runs the same command.
- UI: a checkbox under the stock page's Source picker (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/raw_stock_row.rs`), which queues `CommandKind::SetRawStockOnly`.
- Project file: optional `raw_stock_only` on the stock row, absent = false. No version bump: an older reader drops the key and judges more, never less. An unmarked document saves as before.
- `stock_source::stock_only_model`: the marked source leaves the verdict only while every stock the program starts from is a copy of that model and carries the mark. A new `SetStock` source drops the mark's hold. Any operation (any setup, suppressed included) that names the model in its source or in a boundary pick puts it back in the verdict.
- `posting_sim`: when the mark leaves no other model, the post is refused by name ("nothing is judged as the part: ..."). A gouge refusal on the program stock's source adds one plain sentence pointing at the checkbox, or saying why the mark did not hold. That hint is the only inference left, and it changes no verdict.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/1094-stock-source-not-part.md`. It covers the explicit rule (orchestrator's direction, taken unattended), the dropped inference and clause-by-clause patches, reader-side vs refusing the mark, and refuse vs warn.

## Other readers of "every non-fixture model"

| Reader | Changed? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `simulate_document`, carry `judge`, field view, judged playback | yes, only when marked | all read `part_facets` / `parts_facets_in` |
| model-excess law `model_fidelity::verdict_tol` (#864/#911) | no | a coarse casting still tightens or refuses the verdict: a false refusal at worst |
| per-op collision / rapid / cross-drill laws | no | read the op's own source or the stock, not the document part set |
| rest material | no | reads the stock walk |
| alignment, picks, fixture clash, tree, GPU list | no | placement and display, not judgement |

## Tests

`crates/app/tests/stock_source_verdict.rs` (11, all pass):
- `a_stock_made_from_the_part_with_an_unrelated_model_beside_it_refuses_the_gouge`: the review's reproduction 1, which must refuse (default).
- `the_same_with_the_unrelated_op_suppressed_still_refuses`: the review's reproduction 2.
- `marked_an_op_naming_the_model_puts_it_back_in_the_verdict`: marked, plus an op (suppressed) naming the part. The gouge still blocks, and the hint says why.
- `marked_a_boundary_pick_on_the_model_puts_it_back_in_the_verdict`: the review's item 3.
- `unmarked_the_casting_is_judged_and_the_refusal_says_how_to_mark_it`: the issue's job, off. It refuses, with the hint.
- `marked_raw_stock_only_the_casting_leaves_the_verdict_and_the_program_posts`: the issue's job, on. It posts.
- `marked_the_separate_part_stays_judged_a_cut_below_its_floor_blocks`
- `a_mark_that_leaves_nothing_to_judge_refuses_by_name`
- `the_mark_undoes_redoes_and_a_new_stock_source_drops_its_hold`
- `the_mark_is_refused_on_a_stock_not_made_from_a_model`
- `the_mark_round_trips_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_judges_as_before`

Other new tests:
- `mcp_setup::set_raw_stock_only_marks_the_stock_source_through_the_command`: same command, undo, refusals.
- ui `egui_app::tests::raw_stock_row::the_stock_page_ticks_raw_stock_only_through_the_command_and_undo`: AccessKit label click, undo. Structural, no PNG.

body:

title: fix(post): an absent rotary takes no angle word (fanuc, doosan-dnm)
body:
**Stacked on #1002** (the #926 per-post script suites, whose recorded `rotary` golden pins this fix). This branch carries #1002's commit plus a merge of upstream `main`; merge #1002 first, then this PR's diff is only the #997 change. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

The RTCP path of `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` wrote all three angle words on the arm block whatever the machine stated - on the A+B tilthead, `G00 X0 Y0 Z20 A30 B0 C0`. A control with no C axis alarms on the C address (or, where C is another function, commands it).

- `statesRotary(letter)` reads `machine.rotaries`; `angleWord(letter, v)` writes a word only for a stated rotary. The arm block and the modal changed-letter words both go through it. Arm on the tilthead is now `G00 X0 Y0 Z20 A30 B0`.
- `missingLetter` (now built on `statesRotary`) still runs first, so a **turning** letter of an absent rotary stays refused by name (`tilted move commands C - the machine states no C rotary`). The only letters dropped are stated zeros.
- **Other posts checked:** haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain and carvera refuse a tilted stream outright (no RTCP output); tormach writes A only on its own index path; fanuc-lathe / tormach-lathe refuse posed moves. Only `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps` shared the bug (its RTCP path is a copy of fanuc's) - fixed here the same way.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/997-absent-rotary-word.md`.

## Goldens

- New: `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/fanuc/rotary.nc` (read before commit: G43.4 arm, `A30 B0`, modal `A0 B30`, return `B0`, no C word anywhere); the `("fanuc.cps", "rotary", 997)` line is removed from `KNOWN_BUGS`.
- Every other golden is byte-identical (no `.nc`/`.refusal`/`.cl` file changed). doosan-dnm's recorded `rotary` stays its refusal (no clamp codes declared), unchanged.
- One existing assertion changed: `fanuc_post::rtcp_output_arms_once_and_walks_the_angles` asserted `G00 X10 Y0 Z5 A40 B0 C0` on an **A-only** trunnion - it had pinned the bug. It now asserts `G00 X10 Y0 Z5 A40`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `script_fanuc::rotary` (the #926 recorded golden)
- `fanuc_post::an_absent_rotary_takes_no_angle_word` (tilthead: arm `A30 B0`, modal `A0 B30`, no C word; a turning C refused by name)
- `doosan_dnm_post::doosan_dnm_absent_rotary_takes_no_angle_word`

Gate (macOS, local, worktree target/, sccache):
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: post suites (lib, axis_direction_cli, comp, comp_plane, mch_head_search, post_engine, recorded_streams, every script_*) ok; app doosan_dnm_post, recorded_post_streams ok; fanuc_post failed once on the old word-count assertion below, fixed, then the whole `fanuc_post` suite 12/12 ok.
- App suites, whole: posting 17, golden_cl 25, conformance 6, tilt 8, fanuc_post 12, doosan_dnm_post 8, fourth_axis_pose 9, rotary_verify 9, recorded_post_streams 2 - all ok.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

`rtcp_output_arms_once_and_walks_the_angles` also asserted the modal block had fewer words than the arm block; on an A-only machine both now carry the single A word, so that comparison is dropped (the exact-line asserts still pin both blocks, and the modal law - unchanged angles rest, only the changed letter returns - is pinned by the new `fanuc/rotary.nc` golden: `G01 X20 Y0 Z0 F800`, `G00 X20 Y20 Z50 B0`).

## Not exercised

No hand-post on a real machine; the doosan fix is pinned only by its direct test (its recorded `rotary` case refuses earlier on undeclared clamp codes).

title: feat(sim): draw a turning tool's lathe body at the tool position
body:
**Stacked on #957** (issue #852, `issue/852-necked-tool-envelope`): this branch was cut from #957's head because both change `crates/app/src/sim_tool_body.rs`. Until #957 merges, this PR's diff also shows #957's commit (`54ed3fe7`); the #1038 change is the single commit on top (`feat(sim): draw a turning tool's lathe body at the tool position`). Retarget/merge order per AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack".

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (PROCESS_VERSION 16).

## What changed

Before, `sim_tool_body::for_operation` returned `Ok(None)` for every lathe-held kind, so the simulation and viewport showed only the axis marker for a turning tool, whatever body it carried. Now:

- **New `app::sim_lathe_body`.** It holds a pure pose (`posed(facets, tip, &LatheAxes)`), which maps a tool-frame point (x, y, z) to `tip + x*radial + y*(z x x) + z*along`, and a `LatheBodyCache`. The cache fetches the op's tool's lathe-frame body (`ToolBody::facets`, the same mesh `LatheClearance` is derived from) together with the frame it is judged in. It refits that frame only when the op, its path signature or the body (by `Arc` identity) changes, so the fit does not run every frame.
- **The frame is the holder law's own.** `operation::lathe_body_axes` (= `turning_holder::body_axes`) runs `Frame::about` on the op's source facets (`source_facets`, the read the law and the lathe stock sim use) and takes the radial from `SignedMeridian::of` on the cached path (a new `SignedMeridian::axes` accessor). As a result, every drawn vertex sits where the law reads it: sqrt((X + x)^2 + y^2) from the axis, at station S + z.
- **`SimToolCache::posed`** tries the lathe arm first. The ui seam (`world::sim_tool_tris`) is unchanged, so this adds no second drawing path. `for_operation` now also returns `Ok(None)` for a tool that carries a lathe-frame body, which covers a `Bore` with a lathe body: it is drawn as that body, not as the revolved bar stand-in.
- **A turning tool without a lathe body draws as before** (axis marker only). If the frame cannot be fitted, the refusal is logged once by name and nothing is drawn. No pose is guessed.
- **Display only.** No verdict, warning or posted output changes.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1038-lathe-body-in-sim.md`.

## Tests

Pinned by the new `crates/app/tests/sim_lathe_body.rs`:
- `an_od_holder_is_drawn_at_the_tip_radially_out_up_the_spindle`: OD finish ride with an OD shank, checked at several moves. Every drawn vertex equals its tool-frame vertex posed at the tip (+x along the path radial, +z up the spindle), matches the law's radius identity, and gives one drawn facet per body facet (not revolved).
- `an_id_bar_is_drawn_toward_the_axis_up_the_bore`: boring ride with a slim bar. Same vertex-by-vertex check; the bar stands inside the tip radius, its near corners at hypot(X - 4, 1.5), and it runs up the bore.
- `a_turning_tool_without_a_lathe_body_draws_as_before`: the bare insert draws nothing and the cache stays empty with no refusal.
- `a_new_body_is_drawn_at_once_and_the_frame_freed_with_the_transport`: reuse, rebuild on a new body, freed on `clear`.
- `the_pose_maps_each_tool_axis_onto_its_world_direction`: the pure pose on explicit axes, plus refusal of zero, non-finite and skew frames.

Also run: `sim_tool_body`, `tool_neck_laws`, `turning_holder`, `turning_insert_zone` and `tool_body` (all green), the full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

## Not exercised

- No live GUI check: nobody has stepped a turning op in the running app to look at the drawn body. The ui call path is unchanged and is covered by the existing `tool_body` ui test for milling only.
- Tinting the body on a `HolderHit` move (the issue's optional "could") is not done. It needs a colour channel on the sim body part; see the decision file.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

Effort: high

Changelog: Simulation and viewport draw a turning tool's imported lathe holder body at the tool position, posed in the frame the holder law judges it in (OD and ID), instead of only the axis marker (#1038)

Fixes #1038

title: test(gate): a motion generator change runs the operations suite
body:
## What

`crates/app/tests/operations.rs` generates every operation through the app layer, so its tests pin
the motion generators end to end — but its Gate map named `app::` modules only. A change under
`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/` therefore selected no suite that drives multiaxis rough end to end,
so `cargo xtask gate quick` could pass while
`multiaxis_rough_refuses_a_slot_the_cone_cannot_clear` sat out. PR #1044 hit exactly that: its gate
came out green and the failure surfaced only when a stacked merge ran the whole app list.

## The fix

- `operations.rs`'s Gate map names the generators its tests drive end to end:
  `motion::machining2d`, `motion::machining3d`, `motion::drilling`, `motion::finishing3d`,
  `motion::multiaxis`, `motion::plunge_law`.
- An xtask unit test pins both halves against this checkout: the map names every one of them, and a
  plan for `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/mod.rs` selects `app:operations`. A header that loses a name
  now fails in xtask's own suite instead of in a later PR's gate run.

## Process

`xtask/src/tests.rs` is a process file, so `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 16 → 17 (the same number
as the other open process PRs; whichever merges second renumbers on its merge of main).

## How tested

- `cargo test -p xtask` — 34 passed (new test included)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` — ok (app operations suite 49 s, xtask 2 s)
- Selection proof: with a one-line probe under `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/`,
  `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --plan` lists `app suites ... --test operations`;
  before the header change it listed motion suites only.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean

## Merge note

#965, #967, #972 and #1033 each rewrite the same `Gate map (M4.4)` line of `operations.rs` and
already name some of these modules. Whichever lands first, the other keeps both sets of names —
here `motion::machining3d`, `motion::multiaxis` and `motion::plunge_law` are the additions this PR
brings. The new xtask test catches a lost name.

Changelog: none
Fixes #1068

title: feat(fixtures): a rotary subplate on the plate grid raises the A centerline for the index swing
body:
**Stacked on #1020** (#818, `issue/818-swing-any-horizontal`): this branch starts from #1020's head, so until #1020 merges the diff below also shows its commit. Retarget/merge order per AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack". Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Works #821 as corrected by its 2026-11-11 comment: the microARC subplate does **not** turn with A - it is a base plate that mounts the rotary on a fixture plate (two pin bores) or on the T-slots. The safety core: the index-swing check (#804/#810/#818) assumed the machine file's `nose_to_axis` (10.6 in, rotary on the bare table), which is unconservative once a plate and subplate raise the A centerline.

## What changed

- **Rotary subplate** = a new built-in accessory kind `rotary_subplate` (`Accessory::RotarySubplate`: length, width, thickness, bore spacing, first bore from -X, bores from -Y, bore diameter). Generic default figures, named generic (10 x 6 x 3/4 in, 1/2 in bores 6 in apart) - no maker's dimensions committed; the user enters theirs. Solid-slab mesh (bores drawn solid). It lands **fixed** (never in the swept radius). Its frame is the first pin bore at the underside, +X toward the second, so `PlaceOnPlate` seats it on a #819 dowel pair by its pins.
- **Pin law:** a subplate goes only on a dowel pair whose spacing equals its bore spacing (0.05 mm); a single hole or another spacing is refused by name - at `PlaceOnPlate`, at a `SetPlate` re-seat, and at a `SetAccessory` resize of the placed subplate (which also keeps its footprint on the plate).
- **Raised centerline** (`app::rotary_stack`): the setup's subplates and every plate under each (through the plate locations) form a stack; the tallest one is used. The swing clause judges with the **effective** `nose_to_axis` = machine figure less the stack, or the setup's **stated** figure, which wins.
- **Refusal law:** a stack whose thickness is unknown (an imported plate under the subplate, a vanished or looped plate, a non-finite figure), a stated figure that is no length, or an effective figure at or under zero refuses the swing **by name** - never judged on the table figure. **No subplate: judged word for word as before** (pinned by the exact message).
- **Per-setup stated figure:** `SetupDef::nose_to_axis`, command `SetSetupNoseToAxis` (finite, > 0, <= 5000 mm; no-op refused; undoable), carried by a datum transfer with the machine.
- **Save/load:** additive setup key `nose_to_axis`; the subplate rides the existing `accessory` key. Old files load unchanged (pinned).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/821-rotary-on-plate-stack.md`.

## Commands, MCP, UI

- Commands: `InsertAccessory` / `SetAccessory` (new kind), `PlaceOnPlate` (pin law), new `SetSetupNoseToAxis`.
- MCP: `add_accessory` / `set_accessory` take `rotary_subplate`; `place_on_plate` applies the pin law; new `get_rotary_stack` (stack layers, stated figure, machine rotaries, refusal reason) and `set_setup_nose_to_axis` (number or null).
- UI: the Fixtures page's accessory dialog lists "Rotary subplate" (KINDS-driven); the setup's Machine page gets a "Rotary centerline" section (machine figure, the stack readout or the refusal, a checkbox + field for the setup's stated figure, queued as `CommandKind::SetupNoseToAxis`). Drawn only for a machine with a work-turning rotary. No snapshot PNG changed.

## Tests

- `crates/app/tests/rotary_subplate.rs` (new): `a_subplate_lands_fixed_and_seats_on_a_dowel_pair_by_its_pins`, `the_same_program_clears_on_the_table_and_is_refused_on_the_stack`, `a_stack_of_unknown_thickness_is_refused_by_name`, `an_effective_nose_at_or_under_zero_is_refused_by_name`, `the_setup_s_stated_nose_wins_and_is_an_undoable_command`, `no_stack_is_judged_word_for_word_as_before`, `the_subplate_and_the_stated_nose_survive_a_save_and_old_files_load_unchanged`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_rotary_stack.rs` (new): `a_subplate_is_pinned_on_a_plate_and_raises_the_rotary_over_mcp`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setup_rotary.rs` (new, AccessKit labels): `the_stated_nose_is_one_undoable_command`, `the_machine_page_shows_the_rotary_rows_and_states_the_figure`, `a_machine_without_a_work_turning_rotary_draws_no_rotary_rows`.
- `builtin_accessory` updated for the sixth kind (KINDS, bounds/volume of the slab, insert order).
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 642cd694 (app suites 365 s, index_swing_horizontal 10 fn, ui suites 44 s; 0 failed). By hand (not mapped by quick, #1021): index_swing 9/9, index_swing_horizontal 10/10, tormach_fourth_axis 12/12, rotary_fixtures 4/4, rotary_verify 9/9; ui lib `setup_rotary`, `accessory`, `fixture`, `structural` filters 51/51; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

- **The hardware check on the user's own microARC subplate** (#821 "Checked on the user's microARC subplate") - stays with the user; hence `Refs`, not `Fixes`.
- The camcraft-mcp skill's tool table is not updated (a process file; the new tools describe themselves in `tools/list`).

title: fix(app,motion): judge probe and plasma on a reduced-fidelity model; cone/engrave rides stay refused
body:
Stacked on #1064 (base it on main once #1064 merges; it carries #1064's commits until then).

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed, per kind

#904 left five kinds refused outright on any reduced-fidelity model. Same rule as #864/#904: a law gives the model's excess back out of its slack while a positive slack is left (`verify::excess_floor`); past that it reads untightened and the program gate refuses the op by name.

- **Probe - now judged.** Both halves of the protected-move law read `probe_op::stylus_slack(excess)` = `STYLUS_SLACK` less the excess: the ball distance law (`stylus_hits_excess`) and the stem/body solid law (`stylus_reach_hits_excess`). The old functions forward with 0, so existing callers don't change. `generate` passes `material.excess`. Nothing else judges a probe against the model.
- **Plasma - now judged.** The kerf law (part grown by `kerf/2 - tol`, which the lead planner reads too) and the cover law read `PlasmaParams::kerf_tol()` = `KERF_TOL` less the new `PlasmaParams::model_excess`. `plasma_op` fills that field from `material.excess`. The cut-order, crossing and tip-up laws read only the path.
- **`fidelity_law`**: `excess_aware` now accepts Probe and every Plasma kind. `floor_of` also lists each kind's own slack (`own_law_tol_of`). `GOUGE_TOL` stays the base, so plasma is still refused at 0.01 mm of excess, which is stricter than its 0.025 mm law needs.
- **Cone rides (2D chamfer, deburr) and engrave rides (trace, engrave) - still refused, with the reason recorded.** No law holds them to a tolerance against the model: the ride *is* the mesh edge by construction, so there's no tolerance to give back. Deburr also reads bends between coarse facets as creases. Judging them would need a new stated ride accuracy, which is open design, not a tightening. The reason is in `fidelity_law`'s header and the decision file.
- **Cross drill - still refused; #1053 stays open for it (hence `Refs`).** Its part law and `rapids_radial` would each take a one-line tightening. But the chain is also proved by zero-slack readings of the mesh: `cross_stock::standoff` / `rapids_clear`, `cross_entry`, and `drill_reach`'s reach and holder faces. Tightening those means growing each measured standoff by the excess, which moves the kernel's stations. As #904 set, a law isn't tightened for a kind that stays refused.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1053-fidelity-probe-plasma.md`.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/coarse_probe_plasma.rs`. Each law is pinned so that a reading between the plain and the tightened slack is convicted only on the coarse model (excess 0.007), and a real hit is convicted on both:
- `a_ball_between_the_slacks_is_a_gouge_only_on_the_coarse_model`: a touch 0.006 mm in; a real gouge at 0.05 mm.
- `a_stem_between_the_slacks_is_a_shank_hit_only_on_the_coarse_model`: an overhang lip 0.006 mm into the stem; a real hit at 0.05 mm.
- `the_probe_op_judges_with_its_models_excess`: the same lip through `GenerateOperation` on an import with no flag and one flagged 0.012 mm. This proves the wiring.
- `a_kerf_between_the_tolerances_is_refused_only_on_the_coarse_model`: the part grown 0.02 mm past the cut outline; the kerf law refuses by name. A real reach at 0.1 mm is refused on both.
- `the_stylus_slack_...` and `the_kerf_tolerance_gives_the_excess_back_and_reads_plain_past_the_bound`: past the bound the laws read their plain slack.
- `probe_and_plasma_are_judged_while_a_tolerance_is_left_and_refused_by_name_past_it`, plus `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model`, whose refused list loses Probe and PlasmaProfile: judged at 0.012 mm, refused by name at 0.030 mm.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws`) and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` on the final head: green on 2e4058e7 (motion lib 31 s, 52 app suites 156 s, golden_cl plasma 1 s; 0 failed); clippy -D warnings clean.

## Not exercised

- The plasma cover law's tightening has no marginal pin. Its reading compares the path with the contour, and no fixture puts an edge between 0.018 and 0.025 mm past `kerf` on demand.
- There's no document-level plasma fixture. The part region comes from the model's silhouette slice, which can't be grown by a chosen 0.02 mm, so the law is pinned through `plasma_profile`.
- A bore touch on a coarse model: the tightened slack convicts a tangent touch once the excess passes ~0.0025 mm, because the bore's facets stand inside it. That's a false gouge on the safe side, the #1057 shape, and is recorded in the decision file.

No goldens or snapshots moved (`golden_cl::plasma_plate_with_holes_matches_golden` passes with `model_excess: 0.0`).

Changelog: Probe and Plasma Profile operations can now post from a reduced-fidelity model (e.g. a metre-unit STEP file); their collision laws are tightened by the model's excess and refuse by name past it (#1053)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Refs #1053

title: fix(motion): microlift pieces take longer chords only where they leave no sliver
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 3e9b8ae1; upstream/main a6bd69d8, with #1032, merged in at 6ccef5e4). **Stacked on #1007** (`issue/983-rings-fallback-note`, merged into this branch at 1eff2424: it gives the rotary level reader the ladder's step on the same line of the r6.2 pin this PR rewrites). Until #1007 merges, its commits show in this diff; this PR's own change is commit 42ee5e38 (plus the decision note f23ebc3c).

## What changed

The microlift acceptance (`adaptive/lift.rs`, `lift_returns`) compared the lifted plan's worst reading with the spiral's and flipped on nanometres. It was not a rounding tie: readings are whole rim samples (half degrees), and the extra sample was real. A piece re-thinned to longer chords (0.01 mm sag) cuts inside the arc it replaces and leaves a sliver on the stock side; the next piece meets it as one or two samples the spiral never planned, and which planner cells the sliver covers turns on nanometres of ring geometry.

- `lift_coarse::cut` (new module, `coarsen` moved into it): a piece takes its longer chords only where they read within the bound **and** leave standing no cell its own chords clear (`Raster::stands_over`). Otherwise it is cut on its own chords, the spiral's.
- `lift::keeps`: the acceptance keeps its law, with **no tolerance**. A lifted plan that reads over the spiral (or over the bound, where the spiral read under it) is never kept. The stated tolerance is zero.
- No other planner file is touched (`grow.rs`, PR #953's, and `budget.rs` are as they were).

Why not the tolerance the issue asked for: a one-sample tolerance posts a plan that reads over the stated bound, and two samples are needed (48.5 was read). The decision file has the alternatives: `docs/decisions/982-microlift-acceptance.md`.

## Readings (release, Linux x86-64)

60 x 14 slot, D10, bound 47.5014 deg; lifted / spiral reading. "Opening" is `rings::open` eroding that much deeper than it dilates back, "width" the slot that much wider.

| twin | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unperturbed | 47.5 / 47.5 kept | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| opening 8, 32, 48 nm | 48.0 / 47.5 **dropped** | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| opening 180 nm | 48.5 / 47.5 **dropped** | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| width -125, -62, -8, +32, +510 nm | 48.0 / 47.5 **dropped** | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| width +8 nm | 48.5 / 47.5 **dropped** | 47.5 / 47.5 kept |
| the other 19 twins (opening 16 nm - 1 um, width -250 nm - +5 um) | kept | kept |

Before, 10 of 30 twins dropped the lifted plan. After, 0 of 30, each reading its worst where the spiral does (the first turn out of the entry bore).

Cost: the `adaptive_hsm` narrow slot posts 14 534 moves instead of 13 378 (+8.6 %; a third of its pieces keep longer chords instead of two thirds); cut and air lengths within 3 mm; load, breaks and verdict unchanged. Planning time unchanged.

## The one fixture verdict that changes

The issue's Done-means asks that no adaptive fixture's verdict change. One does, and has to: `rotary_adaptive`'s r6.2 neck levels (5.7, 5.2), pinned "refused for travel" since #55. That verdict was this same coin. On unchanged main, openings perturbed only:

| opening | radius 5.7 | radius 5.2 | old pin |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0, 8, 125 nm | rings | rings | green |
| 16, 62 nm | **HSM-planned** | rings | red |
| 250, 510 nm | rings | **HSM-planned** | red |

After the fix both levels read 47.5 / 47.5 and are HSM-planned on microlift returns at every perturbation tried (0, 16, 32, 250 nm). The pin is rewritten: `the_r62_neck_levels_are_hsm_planned_on_microlift_returns`. They were cut by Offset rings at 100 % D with 15-21 breaks of 45-135 deg; they now read 20.3 % D on the suite's 0.1 mm dexel, no planner overload. Two readings are pinned as read, not at the whole bar's laws, and appear on main too whenever the coin lands the other way: 20.3 % D at the first turn out of the entry bore (law 19.8 %), and three breaks of 5.1-5.5 deg on radius 5.2. Filed as #1050.

Every other verdict is unchanged: bore, rectangle, L-pocket, island, narrow slot, channel (`adaptive_hsm`), the band (`adaptive_band`), `pocket3d_hsm`, `level_links`, the other `rotary_adaptive` tests.

## Goldens

None moves. `tests/golden/` holds no HSM plan, and no digest pins a lifted plan. Posted programs of lifted plans do change (more pieces on their own chords).

## How tested

Pinning tests (all fail without the sliver check; the first two were run that way):
- `adaptive::tests::the_slot_and_its_32_nm_twin_decide_the_same_way` (default lane)
- `adaptive::lift_tests::a_piece_takes_longer_chords_only_where_they_leave_no_sliver` (default lane)
- `adaptive::lift_tests::the_lifted_plan_is_kept_only_at_or_under_the_spiral_reading` (default lane; the zero tolerance)
- `adaptive::tests::the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations` (heavy lane: 20 twins, 8 nm - 0.51 um)
- `rotary_adaptive::the_r62_neck_levels_are_hsm_planned_on_microlift_returns` (heavy lane, rewritten)

Gate, on the final head 6ccef5e4: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green, 0 failed, wall 4.7 min (every motion suite ran: the stack touches a shared test fixture). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

Release `--include-ignored` (heavy lanes): motion lib 198/198 (the 20-twin sweep included), `adaptive_hsm` 6/6, `adaptive_band` 2/2, `rotary_adaptive` 6/6, `pocket3d_hsm` 4/4, `level_links` 12/12, `adaptive_orbit_seam` 1/1 (on 6ccef5e4). App (release, `--include-ignored`, on 42ee5e38): `roughing2d` 7/7, `shoulder_adaptive` 3/3, `pocket_overhead` 2/2, `whole_model_pocket` 5/5, `stock_engine_agreement` 3/3.

## What was not exercised

- **Windows and macOS.** Everything above is Linux x86-64. The planner's output differs in the last bits between platforms (#1010), so which twins flipped before differs there (the first worker saw 32 nm flip on Apple silicon); the fix does not depend on which.
- **The app's STEP bore count pin** (`pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`, re-pinned per platform by #1032): on Linux it reads (16196, 15457, 1570) with and without this change, inside #1032's band for unmeasured platforms, so the exact Windows and macOS triples are not expected to move - but they were not measured. (Before #1032 it read (6490, 6454, 222) on Linux both ways.) A reviewer on Windows or macOS: the test prints its triple.
- The rotary suite under perturbation beyond the r6.2 pin: the r7 bar's and the window's deepest levels flip on the #850 planning budget (main and this branch alike; the r7 pin is red with the openings 250 nm deeper on both). Filed as #1051.
- #882's held speedup was not re-measured on top of this.
- Debug-profile runs of the heavy lanes; UI; batch tier.

Changelog: Adaptive: a microlifted piece is posted on longer chords only where they leave no sliver of stock, so the lifted plan no longer flips to the bare spiral (and the pocket to Offset rings) on nanometre changes of the geometry; the rotary r6.2 neck levels are HSM-planned on microlift returns instead of ring-cut.

Effort: max (no escalation)

Fixes #982

title: fix(import): refuse STEP records nested past 64 parentheses before parsing
body:
## What changed

A STEP record nested about 1000 parentheses deep overflowed the stack inside ruststep's recursive-descent parser and killed the process (#1075). Before ruststep runs, a new linear byte pre-scan, `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_depth.rs`, tracks parenthesis depth outside strings (`'...'`, with `''` as an escaped quote) and comments (`/* ... */`). Past `MAX_NESTING = 64` it refuses the file by name:

`corrupt STEP: record nests deeper than 64 levels of parentheses at entity #999999, line 178` (the 5000-deep test input)

- Single pass over the bytes, no copy, scans bytes rather than chars (non-UTF-8 is fine), and has no unwrap/expect/panic.
- Unbalanced or negative depth, and unterminated strings or comments, are left to the parser.
- Line numbers count `\n` only, so CRLF and LF files give the same line.

**Call sites (one line each, the first statement of the function):**
- `step::parse_with_chord`
- `step_csys::read_tool_csys`

**Entry points covered:**
- Every model import reaches `parse_with_chord` through `import::load_model[_graded]`: GUI `ImportModel`, including the worker thread and its inline fallback; `ImportFixture` and the fixture command (`commands/fixture.rs`); the tool-body mesh (`commands/tool_body.rs`, `tool_body_view.rs`); and MCP `import_model` and the script `import`, both through `script::api::v_import` → `ImportModel`.
- The tool body's coordinate-system read hands bytes to ruststep separately through `read_tool_csys`, and is guarded too.
- `UpdateModel` takes a mesh, not bytes, so it needs no guard.
- Project load does not re-import from files: no call to the importers outside the paths above.
- The kernel-side importer (`crates/kernel`, PR #941, not merged) caps nesting at 64 itself and is not touched.

**Overlap with PR #1006:** both PRs touch `step::parse_with_chord`. #1006 edits the hunk around the `ruststep::parser::parse` error return. This PR adds one line at the top of the function, two lines above that hunk, so they should merge without conflict.

## Review round 1 (review 5869429278): the scan now mirrors ruststep's tokenizer

**What was wrong:** the scan knew only strings and comments. ruststep also reads `<` ... `>` (REFERENCE resources and ANCHOR names) as text. So `<x/*y>` or `<x'y>` put the scan into a comment or string state that ruststep never entered, and every `(` after it went uncounted.

**What changed:**
- The scan gained a `Uri` state for `<...>`.
- It also gained a `Binary` state for `"..."`. ruststep cannot parse binary literals; inside one the scan still counts `(` and ignores `'`, `/*` and `<`.
- I read ruststep's whole tokenizer at the pinned rev 90fdc93 (`token.rs`, `combinator.rs`, `exchange/*.rs`). The construct-by-construct table is in the module doc and in `docs/decisions/1075-step-nesting-cap.md`.
- Where ruststep's rule is unclear, the scan counts the parenthesis.
- The decision file and the comment beside `[patch.crates-io]` in the root `Cargo.toml` now say the scan must be re-audited whenever the ruststep pin moves. They also say that the move to solidcore (#917) removes the dependency.

**New tests in `step_nesting.rs`:**
- `a_reference_resource_cannot_hide_a_deep_record`: both of the reviewer's reproductions, at depth 65.
- `no_lexical_construct_hides_a_deep_record`: 15 constructs, each with a stray `'`, `/*`, `<` or `"` inside, followed by a record one past the cap. The scan must refuse each one.
- `parentheses_inside_text_are_not_counted`: 200 `(` inside a string, a comment and a resource. The file still imports through the real parser.

**Safety of the tests:** every deep input is checked by the scan before the importer sees it, so no test can hand ruststep a record deeper than the cap.

**Mutation check:** I removed the `<` and `"` states and re-ran `step_nesting`. The three new tests failed and the rest passed.

## The cap: measured crash depths

ruststep at the pinned rev, a single record nested N deep, on Windows 11:

| build | 1 MiB stack | 2 MiB stack | 8 MiB stack |
|---|---|---|---|
| debug, last N that survives | 400 | 821 | 3341 |
| release, last N that survives | 530 | 1086 | 4418 |

**Fixtures:** every `testdata/models/*.step` reaches a maximum depth of 3. That covers all nine files: box, empty_list, Milling-test, Milling-test-inch, sample_ap214 (a real AP214 export), and the four tool_csys files.

**Why 64:**
- The smallest default stack an import runs on is the 1 MiB Windows main thread, used by the GUI's inline fallback.
- 64 is about 20x the deepest real record and about 6x below the debug crash on 1 MiB.
- It matches the solidcore importer's cap.

The reasoning and the options dropped (a big-stack thread cannot catch an overflow) are in `docs/decisions/1075-step-nesting-cap.md`.

## How tested

**Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/step_nesting.rs`** (new, default lane, 8 tests, 0.06 s total). The deep inputs are built in code from box.step; no fixture is committed. Every deep input goes through the scan before the importer sees it.
- `a_record_nested_5000_deep_is_refused_by_name_quickly`: the message names the cap, `entity #999999` and the line, in under 1 s.
- `crlf_and_lf_files_name_the_same_line`
- `a_record_at_the_cap_still_imports`: depth 64 imports the same box mesh; depth 65 is refused.
- `the_tool_body_csys_read_is_guarded_too`
- `a_reference_resource_cannot_hide_a_deep_record`: the review's `<x/*y>` and `<x'y>` reproductions, at depth 65.
- `no_lexical_construct_hides_a_deep_record`: 15 constructs, from the table, each followed by a record one past the cap.
- `parentheses_inside_text_are_not_counted`: a file with 200 `(` inside a string, a comment and a resource still imports through ruststep.
- `every_step_fixture_is_under_the_cap`

**Lib tests in `step_depth::tests`** (7): strings, comments, `<...>` and binary literals; `''` escapes; refusal at the cap; CRLF; unbalanced input; non-UTF-8 input.

**Gates, on head 45472061:**
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green, 30.6 min. The comment added to the root `Cargo.toml` widened the quick gate to every crate: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, ui and clippy, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test step_nesting --test import --test tool_csys`: 8/8, 23/23 and 11/11 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib step`: 18/18 pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The GUI was not run.
- The crash depths were measured once with a throwaway probe test (not committed), on Windows only. Linux and macOS main threads are 8 MiB, so the cap leaves even more room there.
- STL and OBJ are not recursive parsers and need no such guard. There is no DXF importer in the tree yet.

Changelog: A STEP file with a record nested more than 64 parentheses deep is refused by name (entity and line) instead of crashing the app with a stack overflow.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1075

title: feat(pick): box-select edge chains and faces into an operation's picks
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main a6bd69d8).

## What changed

- **Viewport box select** (`crates/ui/src/box_pick.rs`, `egui_app/shell.rs`): Ctrl (or Shift) + left drag in Edge or Face mode, with an operation open and no other pick draft collecting, draws a rubber band instead of orbiting. On release it adds every visible feature edge chain (Edge mode) or welded face (Face mode) in the box to the operation's picks, as **one `SetOperationGeometry`**, so it is one undo step. A drag to the right is a **window** (takes only what lies wholly inside), a drag to the left is a **crossing** box (also takes what it touches). The band is solid for a window and dashed for a crossing box. A plain left drag still orbits.
- **The rule** (`crates/app/src/pick/box_pick.rs`: `box_bodies`, `box_select`, `box_select_top`) follows #692's one pick rule. Only feature chains are candidates (never facet seams). A candidate counts only if part of it is unoccluded from the eye, using the click pick's own sight test (`feature_pick::occluded`, now `pub(super)`, with no behaviour change), at most 16 sight rays per candidate. Pick-through stays off. Only parts are candidates, never stock or fixtures, but stock and fixtures still hide what lies behind them.
- **MCP**: new tool `pick_in_box` (`crates/app/src/mcp/box_pick.rs`). It takes a world X/Y box seen from straight above (the Top view, orthographic), with `mode` window/crossing and `kind` chains/faces. By default it adds to the current picks; `replace: true` replaces them. One undo step. An empty, degenerate or already-picked box is refused with a message that names the reason. `mcp::pick::kind_door` is now `pub(super)` so the new tool can reuse it.
- The Selection row's hover text documents the gesture. Decisions are in `docs/decisions/979-box-select-picks.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/box_pick.rs` uses a 100 x 60 x 10 plate with two square through-cutouts:

title: fix(verify): judge a stock-sourced Bore's entry rapid against the stock
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main a6bd69d8).

## What reproduced

In #1066 the planar ladder takes its first descent from the top of the cut plus the plunge height (2 mm): Pocket and Contour read their Top height, Bore reads the hole's `entry_z`. The issue suspected a rapid into stock that stands higher than that top. Fixture: a 40 x 40 x 20 part with a 20 x 20 blind hole (mouth Z 20) in a box 5 mm taller (top Z 25), nothing faced ahead. Each op's entry rapid goes from Z 40 to Z 22, 3 mm into uncut stock.

- 2D Pocket, Contour, and a Bore sourced from the part: already convicted by the rapid law (#96, `RapidInStock`), and the post is blocked.
- **A Bore sourced from the stock: no warning, and it posted.** That's a silent rapid into material, so the issue went to P0.

Cause: `sim::verify::rapids_in_stock` asks `Rest::in_stock`, which falls back to the op's region when `VerifyContext::stock` is `None`, and a stock-sourced op leaves it `None`. For Bore and Thread that region is the stock footprint with the holes' rims punched out, so the column inside the hole never counted as stock.

## What changed

- `operation::material_source::judged_stock` (new, about 20 lines): when the source is the stock and the kind is Bore or Thread, verify's column law reads the stock's own facets instead of the punched region. Every other source and kind reads exactly as before.
- `operation::generate`: the upright and 3+2 verify readings both take that stock. No generator or path changes, so no golden moves.
- `docs/decisions/1066-ladder-entry-height.md`: why the law's reading was fixed rather than raising the ladder's top, and the options dropped.

## How tested

- New suite `crates/app/tests/ladder_entry_height.rs`. Each of its 4 tests runs Pocket, Bore and Contour:
  - `a_ladder_entry_rapid_under_a_taller_block_is_named_and_blocks_the_post`: `RapidInStock` at the entry rapid, and the post gate refuses it. It fails on main for Bore and passes with the fix; I checked both.
  - `a_block_standing_inside_the_plunge_height_is_fed_through_silently` (1.5 mm over the mouth)
  - `stock_to_the_mouth_is_silent_and_posts`
  - `a_face_ahead_to_the_mouth_acquits_the_entry_rapid` (`acquit_by_prior` still clears it)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (1 step, 43 app binaries + lib, 148 s)
- I also ran the suites that build Bore or Thread ops: arc_entry, circular_pick, mill2d_b, mill2d_c, operations, refusal_location, level_links, vertical_arc_entry, project_roundtrip, golden_cl and conformance. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

## Not exercised

- The Thread case is covered by the same `matches!` arm but has no pinning test of its own (its entry is judged by #992's thread-entry law).
- The 3+2 (tilted) reading takes the same stock, but no tilted test was run for it.
- Drill isn't touched: its R-plane law already refuses this case at generate (checked on the same fixture).

Changelog: A milled Bore sourced from the stock now has its entry rapid judged against the stock above the hole's mouth: a rapid into uncut stock is named and blocks the post (#1066)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1066

title: feat(tools): a tool carries cutting data per workpiece material
body:
Stacked on #1070 (on #1060). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- `Tool` gains `cutting: Vec<CuttingRow>` (new `camcraft_tools::cutting_rows`). Each row is `{material, rpm, feed}`, keyed by the built-in `WorkMaterial` groups the document's material already uses. The tool's own `rpm`/`feed` stay the running numbers the post reads, and the fallback.
- Seeding happens only through commands, one undo step each:
  - `SetWorkMaterial` re-seeds every tool that has a row for the new material (`ChangeTool`), plus the milling feed of each op on such a tool (`EditOperationParams`). The status line says how many moved.
  - `AddTool` starts on the document material's row.
  - A `ChangeTool` that edits only the table loads the row. An Apply that also states rpm/feed keeps its own numbers.
  - `EditOperationLinks` (tool retarget) takes the new tool's row feed.
  - Quick-add, MCP `add_operation` and the recognizer seed a new op's feed. An explicit MCP params patch still wins.
- **Nothing moves on load.** With no matching row, everything stays as it is today.
- File: an additive `cutting_data` key on `ToolDto`, written only when the tool has rows. A tool without rows saves byte-identical, so there is no version step. An unknown material word refuses the file by name.
- Validation by tool name at `AddTool`/`ChangeTool` (and `is_sane` at read): rpm and feed must be finite and above zero (a torch row states rpm 0), and no material may appear twice.
- Tool editor: a new collapsed "Cutting data by material" header (`tool_cutting_rows.rs`) with per-row material, rpm, feed, Remove, and "Add material row". The Body column is untouched (#1043).
- MCP: `add_tool`'s `definition` takes `cutting_data`, and `get_job` shows it. Stating the material over MCP is still #732; editing a tool is #1062.
- Decisions are in `docs/decisions/890-cutting-data-per-material.md`, including the #1060 interaction: Update/Replace still match by name and import rows and running numbers as the library states them, with no re-seed.

## How tested
Pinning tests, all in `crates/app/tests/tool_cutting_rows.rs`:
- `a_tool_without_rows_writes_no_key_and_a_table_round_trips`
- `a_project_without_rows_saves_byte_identical_and_a_table_survives_save_load`
- `loading_never_moves_the_numbers_an_existing_project_runs`
- `an_unknown_material_word_refuses_the_file_by_name`
- `the_table_round_trips_the_tool_library`
- `unusable_rows_are_refused_by_tool_name_at_creation`
- `stating_the_material_seeds_tool_and_ops_in_one_undo_step`
- `an_op_on_material_x_posts_x_rows_spindle_speed` (posts S3100/F410 for the steel row)
- `adding_a_tool_and_editing_its_table_seed_the_running_numbers`
- `quick_add_and_retarget_seed_the_op_feed_from_the_row`
- `mcp_add_tool_takes_the_table_and_refuses_a_bad_row`

Also unit tests `cutting_rows::tests` (tools) and `tool_cutting_rows::tests::rows_add_per_material_and_ride_the_draft_both_ways` (ui).

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/898-tool-catalog-fields` green on the final head 78a23c8b (tools, motion, app, ui suites - 4 steps, 0 failed, 3.3 min); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

No golden moved: no fixture tool has rows, and the posted numbers still come from `Tool::rpm` and the op feed.

## Not exercised
- The editor widget was not clicked by hand; only the draft round-trip is unit-tested. No structural/snapshot assertion was added, because the header is collapsed by default for a tool without rows.
- With a dirty op-page draft, a retarget's seeded feed can be overwritten by a later Apply of that draft. That is the draft's normal last-write-wins behaviour.
- MCP `add_operation` seeding is not driven end to end, because MCP cannot state the material yet (#732). The seed fn it calls is pinned directly.

Changelog: A tool can carry cutting data (rpm, feed) per workpiece material; stating the material, adding the tool or editing its table loads the matching row into the tool and its operations' feed, one undo step; old files load and save unchanged (#890)

Fixes #890

title: feat(import): the STEP facet budget is a setting carried with the import
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main a6bd69d8).

## What changed

The STEP importer's facet budget (the constant `MAX_FACETS`) becomes a setting that travels with the import (`app::geometry::import::step_budget`):

- **Default and bounds.** The default is today's cap, 30,000,000 facets, so no default import changes and no golden moves. A set budget must be in 1,000..=60,000,000. Outside that range, every door refuses it by name before parsing (`STEP facet budget N is outside 1000..=60000000 facets`). A budget given for an STL or OBJ file is also refused.
- **Doors.**
  - `ImportModel::within(path, budget)` is the one command the GUI, the script and MCP all build.
  - The script verb is `cam.import(path, name?, facetBudget?)`. A null name keeps the file stem. `cam.d.ts` is regenerated to match.
  - MCP `import_model` takes an optional integer `facet_budget`, declared in the schema with its min/max.
  - Script and MCP take whole numbers only. A fraction, a negative or a string is refused, never rounded.
- **Recorded with the model.**
  - A new component, `schema::StepBudget`, holds the budget, but only when it is not the default. `model_fidelity::budget_of` / `set_budget` read and write it.
  - Import, update (re-import), repair (keeps it), delete and their undo all trade it together with the facets.
  - The project file stores it as an optional `facet_budget` key. An absent key means the default, so default documents save byte for byte as before and older files load unchanged. An out-of-bounds value, or one on a non-model row, is refused by name at load.
  - `get_job` and `cam.import` report the budget.
- **Reduced fidelity (#864) is computed exactly as before.** A smaller budget flags the model; a larger one meshes finer and clears the flag on re-import. The refusal text now names a setting that exists: "re-import with a larger STEP facet budget".
- **GUI.** The model page has a "STEP facet budget (next import)" row (type a value, then Enter or Set). An out-of-range value is refused by name on the row and on the status line, and the last good value stays. The row also shows which budget the model was imported under. Every STEP import started from the window (Model button, recent list, drag and drop) reads the setting. A re-import under the same name stays the undoable `UpdateModel`.
- **`step.rs` edits are minimal.** `parse_with_chord_budget` was added, and the thread-local test override now only lowers the requested budget. This should merge additively with #969's log-line change.

Decisions (60M ceiling, a session-scoped GUI setting on the model page rather than a post-picker modal, re-import uses the current setting, no project version bump) are in `docs/decisions/1054-step-facet-budget.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/step_budget.rs` (new, 6 tests):
  - `the_default_budget_imports_exactly_as_before`
  - `a_lowered_budget_flags_and_a_raised_one_clears_through_undo_and_delete`
  - `an_out_of_bounds_budget_is_refused_by_name_before_parsing`
  - `the_script_verb_takes_the_budget_and_refuses_one_out_of_bounds`
  - `mcp_import_model_takes_the_budget_and_get_job_reports_it`
  - `the_budget_round_trips_through_the_project_and_an_older_file_reads_the_default`
- `step_budget::tests` unit tests: bounds, JSON whole numbers only, the default records nothing.
- `crates/ui` `egui_app::tests::step_budget::the_model_page_sets_the_budget_the_next_step_import_runs_under`: the row is drawn, an out-of-range value is refused on the row and the status line, a lowered budget's import lands flagged, a raised re-import clears the flag, and undo restores both.
- `crates/app/tests/model_fidelity.rs`: the two refusal-text pins now expect the new wording.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green on c93c64ef (app suites ok 167 s, ui suites ok 21 s, 3.1 min wall, 0 failed)

## Not exercised

- A real model that needs more than the 30M default to reach full fidelity. No such fixture is committed. "Raised clears" is pinned from 2,000 up to 5,000,000 on `Milling-test.step`.
- The native file picker and typing into the egui field by keyboard. The test drives the setter and the import queue.
- The camcraft-mcp skill doc does not mention `facet_budget` yet. It is a process file, which would need a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump; the tool's schema and description carry the argument.

Changelog: The STEP facet budget is a setting: the model page, `cam.import(path, name?, facetBudget?)` and MCP `import_model`'s `facet_budget` set it (1000..=60000000, default 30000000), and each model records the budget it was imported under (#1054)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1054

title: fix(sim,app): read a containment kind's declared rim at the plain gouge tolerance on a reduced-fidelity model
body:
Stacked on #1064 (branch `issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws`: this uses its `verify/excess.rs` split and its `coarse_contain` fixture). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## Root cause

A Z drill, bore or thread mill verifies (`Mode::Boundary`) against rim loops that are our own polygons of each hole's declared circle (`material_source::rim_loop`), built to `RIM_SAG_BUDGET` = 0.005 mm, half the 0.01 mm `GOUGE_TOL`. A 2 mm rim (48 sides) stands 0.00428 mm inside its circle, so a matched drill reads `r - 0.00428` off it. #864 had law (b) read **every** loop at `GOUGE_TOL - excess`. Past 0.01 - 0.00428 = 0.00572 mm of excess (a model flagged above ~0.0107 mm; the issue saw 0.0105 clean, 0.011 convicted) the tolerance left no longer covered the rim's own sagitta: `Gouge { at: 1 }` on a matched drill, and on every ring of a matched bore. Past 0.015 mm `excess_floor` reads untightened and the gate refuses by name, which is why 0.03 read clean.

## What changed

- `sim::verify::VerifyContext` gets `rims: &[(Point2, f64)]` (empty by default): the declared circles of a containment kind. `VerifyContext::is_rim` / `loop_tol` (in `verify/excess.rs`) match a loop to one (every vertex within 2 um: the region's 1 um lattice snap).
- Law (b) (`verify/section.rs`), both the law-point reading and the Boundary whole-move wall reading, reads a rim loop at the plain `gouge_tol` and every other loop at `tightened(gouge_tol)` as before. Rims are found once per verify call.
- `app::operation::generate` fills `rims` from the Drill (Z holes), Bore and Thread params when the depth law is `Contain` (`material_source::rims_of`), at both verify sites.
- The solid law against the model's facets (`contain_into`) is untouched and still tightened.

Why the plain tolerance is honest: the excess measures how far a coarse model's facets stand inside its true surface; a rim is not a facet but a circle we draw from the hole's own centre and radius, so the rim's reading is exactly today's full-fidelity verdict. Nothing a full-fidelity model convicts is acquitted. Decision file: `docs/decisions/1057-drill-excess-false-gouge.md` (options dropped: finer rims, exact-circle reading, zeroing the excess for the containment kinds, recognising rims structurally in sim).

## Readings (`coarse_rims` fixture: 40x40x20 block, 20x20 cavity blind at Z 10, DR-0400 to Z 10.2)

| flagged | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| full, 0.008, 0.0105 | clean | clean |
| 0.011, 0.012, 0.0149 | `Gouge { at: 1 }` | clean |
| 0.03 | clean + refused by name | clean + refused by name |

Matched bore (EM-0800-4FL in a 6 mm-radius hole) at 0.011 / 0.0149: before `Gouge { at: 6, 7, 8, 17, ... }`, after clean.

## How tested

Pinning tests (all fail before the fix where they name a false conviction, pass after):
- `coarse_rims::a_matched_drill_is_clean_on_a_model_flagged_anywhere_below_the_refusal_bound` (full, 0.008, 0.0105, 0.011, 0.012, 0.0149)
- `coarse_rims::a_matched_bore_is_clean_near_the_refusal_bound` (+ a bore offset 1 mm into the wall still convicts at 0.0149)
- `coarse_rims::the_real_drill_gouges_still_convict_on_a_model_near_the_refusal_bound` (oversize drill, drill offset into the wall, drill 0.5 mm past the floor - each at full, 0.011 and 0.0149; and 0.005 mm past the floor: clean at full fidelity, a gouge at 0.0149)
- `coarse_rims::a_matched_drill_past_the_bound_is_refused_by_name_not_convicted` (0.03: no warnings, the gate's fidelity line by name)
- `coarse_rims::a_thread_mill_reads_the_same_near_the_bound_as_at_full_fidelity`
- `model_excess::a_declared_rim_is_read_untightened_and_no_other_loop_is` (sim: an undeclared rim convicted near the bound, declared clean, a 2.01 drill still convicted, a declaration that does not trace the loop leaves the coarse boss convicted)

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws` on the final head fe7403bc - sim 9 s, motion 4 s, app 201 s, 0 failed (3.6 min); plus `verify` and `mill2d_c` (rim law and bore/thread from stock) green; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. No goldens or snapshot PNGs moved.

## Not exercised

- The thread mill is **not** clean: on a model-sourced hole it is convicted on every helix move at full fidelity too (its helix runs the thread depth past the declared rim by design). Not a fidelity bug; filed as #1071. The pin here is only that the excess no longer changes its verdict.
- The 3+2 framed verify site passes the same rims; a rim drawn in the local frame that does not match the world-frame circles simply falls back to the tightened reading (today's behaviour). Not exercised by a framed fixture.

Changelog: A drill or bore matched to its hole is no longer falsely convicted of a gouge on a model imported between ~0.0105 mm and the 0.015 mm refusal bound (#1057, PR #1073)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1057
