title: feat(post): judge the index swing of any work-turning rotary about a level line
body:
## What changed

The index-swing clause of the program gate (#804, #813) judged only an A that turns the work about X. A table **B** (stated `[0,1,0]`, or unstated and named B) and an **A stated level but off X** read as "off X", so they got no swing check, no refusal and no load note. A `G0 B..` index could swing the work into the retracted tool without anything judging it. This PR generalises the clause to any work-turning rotary about a **horizontal** line through the WCS origin.

- `crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs`
  - `rotary_line` now returns the line itself:
    - `Horizontal(u)`: a stated level vector, normalised, or an unstated `A` (X) or `B` (Y). Judged.
    - `Vertical`: a stated vector along ±Z, or an unstated `C`. It keeps every height, so it stays safe and unjudged, as before.
    - `Leaning`: a stated vector that is neither level nor vertical, or a zero or non-finite one. **Refused by name** ("about a line that is neither level nor vertical ... its index swing is not judged"). It is never judged as if it were level.
    - `Unknown`: no vector and no RS-274 letter. Refused, as in #813, and this refusal still wins over the others.
  - "Level" is now strict: the off component must be within 1e-6 of the vector's length. That is 1 µm of height over 1 m of travel. The old X test allowed about 5.7° of lean.
  - The swept radius is the farthest turning vertex from the rotary's own line, `|(p - o) × u|`. For u = X this is the old `hypot(y, z)`.
  - An unstated `nose_to_axis` refuses by name, exactly as for A. A non-finite one refuses by name too. `LoadMachine` already refuses a non-finite number at creation, so this is defence in depth.
  - A non-finite facet vertex now counts as an unbounded sweep, so the post is refused. Before, that vertex was skipped.
  - **Two rotaries turning the work** (a table B carrying a C, a trunnion): each turn moves the other's line, so the sweep is taken from the WCS origin itself, and the message says so. No shipped machine has this setup.
  - The index angle in the messages is read about the rotary's line, `atan2(t·(u×Z), t·Z)`. That is the post's `atan2(-y, z)` for X and `atan2(x, z)` for Y.
- `crates/app/src/project/swing_note.rs`: the pre-#804 load note now names every rotary with an unstated `turns_part` unless its line is vertical. A saved table B is now named on load.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/818-swing-any-horizontal.md`. It covers why a leaning line refuses instead of getting a "conservative" judgement, the 1e-6 level tolerance, and the stacked-rotary sweep from the origin.
- Shipped machines are unchanged. The only machine that turns the work on a level line is the microARC (A, `[1,0,0]`), and it is judged exactly as before.

## The math

A vertical tool's tip at height h above a horizontal line through the origin is at distance `sqrt(h² + d²) ≥ h` from it, where d is its level offset from the line. So the tip is the tool's nearest point to the line wherever the G30 puts it along X and Y. The #804 law, `tip = nose_to_axis - tool length ≥ swept + MARGIN_MM`, therefore holds unchanged for any level unit vector u; only the swept radius `max |(p - o) × u|` depends on u.

A leaning line rises along its travel, so its distance to the tip depends on the unknown G30 position. No bound short of the whole envelope holds, which is why it is refused. Turns about lines through the origin keep each point's distance from the origin, so that distance is the conservative sweep when two rotaries turn the work.

## Tests

New suite `crates/app/tests/index_swing_horizontal.rs` (10 tests). It uses a test-only table-B machine file, inline as `TABLE_B`: a 770MX-sized mill with a work-turning B `[0,1,0]` and `nose_to_axis` 10.6 in.

- `a_table_b_too_long_to_clear_the_bar_is_refused_by_name`: B90 index. The bar's far end sweeps `hypot(STICK, R)` about Y. The test checks the refusal line, the 3.000 mm clearance and that the post writes nothing.
- `a_table_b_with_a_short_tool_clears`: no false refusal.
- `a_table_b_with_no_nose_height_is_refused_by_name`
- `a_table_b_with_no_axis_vector_is_judged_about_y`: an unstated B is judged about Y.
- `an_a_stated_level_but_off_x_is_judged_about_its_own_line`: A `[3,4,0]`, swept about `[0.6,0.8,0]`. It refuses and clears at the same lengths as the A case.
- `a_leaning_or_zero_work_turning_line_is_refused_not_judged`: `[1,0,1]` and `[0,0,0]` are refused by name, and the post writes nothing.
- `a_non_finite_vector_or_nose_height_never_reads_as_judged`: `LoadMachine` refuses NaN and inf. `rotary_line` reads NaN or inf as `Leaning`, `[0,2,0]` as unit Y, `[0,1,0.01]` as `Leaning` and `[0,0,-3]` as `Vertical`.
- `a_work_turning_c_alone_stays_unjudged`: stated and unstated C, a too-long tool and no nose height. Nothing is raised.
- `two_rotaries_turning_the_work_sweep_from_the_wcs_origin`: B with C. The sweep is the bar corner's distance from the origin.
- `a_project_saved_before_804_names_its_unjudged_table_b_on_load`

The existing `index_swing` suite (9) passes unchanged.

## Revert check

I restored `posting_index_swing.rs` and `swing_note.rs` to `upstream/main`, ran the new suite, then restored the fix.

- **Fail on revert:** the B refusal, the no-nose refusal, the unstated-B judgement, the off-X A, the leaning/zero refusal, the stacked sweep and the load note (7 tests).
- **Does not compile on revert:** `a_non_finite_vector_or_nose_height_never_reads_as_judged`. It uses the new `RotaryLine` variants, so for this check I set it aside temporarily.
- **Pass on revert, as intended:** `a_table_b_with_a_short_tool_clears` and `a_work_turning_c_alone_stays_unjudged`. They guard against false refusals and are not pins of the fix.
- **Separate stacked check:** I forced `stacked: false` and the fixed code passed everything except `two_rotaries_turning_the_work_sweep_from_the_wcs_origin`, so the origin sweep is pinned on its own.

## Gate

All results are on Linux, on head `0722074d`.

- **`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`:** green. The app suites step ran 62 suites mapped to `app::project` plus the lib, in 211 s, followed by the 10 new tests. 0 failed.
- **Pinning tests:** run through `cargo xtask gate test` (`--crate app --binary index_swing_horizontal`). Green.
- **Existing swing and rotary suites:**

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| index_swing | 9 passed |
| tormach_fourth_axis | 12 passed |
| microarc_test_part | 2 passed |
| rotary_letter | 3 passed |
| rotary_verify | 9 passed |
| conformance | 6 passed |
| posting | 17 passed |
| machine | 33 passed |

- **`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`:** clean.

## Not exercised

- I never posted a table-B program that clears: the PathPilot post is the only post in the fixture, and the test checks only the gate, not B output.
- No shipped machine turns the work on B or on two rotaries, so none was exercised; the stacked case runs only on the test machine.
- The headless-load note gap (review note 2 on #815) is pre-existing and unchanged.

Changelog: The index-swing check now judges any rotary that turns the work about a level line (a table B, an A stated off X), not only an A about X. It refuses by name a leaning or garbled rotary line, and with two work-turning rotaries it takes the sweep from the WCS origin (#818)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at v0.17.0.

Fixes #818

title: fix(post): canned-cycle posts traverse between holes at the stream's hop, not at R
body:
**Stacked on #1002** (issue #926, `issue/926-post-script-suites`). Until #1002 merges, this diff also shows its commit (`b471395e`). This PR adds one commit on top. Retarget/merge order per AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack": #1002 first.

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (PROCESS_VERSION 16). Effort: high (P0, under the safety floor: posted G-code).

## What was wrong

The six posts that write canned cycles swallowed every rapid after a cycle until the section ended. They also wrote `G98` once, read while the tool already stood on R (the stream's rapid down to R is posted before the cycle), so the "initial level" was R. Result: the traverse between holes and the exit from the last hole ran at the R plane, lower than the hop/clearance the path was simulated and verified at.

## What changed (per dialect)

All six now follow the same law (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, "The hop law"):

- **The chain a cycle replaces is only what stays on its hole**: its XY, at or below R. The **first rapid that leaves the hole** (the hop up, the traverse, the exit) ends the group with `G80` and posts as the stream says. So the posted traverse is the stream's own rapids, at the stream's hop/clearance.
- **Each hole returns to R.**
  - `fanuc`, `haas`, `mazak`, `doosan-dnm`, `tormach` (PathPilot/LinuxCNC): a `G99` block when each cycle group opens (RS-274 / ISO 6983: G99 = return to R, G98 = return to the level the tool stood at). The once-per-program `G98` is gone.
  - `sinumerik`: still no G98/G99 word (none invented, return mode not assumed). The tool is seated on R before the cycle is read, so either return mode lands on R.
- **Seat (`cycleSeat`)**: a cycle read away from its hole position (a stream whose cycle is anchored on the rapid down to R) is seated first. It goes up to R when below it, then over the hole, then down, so it never runs under the stream's straight rapid. A cycle that is its section's first motion is not seated: there is no stream position yet.
- **A cut (linear/arc) that leaves the hole inside a cycle group is refused by name** ("a cutting move leaves its hole inside a canned-cycle group"). Before, it was silently swallowed. Heidenhain already refused this.
- Heidenhain and Carvera are unchanged. They already post the safe links explicitly.

## Before / after (`drill_retract`: R 1, hop 3, clearance 10; fanuc)

Before (from the issue):
```
G00 X10 Y10 Z1
G98
G73 X10 Y10 Z-20 R1 Q4 F60
G80
G73 X30 Y10 Z-15 R1 Q4 F60   <- X10 -> X30 at Z1
G80
M5                            <- leaves at Z1
```
After (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/fanuc/drill_retract.nc`):
```
G00 X10 Y10 Z1
G99
G73 X10 Y10 Z-20 R1 Q4 F60
G80
G00 X10 Y10 Z3
G00 X30 Y10 Z3
G00 X30 Y10 Z1
G99
G73 X30 Y10 Z-15 R1 Q4 F60
G80
G00 X30 Y10 Z3
G00 X30 Y10 Z10
M5
```
App golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/drill_plate.nc` (R 0 = stock top, hop 5): it used to rapid X10 to X30 at Z0. It now posts `G00 X10 Y10 Z5 / G00 X30 Y10 Z5 / G00 X30 Y10 Z0` between the holes and `G00 X30 Y10 Z5` after the last.

## Goldens (all read)

New, #1002's `drill_retract` (removed from `KNOWN_BUGS`, which keeps the two non-#994 entries): `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/{fanuc,haas,mazak,sinumerik,tormach,doosan-dnm}/drill_retract.nc`

Moved, app NC goldens (`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/`):
- `drill_plate.nc`, `drill_peck.nc`, `tap_plate.nc` (the fanuc legacy matrix)
- `{haas,mazak,sinumerik,tormach,doosan-dnm}/{drill_plate,drill_peck,tap_plate}.nc`
- `synth_{fanuc,haas,mazak,sinumerik,tormach,doosan-dnm}.nc`: the synthesized conformance stream anchors each cycle on its rapid to R, so the seat now posts the stream's own positioning. After the contour it first climbs to R, then goes over the hole. The stream itself traverses at R between these holes, and the posts now post exactly that.
- `inverted/{fanuc_x,haas_x}.nc`: the inverted-axis fixture now anchors its hole on the first cut, as the generator does, so the rapid to R posts as motion before `G99`.

`drill_peck` / `tap_plate` single-hole programs gain the exit rapid (`G00 ... Z6` / `Z5`), so they no longer leave the hole at R.

## Tests

- **New `crates/post/tests/cycle_hop.rs`**: one generic read-back checker, run on all six cycle posts. It parses the posted program as a control runs it: XY positioning at the current level, G98/G99 return, the lower level when no mode is stated, and a dogleg rapid's lower Z. It asserts that every XY traverse after the first hole is at Z >= the stream's `RetractPlane` and that the tool leaves the cut at Z >= `ClearancePlane`.
  - `every_cycle_post_traverses_between_holes_at_the_hop`: the recorded `drill_retract` stream.
  - `a_cycle_anchored_on_the_rapid_to_r_is_seated_first`: the same stream with the cycles anchored one move earlier (the seat path).
  - `the_checker_catches_the_r_plane_traverse`: the checker flags the issue's program (two faults) and an unstated-mode R traverse, and passes the fixed shape.
  - On the pre-fix posts, both stream tests fail (checked by hand by stashing the `.cps` changes).
- `script_*::drill_retract` for the six posts (goldens above).

title: feat(app): refusal ghost for part-way refusals; ghost-aware match sites; ground-aware ghost colour
body:
Follow-up to #261 and PR #861. Generators that refuse part-way now hand back their partial path as the display-only ghost. Both match sites now handle the `Ghosted` variant, and the ghost's colour uses #698's ground-aware dimming.

## What changed

**Part-way refusals carry their moves.** There is a new `GenError::with_ghost_moves(&[Move])`, which is `with_ghost` over a builder's moves. Every adoption is one `map_err` / `.with_ghost..` on an **error path**. No generator finishes early or changes its control flow. The ghosts are in the generator's own frame, which `run_job` already maps to world through `world_path` (a 3+2 tilt) or which is world already.

| Generator | Refusal | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2D Contour (`contour_impl`) | control comp with no lead-in/out; `push_span` | ghost added: rings so far |
| Bore | per-hole pass budget (`cut_levels`) | ghost added: holes bored so far |
| Circular | per-ring pass budget | ghost added: rings so far |
| Trochoidal slot | level emit (helix-turn cap); loops cross themselves | ghost added: levels so far / the finished path |
| 3-D ladder (Pocket3D, Multi-Axis Rough) | `hsm::plan_level` adaptive level refusal | ghost added (Rotary Offset still drops it, `without_ghost`) |
| Plasma profile | no cut, G41 span off its cut, cover and kerf laws, torch spans | ghost added: contours so far / the whole cut |
| Probing | touch not toward its target | ghost added: the built cycle |
| Turning form | crown on or through the axis | ghost added: valleys so far |
| Turning groove (blade) | rung budget per station | ghost added: stations so far |
| Before any move (parameter, region and tool doors; bore and thread-mill hole checks) | | listed: nothing built |
| "Path left the finite horizon" tails (all generators) | | listed: `Ghost::of` drops non-finite moves by law |
| Drilling cycles (axial, radial) | per-hole doors | listed: each already names the hole's mouth (#261 part 2); the earlier holes are plunges elsewhere |
| Rotary Offset inner ladder | | listed: wrap space, on purpose |
| Trochoidal slot lifted-return trial | | listed: the `trial` is a scratch level, not the path |
| Boundary turn mid-rotation | | listed: half-rotated moves, no frame |
| finishing3d raster/rings/swarf, rotary links/posing, Face under an area turn, cross drill app-side laws, nested (already-ghosted) refusals, multiaxis stamp/swarf/curve, rotary gate, fixture route | | listed as owed: each needs a frame map or a ghost merge first; follow-up issue #1015 |

The full reasoning is in `docs/decisions/871-refusal-ghost-rest.md`.

**Match sites.**
- `cross_spindle::in_world`: a `Ghosted` refusal has its sentence rewritten and its spot moved by the hole shift, and its moves are carried by the same translation. With no shift to read, or a ghost holding an arc, the ghost and spot are dropped. Nothing is ever drawn in the spindle frame.
- `picks::door_refusal`: reads a `Ghosted` refusal's words like the plain `Invalid` one. The pick shows words only.
- Also found: `body_judged::name_enclosure` rewrote only `Invalid`/`At`, so a ghost-carrying holder refusal would have lost its "(enclosure)" words. It now goes through `GenError::map_msg`.

**Colour.** The ghost uses #698's ground-aware dimming (`ground_ink::dimmed`, and `ground_ink::faded`, its light half now public for a caller's own share):
- Dark ground: unchanged, byte for byte.
- Light ground: the ghost fades toward the ground and never toward black. Cutting moves keep 0.9 of the gouge colour and clear WCAG 3:1 on the light viewport in every colour-vision palette (3.12:1 for the house palette; `dimmed`'s 0.6 would read 2.26:1). Rapids take `dimmed`'s 0.6, fainter still.

No snapshot PNG changed.

## Tests (pinning)
- `refusal_ghost::tests::the_ghost_reads_on_the_light_ground_and_keeps_its_dark_tones` (ui lib): the light-ground contrast test. The dark tones are unchanged, the light tones lie between the gouge ink and the ground, cut ≥ 3:1, rapid fainter, never a path colour.
- `a_part_way_refusal_hands_back_the_holes_bored_before_it` (motion `refusal_ghost`): bore refuses hole 2 with hole 1's moves as its ghost. A refusal at hole 1 carries none, with the same words.
- `operation::cross_spindle::tests::a_ghosted_kernel_refusal_lands_its_words_spot_and_moves_in_the_world` (app lib).
- `operation::picks::tests::a_ghosted_door_refusal_is_read_like_the_plain_one` (app lib).
- `a_law_that_keeps_the_cylinder_names_it` (app `tool_body_judged`): extended with the ghosted case.
- `trochoid_bore_past_the_helix_turn_cap_is_refused` (motion `trochoid_slot`): now also accepts the `Ghosted` variant of the same refusal.

## Gate
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green (motion, app, ui suites; 5.9 min)
- `golden_cl` (6), `conformance` (25), app `refusal_ghost` (4): green. **The goldens are byte-identical.**
- The #861 suites, motion `refusal_ghost` and ui `refusal_ghost_tests`: green.
- Also run: motion `machining2d`, `machining3d`, `tiny_step`, `offset_shells`, `ruling`, `turning_face`, `posed_subtract`, `trochoid_slot`; app `operations`, `tool_body_judged`. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- Visual check on screen. The colour is pinned by the unit test only, and snapshots are release-lane.
- Ghost-carrying refusals for the circular, contour push_span, ladder, plasma, probing and turning sites are not each pinned by their own trigger. Each is a one-line `map_err` on an error path; bore pins the mechanism.
- `contour.rs` (430 lines) and `trochoid_slot.rs` (401 lines) were already over 400 lines before this change; it adds 4 and 2 lines to them.

Changelog: A refused generation that stops part-way (contour, bore, circular, trochoidal slot, 3-D ladder levels, plasma, probing, turning form and groove) now shows the moves it had built as the dashed ghost. The ghost reads on the light viewport (#871).

title: test(app): the STEP bore's heavy test pins platform-robust facts
body:
## What changed

`app pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (heavy lane) re-pinned to platform-robust facts. Test-only; no product code.

**Root cause, two parts (measured on macOS Apple silicon, release):**

1. **Platform float.** On the same commit ecb54b7f, macOS plans the bore as 5786 moves / 5753 planar / 651 arcs (Z 20.000 alone on the rings, crossing at -2.33, -2.78), against the Windows measure of #850 / PR #865 (5530 / 5497 / 600). macOS is deterministic run to run, so this is not hash order. Rust does not fuse to FMA unasked, so the most likely source is platform libm last-place rounding (sin, cos, atan2, hypot) under the STEP tessellation and the planner, amplified by the planner's knife edges (#882, #982). The test was red on macOS from the moment the counts were pinned (6c198278). Filed as #1010 (effort:max).
2. **Input change.** `git bisect --first-parent` ecb54b7f..f490458a on macOS puts the second rings level (Z 10.000, "crosses itself") at the #689 merge 575f02d8 (STEP chord cap + arc fit). #689 changed the bore's mesh and arcs on every platform (macOS now 6503 / 6467 / 222) and the heavy bore test was not re-measured there.

Not a planner bug to fix narrowly: the crossing is caught by the planner's own guard and the level falls back to Offset rings by name, and the path verifies clean. Making the plan robust to sub-micron perturbation is #882 / #982 work.

**Kept (unchanged):** no verifier warning (verifies clean), no planning-budget refusal, every rings level named by Z in the notes and the status line.

**Replaced:** "exactly one rings level, Z 20.000" -> Z 20.000 is among the rings levels, every rings level is for a crossing, at most two of five levels on the rings; "(5530, 5497, 600)" -> arcs posted, 5000..=8000 moves, >= 98 % planar feeds. Decision: `docs/decisions/984-bore-heavy-pins.md`.

## How tested (macOS Apple silicon, local, RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache)

- Reproduced red on upstream/main f490458a (Z 20.000 and Z 10.000 crossings).
- Bisect builds: ecb54b7f, 45e99d3e, 733409bf, 3bd54fc9 -> Z 20.000 only, 5786/5753/651; 575f02d8, bdf17d8a, f490458a -> Z 20.000 + Z 10.000.
- Pinned: `app pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (release, --ignored): ok, 151 s.
- app `pocket3d_hsm` (debug default): ok. motion `adaptive_band`, `adaptive_hsm`, `pocket3d_hsm` (debug): ok. motion `adaptive_hsm --ignored` (release): ok, 48 s.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

Windows and Linux: not run here. The band and level facts cover the Windows measure (5530, Z 20.000 alone) from before #689; the post-#689 Windows numbers are unknown.

title: feat(ui): edit each milling tool kind by its parameters inside the outline editor
body:
**Stacked on #957** (#852): merged `issue/852-necked-tool-envelope` into this branch (0ea437f9), because both touch `crates/app/src/mcp/cutter_tools.rs` and `crates/tools/src/lib.rs`. Until #957 merges, this diff also shows #957's commit. #957 merges first.

Slice 3 of #93: editing each milling tool kind by its parameters inside the outline editor (the Profile tab's Draw cutter view).

## What changed
- **Parameters in the outline editor** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_cutter_params.rs`). Above the points table, the Draw cutter view now shows the numbers each kind's outline is drawn from. They edit the same draft as the editor's fields, so the two always agree:
  - every milling kind: cutter Ø, flute length, shank Ø, shank length, Neck (Ø and length);
  - Ball nose / probe: ball R, shown read-only (d/2, #263);
  - Bull nose: corner R;
  - Drill: point angle;
  - Chamfer mill: cone angle;
  - End mill, tap, bore, torch: no tip parameter (a flat tip).
- **The outline follows the parameters.** A Parametric outline is redrawn from the numbers, as before. A Custom outline is carried onto the new numbers by the new `camcraft_tools::cutter_fit::refit`:
  - the tip inside the flutes is regenerated from the kind;
  - whatever is drawn above the flute top keeps its shape and moves with the flute top;
  - the shank top moves to the new one;
  - the stated shank radius follows the new shank, and anything wider than the new shank is clamped to it.

  The result is still judged live by `cutter_profile::check`. An edit that can't be carried is refused by name.
- **The neck is a parameter of the outline.** `cutter_fit::necked` and `neck_of` handle it. `Tool` has no neck number, so the neck lives only in the drawn outline. A neck at or above the shank Ø, or not fitting inside the shank length, is refused by name.
- **New undoable command `ReshapeTool`** (`crates/app/src/commands/tool_cutter.rs`). It lands the tool's numbers and its drawn cutter together, in one undo step:
  - every `ChangeTool` law runs on the new numbers (`ChangeTool::judged`, with the stale-cutter agreement skipped);
  - the outline is judged against the **new** numbers.

  Apply cutter queues it when the draft numbers moved (otherwise `SetToolCutter`, as before). The editor's Apply queues it when a drawn cutter is landed and the edit changes a number the outline is drawn to, carrying the landed outline. Before this, such an edit was refused ("reset the cutter profile to Parametric first"). `ChangeTool` alone is unchanged and still refuses.
- **MCP:** new `set_tool_cutter_params` (any of diameter / corner_r / tip_angle / flute_len / shank_d / shank_len, plus `neck` `{diameter, length}` | null | omitted). It runs the same `ReshapeTool`. `get_tool_cutter_profile` now also reports `neck`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/93-outline-param-editing.md`.

## Tests
- `camcraft-tools` `cutter_fit::tests` (4 tests): every shape edit (diameter, flute length, shank length and Ø, a retype to ball, bull, drill or chamfer) carries a hand-drawn neck and still passes `check`; every catalog milling tool carries its own outline onto new numbers; unchanged numbers leave the drawing alone; a narrower shank clamps it; the neck round-trips; and the neck refusals.
- `crates/app/tests/tool_cutter_params.rs` (3 tests, new binary): `a_parameter_edit_carries_the_drawn_cutter_in_one_undo_step`, `a_reshape_is_refused_by_name_against_the_new_numbers`, `the_tool_is_edited_by_its_parameters_over_mcp`.
- `egui_app::tests::tool_cutter_params` (5 tests): the per-kind parameters, Parametric redraw and Custom carry, the neck refusal by name, Apply cutter's one undo step, and the editor's Apply carrying a landed cutter.
- Structural twin: `egui_app::tests::structural::tool_cutter_params_structure`.
- The slice 2 suites (`tool_cutter_profile`, `egui_app::tests::tool_cutter`, `tool_profile`) still pass.
- No snapshot PNG was changed.
- Quick gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head: green (tools, app 461 s, ui 55 s; 0 failed), plus `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised
- No hand check in the GUI: the window's taller third column was checked only through AccessKit placement, not by eye.
- The camcraft-mcp skill's tool table doesn't list the new tool. It is a process file, so updating it needs a PROCESS_VERSION bump; I left it alone, the same as slice 2.
- The simulation and collision feed of the drawn profiles is #852 / PR #957; that seam is untouched.

## MCP
The new user-facing command `ReshapeTool` ships with its MCP tool, `set_tool_cutter_params`. Editing and deleting a tool by its full definition over MCP stays #734.

Changelog: Tool editor: edit a milling tool by its parameters (diameter, tip, flutes, shank, neck) inside the Draw cutter view; a drawn cutter follows the numbers instead of blocking the edit, landed with them in one undo step; MCP `set_tool_cutter_params` (#93)

title: fix(build): keep Cargo.lock intact in web/build-app-wasm.sh
body:
## What changed

`web/build-app-wasm.sh`: the `--config patch.crates-io...` build makes cargo rewrite the workspace `Cargo.lock` (flecs_ecs 0.2.2 / flecs_ecs_sys 0.2.1 lose `source` and `checksum`). The script now saves the tracked lock to `target/wasm-tools/Cargo.lock.keep` before its first cargo call (moved up from step 3, so `cargo fetch` and the wasm-bindgen install are covered too), and an `EXIT` trap restores it on success, failure and Ctrl-C/TERM. The header documents this; the only gap is SIGKILL, where the header says to run `git checkout -- Cargo.lock`.

Note: the main-branch script already had a restore trap on the cargo build step. The bug as filed reproduces only without it (a direct cargo call with the same `--config` dirties `Cargo.lock`). This PR moves the save/trap ahead of every cargo call and documents it.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/949-wasm-script-lock.md` (restore-from-copy chosen over a temp manifest dir).

## Readings (run in the worktree, `git status --short`)

- Before the change, direct cargo with the same `--config` patches: ` M Cargo.lock` (bug reproduced).
- Failed run, new script (wasm32 target not installed, so cargo fails after resolving): exit 101, `error[E0463]: can't find crate for core`; `git status --short` shows only the script edit, `Cargo.lock` clean.
- Interrupt check with the same save/restore shape and a 30 s step: lock dirty mid-run (` M Cargo.lock`), clean after SIGINT (EXIT trap runs on signal exit).
- `bash -n web/build-app-wasm.sh`: ok.

## Not exercised

- A successful full wasm build: the wasm32-unknown-unknown target is not installed on the test machine, so the success path was not run. It uses the same EXIT trap, but this is unverified by a real success run.
- No test was added. The repo has no shell-test harness, and a grep-style "script contains the trap" test would prove little. The readings above are the proof.
- No PowerShell twin exists (`web/` has only `build-app-wasm.sh`), so nothing to fix there.

## Notes

- `web/` scripts may be marked `needs-maintainer` by the PR reviewer as scripts; that is expected.
- Not a process file (not in AGENTS.md's list), so no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump.
- Fork synced at v0.17.0.

title: fix(post): command-line post mirrors a vendor .mch like the app
body:
## What changed

`post --machine <file>` (`crates/post/src/bin/post.rs`) handed the engine the raw `.mch` JSON. `script_props` reads only the static grammar (`kinematics.static.*`), and every shipped machine is a vendor kinematics tree (`kinematics.default.parts`). So the CLI script saw no rotaries, no spindle max, no coolant codes and no rates.

The binary now posts a vendor tree with `post::machine::mirror(parse_mch(..))`, the same value the app hands the engine (`posting_mounts::machine_value_for`). It calls this through a small `script_machine` helper. The mirror already lives in camcraft-post, so no new crate edge is added.

- A static-grammar file (no `kinematics.default.parts`) still posts exactly as written. Mirroring it would empty it.
- The raw-file refusals run first and are unchanged: the parse errors and `inverted_post_refusal` (inverted Z or a letter other than X/Y).
- The mirror carries the file's inverted axes as `invertedAxes`, computed by the same `Machine::inverted_axes`, so `invert::apply` mirrors or refuses an inverted X/Y the same way it did before.

Decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/996-cli-post-mirrored-machine.md`.

## Before / after

- **Before:** `post --machine assets/machines/tilthead.mch fanuc.cps <tilted stream>` warned "tilted move on a machine without a tilting rotary" and wrote no angle words. On `vmc.mch`, a 20000 rpm stream gave no spindle warning, and a mist op got no M7.
- **After:** tilthead posts G43.4 with A/B words and M8, with no warnings. vmc warns "spindle rpm over machine maximum" at 20000 rpm (max 12000) and posts M7 for mist. In both cases the CLI's program is byte-equal to `engine::run(cps, mirror(parse_mch(file)), stream)`, the app's program.

## Tests

- New suite `crates/post/tests/vendor_mch_cli.rs`:
  - `the_cli_posts_a_tilted_stream_on_the_shipped_tilthead`
  - `the_cli_holds_a_shipped_machines_spindle_max_and_coolant_codes`

  Both fail on the old binary and pass on this head.
- The existing `axis_direction_cli` tests still pass: inverted X mirrored, inverted Z refused by name, unverified script refused.
- I ran every `crates/post/tests` suite by hand (post_engine, axis_direction_cli, comp, comp_plane, mch_head_search, vendor_mch_cli), plus `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`.

## Not exercised

- I only checked the Fanuc post through the CLI on vendor files. The other scripts read the same `machine` global the app already feeds them.
- I did not compare the CLI against the app on a `.mch` whose default holder the holder library would refuse. The CLI keeps the word-only reader, because camcraft-post does not depend on camcraft-tools. That check only refuses and never changes a posted word.

## Follow-up

The #926 recorded runner (`crates/post/tests/recorded/mod.rs`, PR #1002, also edited on #994's branch) works around this bug by mirroring the machine itself. title: fix(motion): name every adaptive level cut by rings; read only ladder planes
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branched from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed
- **`machining3d::hsm::plan_level`**: every arm that hands an Adaptive level to the Offset rings now goes through one helper, `rings_named`. These arms are: a level the seam crosses, a narrowed helix on the wrap, a hard planner refusal on the wrap, and `adaptive_passes`' own fallback. The helper writes `<why> - Offset rings cut <level> instead`, with the level named by its Z, or by its developed radius on the wrap. The text of every note is unchanged. A guard was added: if the planner ever hands back rings without a note naming the level, `plan_level` adds one. Toolpaths and verdicts do not change. Only notes are affected, and only if that guard ever fires.
- **The reported case was a test-reader artifact.** I reproduced "radius 5.6 cut by rings, no note" on #882's held commit 70ac996f with `INSET = 0` (the "0.25 um thinning" variant). It is not a planner fallback. The 5.0 level's microlift lifts to 5.6, and one down ramp runs 5.7 -> 5.6 -> 5.5 with a vertex on 5.6. The rotary_adaptive reader counted any plane that a descent ends on as a cut level. It therefore read the lifted runs as a level with 7 planar moves, no arcs and no load. The reader (`rotary_adaptive_fixture::read_levels`) now reads only the ladder's own planes (`top - k * stepdown`) and takes the stepdown as an argument.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/983-rings-fallback-note.md`. It covers why rest and shell passes keep their single note, and why the r6.2 travel pin was left alone (its flip is #982's microlift-acceptance knife edge).

## How tested (local, macOS, debug unless noted)
- New pins: `machining3d::hsm::fallback_tests::{a_developed_level_the_planner_refuses_is_named_by_its_radius, a_planar_level_the_planner_refuses_is_named_by_its_z, a_developed_level_the_seam_cuts_is_named_by_its_radius}` and `rotary_adaptive::a_microlift_plane_is_not_read_as_an_unnamed_ring_level`.
- motion lib: 192 passed. adaptive_hsm 1, adaptive_band 2, pocket3d_hsm (motion) 3, rotary_adaptive 3: all pass.
- Release `--ignored`: adaptive_hsm 5/5, rotary_adaptive 3/3. adaptive_band has no ignored tests.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Repro check: on #882's held commit with `INSET = 0` and this PR's reader, the phantom 5.6 level is gone and all three rotary heavy tests pass.

## Not exercised
- App and UI suites: no note text changed, so nothing reads differently there. The app `pocket3d_hsm` bore heavy test is #984's and was not run.
- The new guard cannot fire on any current path; it is defensive and has no test that drives it.

Overlaps: none with #953 (grow.rs not touched), #982 or #882.

Changelog: none (notes-only refactor plus a test-reader fix; no output change)

Fixes #983

title: fix(import): STEP parse error names the failing entity and line
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0.

## What changed
When `ruststep` rejects a STEP file it fails the whole DATA section and its position is not the bad entity (#887). `step_diag::locate` (new, `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_diag.rs`) now re-scans the text once after a parse failure: records split on `;` outside `'..'` strings and `/* */` comments, line numbers tracked, DATA..ENDSEC followed, each record parsed alone with ruststep's `entity_instance`. The first failing record is named. Unterminated strings/comments name the line they opened on; a file with no DATA section says so. If every record parses alone, ruststep's own message is kept. Linear in file size (each byte visited once, each record parsed once); no unwrap/expect/panic. ruststep is not patched.

## Error text
- Old: `syntax error: <ruststep position, at the DATA section>`
- New: `syntax error in DATA section: entity #9 at line 16 cannot be parsed: #9 = PRODUCT_DEFINITION_CONTEXT('part definition' #2, 'design')`
- Also: `syntax error: comment starting at line 6 is never closed`, `syntax error: no DATA section found`.

## Tests (crates/app/tests/import.rs)
`step_parse_error_names_the_bad_entity_and_line` (hand-made fixture `testdata/models/bad_entity_mid_data.step`, empty_list.step with one comma removed), `step_parse_error_line_survives_strings_and_comments`, `step_parse_error_unterminated_and_no_data`. Real HOOPS Exchange file from #887 (vendor files are not committed); multi-GB files; complex-entity (`#n = ( A() B() );`) failures beyond the shared per-record parser.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/912-step-error-line.md`.

title: feat(threadmill)!: thread-mill tool kinds and a reworked helical thread-milling operation
body:
## What changed

First slice of #894: thread mills can be stored, and an internal thread-milling operation verifies clean and posts helical G2/G3 with Z.

**Tool model**
- Two new tool kinds: `thread_mill` (multi-form: rows of teeth at one pitch) and `thread_mill_single` (single-form: one row, a pitch range). They read diameter (across the crests), form angle (`tip_angle`), `pitch`, cutting length (`flute_len`), flutes and shank; a single-form mill also reads the new `pitch_min` key. Sanity law, pitch door and form door live in `crates/tools/src/thread_mill.rs`.
- Library and project file round-trip (`pitch_min` is written only when set; additive, no project-version step), the tool editor (kind list, pitch / pitch range / form angle rows, a sane draft when the kind is picked), the tree's kind name, the operation digest, and two starter-catalog tools (`TM-0600-P125`, `TMS-0600-P050-150`).
- The program simulation sweeps a thread mill at its tooth roots, the reading a tap already has (#266).

**Thread operation** (the existing `Thread` kind, reworked)
- The kernel is rewritten (`machining2d/thread_mill.rs`, `thread_ride.rs`): radial passes are full helices (equal steps, the last on the thread depth), a single-form mill winds one turn per thread, a multi-form mill makes one revolution per level; tangential lead-in / lead-out arcs that keep the helix's axial rate; climb / conventional and right / left hand by the handbook rule; the tip never below the floor, no rapid below the feature's top; the feed stated at the cutting edge and programmed at the tool centre.
- New operation fields `pitch` (optional: unstated reads a multi-form mill's own) and `hand`; both in the file, the page (Passes tab) and the MCP `add_operation` / `edit_operation` params.
- Refusals by name when the operation is created, edited, retyped or re-tooled, and again at generate: a pitch outside a single-form mill's range, a pitch other than a multi-form mill's, a form angle other than 60 degrees, an infeed past the thread depth, a mill no smaller than a hole's minor diameter, a zero / negative / non-finite pitch. A single-form mill with the pitch not stated yet is an unfinished operation (a new Thread operation starts that way): it may be made and edited, and generate refuses it by name.
- Gouge laws: the tooth crests are judged against the thread's major circle (tangency law), the body under the teeth against the part solid with no allowance at the tip (solid law). The crossing law stands down for Thread only (passes retrace one helix by design).

**Why the kernel was rewritten rather than extended** - on `main` no Thread operation can post: the old ride retraces itself (the crossing law convicts every pair) and stands past the hole rim (the tangency law convicts every move). It also deepened the radius turn by turn while descending, so the top threads were shallower than the bottom ones, and its "climb" wound counter-clockwise while descending, which is a left-hand helix. Details and sources: `docs/decisions/894-thread-mill.md`.

## Breaking

- A `Thread` operation no longer accepts a Tap-kind tool (`tool_law::THREAD_MILL` was `[Tap]`). An existing one shows the tool law's after-state and refuses to generate or post until its tool is re-kinded as a thread mill.
- Every existing `Thread` operation reads Stale once (its digest now carries pitch and hand) and regenerates to the new ride.
- `Tool` gains the field `pitch_min`: a branch that builds a full `Tool { .. }` literal needs `pitch_min: 0.0` after it merges main.

## How tested

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

Quick gate on the final head `d5f32a6a`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` - tools, motion, app and ui suites, 4 steps, 0 failed (12.3 min; the diff touches the tool model, so the plan is every suite of the four crates). A first run failed to compile one app test (`tests/tool_law.rs`, an exhaustive `ToolKind` match) and was fixed before this head. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Pinning tests:
- `camcraft-tools` (lib): `thread_mill::tests::*` (4) - the two kinds' sanity, the pitch door, the form door.
- `camcraft-motion` (lib): `machining2d::thread_tests::*` (8) - hand and orbit sense for all 16 hand / climb / internal-external / form combinations, equal passes landing on the ISO depth, one shared helix across passes and levels, floor and no-rapid-below-top laws, the lead arcs' form law (a 60-degree tooth never leaves the groove), the centre-feed scaling, a boss never cut past its depth, the refusals.
- `camcraft-app` `--test thread_mill` (8): M8 x 1.25 with the multi-form mill and M8 x 1 with the single-form mill through the command path - no blocking warning, the post gate passes, the program simulation finds no gouge, Fanuc output carries `G03 ... Z ... I ...` blocks; left-hand and conventional variants; a mill whose roots meet the wall is a gouge; a bottom below the blind floor is a gouge; the creation-time refusals; a gated, undoable pitch edit; tool JSON and project-file round trip.
- `camcraft-app` (lib): `operation::thread_op::tests::*` (3) - the crest region, the root cutter, the crossing stand-down is Thread-only.
- `camcraft-app` `--test mill2d_c`: the M2.4 C thread tests, updated to the new ride and tool kind.
- `camcraft-app` `--test mcp`: `thread_milling_over_the_tools`.
- `camcraft-ui` (lib): `egui_app::tool_thread_mill_row::tests::picking_a_thread_mill_kind_seeds_a_sane_tool_and_round_trips`, `egui_app::thread_mill_page_tests::the_thread_page_states_the_pitch_and_the_hand_and_apply_undoes`.
- `camcraft-app` `--test tool_gate` / `--test tool_law`: updated for the new kinds (the Thread row's catalog hint is now `TM-0600-P125`).

Goldens added (none moved):
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_internal_single_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_internal_multi_form_left_hand.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_external_single_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/thread_mill_m8_fine_single_form.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/thread_mill_m8_multi_form.nc`

## Known gap (read before merging)

- **An undrilled hole is not refused.** A thread mill is not centre-cutting, and the ride feeds it down the hole's axis. Nothing yet checks that an earlier operation opened the hole: on a part whose hole is modelled, a Thread operation with no drilling before it generates and verifies clean. Before this PR no Thread operation could post at all, so this path is newly reachable. The check needs the stock the earlier operations leave standing (the grid `operation::drill_prior` reads) and is filed as #992 (`bug`, P1). The tests here thread a modelled hole in a solid stock box with no drill before it - they pin the ride and the part laws, not that entry.

## What was not exercised

- External threads at the operation level: the kernel cuts a boss and is pinned by tests and a golden, but the operation always passes `external: false` (no boss recognition or pick, and the static region cannot judge a tool beside a boss). Filed as #985.
- The thread form in the simulation and the tool preview: the stock sim removes the root cylinder only, and the tool draws as the cylinder its crests sweep. Filed as #986.
- Forms other than 60 degrees (Whitworth, NPT taper, trapezoidal) are refused, not cut. Filed as #987.
- Spring passes, unequal pass depths, a stated thread-depth override and M4 (left-hand cutter) climb sense. Filed as #988.
- Posts other than Fanuc were not run on a thread program; the inverted-machine post path already refuses a helical arc by name (`post/invert.rs`) and was not changed.
- The UI rows were compiled and unit-tested through the draft; no pixel snapshot was touched and the release-lane snapshot suite was not run.
- The heavy `--ignored` release lanes and the batch tier's clippy over untouched crates.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill text does not yet mention the new kinds and fields (a process file; it would need a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump). Filed as #989 (`MCP:`).

Changelog: Thread mills (multi-form and single-form) as tool kinds, and a reworked Thread operation that cuts internal threads by helical interpolation - radial passes, climb / conventional, right / left hand - verifies clean and posts G2/G3 with Z; breaking: a Thread operation no longer accepts a Tap-kind tool.

Effort: max (no escalation)

Refs #894

title: fix(app): face, trace and contour on imported meshes with float-noise corners
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a82c45bcf8ba44e8258a77b3cf5b31397).

## What reproduced, and what did not

I loaded the user's `cutouts.camproj` (attachment to #241) through the project API on upstream/main f490458a. For Face, Trace, 2D Contour and 2D Pocket I created an op with the GUI's default parameters and gave it each of these picks: the planar top face, all 57 edge chains rimming it, the outer rim's 4 chains, one cutout's 9 chains, and the whole model as the source.

**Already fixed on main (pinned there):**
- Picking the face and the edges resolves: 1 outer ring and 6 hole rings.
- Facing on the face pick used to refuse with "15.15 mm gap / 3 mm tool". That was #260, fixed by PR #313 (merge `1da9695b`) and shipped in v0.15.0. It is pinned by `face_concave_holes` in camcraft-motion. Face on the face pick now generates 726 moves on main.
- Trace, 2D Contour and 2D Pocket on the face pick and on the edge picks generated on main.

**Still failing on main, fixed here (all three were wrong refusals on a valid closed part):**
1. **Face on the edge picks refused**: "two holes stand 0.63 mm apart on the row at Y=-25.50". A chain-only Face pick is clipped by the part's silhouette. That silhouette came from the fallback (see 2), which unions the facet shadows through `Region::new`'s nesting parity. Any bottom-face facet whose shadow lay inside a top-face facet's shadow became a hole, so 27 phantom triangles (up to 433 mm²) were cut into the solid webs. The fallback is now a pure union (`Region::union_all`, each shadow oriented CCW).
2. **The slicer refused the closed mesh**: "open at z = -19.375: 12 dangling chord ends". The part's shared corners scatter by up to 1.04 µm, and the slicer's 1 µm rounded weld key split crossing pairs that straddled a rounding boundary. The slicer keeps the exact key as its first try. Only when that leaves ends dangling does it re-slice with chord ends welded within 2 µm through a neighbourhood search, in the new `camcraft_geometry::geometry::slice_weld`. Every mesh that sliced before slices exactly as before. A real 0.1 mm gap is still refused as open. A first version used the tolerance weld for every slice; the gate caught it moving an exact mesh's islands (`blind_floor` Crossing), so it is a fallback only (second commit). This also fixes Face with the whole model as its source, which refused with the same "open mesh" error.
3. **Contour and Trace with the whole model as source refused** with "no material at z = 0.000". The part's top corners are uneven by 3e-13 mm, and a section exactly at Top of Part met only the highest corner. `section` now retries 1 µm lower on an empty answer, as it already did on an error. A plane that really misses the part still refuses, and the message now says what to change: "the source spans Z0.000 to Z5.000; set Top of Part Z inside that span, or pick the face or edges to machine".

After the fix, every pick set above generates on the user's project for all four kinds with no verifier warnings. Face on edge picks produces the same 726-move path as Face on the face pick.

**Not part of this fix:** the issue's aside asks for box selection of edges. That is a new UI feature, filed as #979.

## Changed
- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/slice_weld.rs` (new): the exact weld plus a tolerance weld (spatial hash over neighbouring cells). `slice.rs` tries exact, then tolerant on `Open`.
- `crates/app/src/operation/picks.rs`: `silhouette`'s fallback is `facet_shadow`, a pure union.
- `crates/app/src/operation/material.rs`: `section` retries on empty, and the empty refusal names the Z span.
- `docs/decisions/241-cutouts-ops.md`: the reproduction and the decisions.

## Tests (each fails on the old code; checked by reverting the fix file and rerunning)
- `an_open_mesh_rim_pick_faces_the_whole_top_with_no_phantom_holes` (camcraft-app `face_holes`): an open plate with nested bottom facets, rim chains picked. The region is one 1600 mm² loop, and the path equals the face pick's path.
- `sub_micrometre_corner_scatter_still_welds_into_a_closed_slice` and `a_tenth_of_a_millimetre_gap_is_still_open` (camcraft-geometry `slice`). The second one passes on the old code too; it is the control that the tolerance stays at micrometre scale.
- `a_whole_model_contour_at_a_noisy_top_sections_the_part` and `a_top_plane_above_the_part_still_refuses_and_names_the_span` (camcraft-app `top_plane_noise`, new). The contour stays a tool radius off the box and has no warnings.

The user's project itself is not committed: it is 697 KB and the user's file. The synthetic fixtures reproduce each mechanism.

## Gate
`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` fell back to the batch plan because camcraft-geometry changed. It ran geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui suites plus clippy `-D warnings` across all of them: **green** on the final head 45373c9b (9 steps, 15.1 min). The first run, on 7132909e, was red on `blind_floor` (see item 2) and led to the fallback-only weld.

## Not exercised
- The GUI itself: no viewport clicks. The picks were driven through `SetOperationGeometry`, which is the command the clicks use.
- Release-tier heavy lanes and the snapshot PNGs. No PNG was changed.
- Goldens: none moved (`golden_cl` and `solid_law_goldens` pass unchanged).

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: Facing, Trace and 2D Contour work on imported parts whose corners carry float noise: edge picks no longer refuse on phantom holes, a closed mesh no longer slices as "open", and a whole-model contour at Top of Part no longer reads "no material" (#241)

Fixes #241

title: test(post): per-post script suites on recorded edge-case streams
body:
Slice 1 of #926, per the maintainer's direction on the issue: every shipped post script is tested against the post binary on a shared set of recorded edge-case intermediate files, with no `camcraft_app` and no toolpath generation in the suites.

## What changed

- **`crates/post/tests/script_<stem>.rs`** - one suite per `assets/posts/*.cps` (11). Each is three lines: `post_suite!("<stem>.cps")` generates one `#[test]` per recorded case, so a failure names the post and the case. Each names its script, so #923 (PR #967) selects it on a `.cps` change.
- **`crates/post/tests/recorded/mod.rs`** - the shared runner: runs `CARGO_BIN_EXE_post` (`--log` for warnings) on `recorded/streams/<case>.cnc` and compares with `recorded/golden/<stem>/<case>.nc` (the released program: exit 0, no warning) or `<case>.refusal` (the named refusal: the counted warnings the in-app gate blocks on, or the error the binary stopped on). `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` records them.
- **`crates/post/tests/recorded/streams/*.cnc`** - the nine recorded inputs (the post's `.cnc` intermediate: the `.cl` dump carries no tool, spindle, section, thread or probing records).
- **Staleness guards** - `crates/post/tests/recorded_streams.rs` rebuilds the six cl-built streams (cl `PathBuilder` + `post::dump` + `cnc::serialize`) byte for byte; `crates/app/tests/recorded_post_streams.rs` rebuilds `probe` (`motion::probing::probe_cycle`) and `drill_retract` (`motion::drilling::drill`) - app is the one crate that sees both motion and post, so no new crate edge. The one hand-written stream (`full_circle_raw`) is guarded by "parses, and the writer gives back the same text, and it holds its 360-degree record". The post guard also fails when a shipped `.cps` has no suite, when the stream dir and the case list disagree, or when a known post bug has a golden.
- `docs/decisions/926-post-script-suites.md`.

No product code changed. No new dependency between crates.

## Edge cases (shared by all posts)

| Case | What | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `arcs` | XY ccw + cw, XZ, YZ (split at its Z extremum by the builder), a 2 mm helix | cl, guarded in post |
| `full_circle` | a ring as the generators write it (two XY halves) | cl, guarded in post |
| `full_circle_raw` | one 360-degree arc record (a foreign producer could write it) | hand-written, round-trip guard |
| `drill_retract` | two pecked holes, R plane Z1, hop Z3, clearance Z10 | motion, guarded in app |
| `tool_change` | T1 facing (M3), then T2 a left-hand thread toward -Z that needs M4 (`PARAM SpindleDirection reverse`) | cl, guarded in post |
| `rotary` | 3+2 index to A30, a feed that changes the lean to B30, commanded return upright; posted on `tilthead.mch` | cl, guarded in post |
| `probe` | bore centre, four touches, sets G55 | motion, guarded in app |
| `empty_section` | a section with no motion | `post::dump` of an empty path, guarded in post |
| `extreme_coords` | 1 um moves, a 2 um arc, +-9999.999 and 99999.999 mm, F1 and F99999 | cl, guarded in post |

## Golden / refusal matrix

`nc` = program golden, `R` = refusal golden (its named reason), `BUG #n` = known post bug: posted, not compared, no golden.

## Post bugs found (filed, not baked into goldens)

- **#994 (P0)** - canned-cycle posts (fanuc, haas, mazak, sinumerik, tormach, doosan-dnm) traverse between holes at the R plane, below the hop the verified path uses. Already visible in the app golden `nc/drill_plate.nc` (R0: rapid X10 -> X30 at Z0).

body:
## What changed

Issue #879 asked for the remaining user-facing "setup furniture" errors to be
reworded and for the frame-watch clamp to be pinned.

**Wording: no change needed on this base.** Re-checked on upstream/main
(f490458a). No string literal in `crates/` says "furniture". The four
messages the issue cites already read:

- `commands/repair_model.rs` (`not a model`): "'...' is not a model - it is a setup's stock or work offset, a setup, a tool, an operation or other CAM data" (was "setup furniture")
- `commands/update_model.rs` (`not a model`): same text as above
- `commands/tool.rs` (reserved name): "'...' is a name reserved for a setup's stock and work offsets"
- `commands/setup.rs` (`:95`, `:109`): "a setup name must not contain '/' - names with '/' are reserved for a setup's own stock and work offset"; "'...' is a name reserved for a setup's stock and work offsets"

The existing guards already assert the absence of the word: `tests/repair_model.rs`
(`!contains("furniture")`) and `setup_refusals_never_say_furniture` in
`tests/setups.rs` (#878).

**Test hardening (the code change):** `FrameWatch::excuse` clamp case
`an_excuse_is_clamped_to_the_time_since_the_last_mark` in
`crates/ui/src/egui_app/frame_watch.rs`. A 200 ms commands phase, then
`excuse(5 s)` at +210 ms, then `end` must still report "slow frame 200 ms"
and `"commands" 200 ms`. Without the clamp the stamps move past `now`, the
frame reads as 0 ms and `end` returns `None`, so the test fails.

Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/879-furniture-wording.md` (a repo-wide
source scan for "furniture" was dropped: literals span lines and identifiers
sit beside them, so it would need a lexer to avoid false positives).

## Tests

title: test(goldens): post NC goldens only for programs the gate passes
body:
## What changed

`contour_disc_hole` and `contour_tangential_lead` were refused by the program gate. Their 3 mm leads on the R6 bore (6 mm tool, so the cutter centre runs on an r = 3 ring) lie on that ring's own circle, so the leads crossed it (`Warning::Crossing`). Yet both had posted NC goldens in every milling dialect, compared byte for byte by `conformance`.

I took **option (a)** and moved the leads. Both fixtures now use **2 mm** leads (quarter arc and half arc). These sit inside the ring, tangent at the seam, and both programs verify clean. I probed 0.5 / 1 / 1.5 / 2 / 2.5 mm and all were clean; 2 mm leaves a full millimetre of margin. Each fixture still tests what it was made for:
- `contour_disc_hole` still shows a tessellated round bore fitting to arcs. That comes from the ring, not the lead.
- `contour_tangential_lead` still shows a half-arc lead posting as one `S±1` arc with a 2 x radius standoff (now 4 mm).

The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/862-refused-program-goldens.md`.

**The refusal is kept.** `solid_law_goldens::a_lead_on_the_rings_own_circle_is_refused` builds the old 3 mm programs on the same plate inside the test (no golden is kept for them). It asserts the exact crossing pairs the old verdicts carried: 6 for the arc lead, 12 for the tangential lead.

**New guard.** `solid_law_goldens::every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` walks every `.nc` under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/` whose stem is a `.cl` golden. Each one must meet one of three conditions:
- a depth-law golden (judged by `verdicts()`) must verify clean;
- a golden no depth law judges must be named in `UNJUDGED` with its reason (slots, trochoid, trace, `arc_planes`, `plasma_plate_with_holes`);
- a golden of a refused program must carry `refused program, posted for syntax conformance` on its first line (option (c)'s door; nothing uses it today).

So a new posted golden is either judged or explicitly classified. Before the fix, the guard would fail on the 16 disc-hole `.nc` files.

`every_depth_law_golden_verifies_exactly_as_before` now asserts that all 14 depth-law goldens verify clean.

`solid_law_goldens.rs` was at 405 lines. Its plate/part builders (`rect`, `circle`, `region`, `walls`, `cap`, `plate`, `plate_cell`, `mill`) moved verbatim, now `pub`, into `crates/app/tests/common/solid_part.rs`. The two files are now 338 and 151 lines.

## Goldens that moved (regenerated, none deleted)

CL (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test golden_cl -- contour_disc_hole_matches_golden contour_tangential_lead_matches_golden`):
- `crates/app/tests/golden/contour_disc_hole.cl`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/contour_tangential_lead.cl`

NC (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test conformance`), `contour_disc_hole.nc` and `contour_tangential_lead.nc` in each of:
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/` (Fanuc)
- `nc/haas/`, `nc/sinumerik/`, `nc/heidenhain/`, `nc/mazak/`, `nc/tormach/`, `nc/doosan-dnm/`, `nc/carvera/`

That is 18 files. No other golden moved, and no snapshot PNG was touched.

**How they were checked.** I read the diffs; I did not just accept them.
- Both CL files keep `moves=69`, and every move keeps its kind.
- Only the lead-in/lead-out moves and the rapids/plunges to their start points moved; the ring and the outer contour are byte-identical.
- I checked the new arcs by hand. The bore lead arc centre (19.951, 9.002) is 2.000 from its endpoints and 1.0 from the bore centre (= 3 - 2), so it is internally tangent to the ring.
- The tangential lead's start point (20.049, 11.000) is 4.0 from the ring seam (19.853, 7.005), which is the 2r standoff.
- The outer lead centre (40.576, -4.967) is 2.000 from (40.346, -2.98).
- Every NC file keeps its line count (+/- balanced). The NC I/J words match the CL centres, e.g. Fanuc `G02 X40.346 Y-2.98 I-0.231 J1.986` and Heidenhain `I+40.576 J-4.967`.

## Tests

- Pinning:
  - `solid_law_goldens::a_lead_on_the_rings_own_circle_is_refused` (the refusal)
  - `solid_law_goldens::every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes` (the guard)
  - `solid_law_goldens::every_depth_law_golden_verifies_exactly_as_before` (now all clean)
- `#[test]` count: `solid_law_goldens` 1 -> 3; no other file changed its count. Before: 1, after: 3 (+2 new tests, none removed).
- Gate, all on head `a78f977e`:
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 278 camcraft-app test binaries, 2037 passed, 0 failed, 18 ignored. This includes `conformance`, `solid_law_goldens`, `golden_cl`, `posting`, `fanuc_post`, `heidenhain_block_form`, `arc_planes`, `tormach_post`, `tormach_end_units` and `program_comments`.
  - The golden readers in other crates are green: `camcraft-post` `post_engine` (33/33) and `camcraft-cl` `headless_bin` (3/3; its `moves: 69 (... arcs 33)` stat holds).
  - Each of the three pinning tests passes on its own via `cargo xtask gate test <name> --crate camcraft-app --binary solid_law_goldens --exact`.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- `plasma_plate_with_holes` is named in `UNJUDGED`: its plasma program is not run through the plasma gate here. That is the same as before, just named now.
- The slot, trace and trochoid goldens get no gate verdict in this suite. No depth law runs on them, as the suite header already said.
- No GUI, and no release-lane heavy tests.

title: fix(sim): drill reach, cross drill and probe stylus read the body's band stack
body:
**Stacked on #957** (issue #852, branch `issue/852-necked-tool-envelope`). The base here is upstream `main`, so until #957 merges this diff also shows #957's commit (`54ed3fe7`); this PR's own change is the single commit on top (`fix(sim): drill reach, cross drill and probe stylus read the body's band stack`). Merge #957 first.

## What changed

#835 moved most of the stack laws onto a modelled tool body's band stack (`Cutter::body`) but left three on the cylinder enclosing the body. #957 later did the same for the neck. This PR moves those last three onto the bands, so they judge the same shape the simulation draws:

- **Axial holder-face law** (`operation::drill_reach::axial_reach`): each band's face disc (`bottom + band.above`, at that band's own radius) is checked against the material top over that disc (prior grid read at that radius). A refusal names the offending band: "tool T's body band (dia. D, A mm above the tip) sinks to Z ...".
- **Cross-drill holder law** (`drill_reach::cross_holder`): the per-move law (the on-station tube, or the swing's swept rectangle) runs once per band, at that band's face, radius and length. The per-band body is split out into `band_clear`. `seg_dist`, `holder_approach` and `hull_dist` moved verbatim into `drill_hull.rs` to keep the file under 400 lines.
- **Cross-drill part law** (`operation::cross_part::part_clear`): now takes the body-carrying cutter (`Cutter::of(tool).with_body(..)`, the one `generate` builds) and re-judges it against the tool's geometry (`Cutter::judged`).
- **Probe stylus** (`operation::probe_op::stylus_cutter(tool, stack)`): rebuilt as ball, stem, probe body (the record's shank band), then the body's own bands, checked as a `BodyBands` of the stylus stack.
- `run_job_arms` now builds `geom` / `holder` / `cutter` once at the top, so the probe and drill arms can use them. The code at the old site moved up unchanged.
- The enclosure wording ("judged here by the cylinder enclosing it") is gone wherever the bands are read. It stays only for the fallback case: a body whose stack does not fit the record (`body_judged::falls_back`, used for generator refusals), or one that does not fit the stylus (the probe note).

Safety: no body, or a stack equal to the holder cylinder, carries nothing. The laws then read exactly the `holder()` cylinder they read before, with the same refusal text (pinned to the byte). A carried band that is non-finite, starts below the shank's top, or is wider than the enclosing holder is not trusted, and the cylinder stands in. No holder modelled still sweeps nothing, and a non-finite holder field is still refused by name. The probe is handed a stack only when the tool has a body.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/842-band-stack-drill-probe.md`.

## Pinning tests

Each law is pinned three ways: a stepped body whose flange clears is no longer refused, a flange that reaches is still refused, and a tool with no body reads unchanged.

- Axial (`crates/app/src/operation/drill_reach_body_tests.rs`): `a_stepped_body_whose_flange_clears_the_wall_is_not_refused_by_the_axial_holder_law`, `a_stepped_body_whose_flange_sinks_beside_the_wall_is_still_refused_by_the_axial_holder_law`, `a_tool_with_no_body_reads_the_holder_cylinder_bit_identically`
- Cross holder (same file): `a_stepped_body_whose_flange_clears_the_ear_is_not_refused_by_the_cross_holder_law`, `a_stepped_body_whose_flange_meets_the_ear_is_still_refused_by_the_cross_holder_law`
- Cross part (`crates/app/src/operation/cross_part_tests.rs`): `a_stepped_body_whose_flange_clears_the_part_is_not_refused_by_the_cross_part_law`, `a_stepped_body_whose_flange_meets_the_part_is_still_refused_by_the_cross_part_law`, `a_tool_with_no_body_reads_the_cutter_it_always_did`
- Probe and end to end (`crates/app/tests/tool_body_drill_probe.rs`): `a_stepped_body_over_the_stylus_is_judged_by_its_bands`, `a_flange_over_the_stylus_that_meets_the_part_is_still_refused`, `a_probe_with_no_body_reads_its_one_band_unchanged`, `a_drawn_stepped_body_on_a_drill_is_judged_by_its_bands_not_the_enclosing_cylinder` (through `operation::generate` with `SetToolBody::spun`), `a_drawn_body_on_a_probe_is_judged_by_its_bands_end_to_end`

## Readings

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`, full plan, final head): green - tools, sim, motion, app (incl. lib, tool_body_drill_probe, drill_reach*, drilling_cross*, probe_*, tool_body*), ui: 5 steps, 0 failed, 1526 tests passed, 22.2 min wall
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Moved goldens: none. No golden or snapshot carries a tool body. No snapshot PNG touched.

## Not exercised

- An imported-mesh body (#368) end to end on a cross drill. The cross laws are pinned at law level with hand-built band stacks; the drawn-profile path is pinned end to end for the axial drill and the probe.
- The multi-axis shank-avoidance dodge (`motion::multiaxis::avoid`) stays on the cylinder: it is a generator choice, not a verdict, and #835 lists it as kept.
- Lathe cross drilling with a body: same code path as the mill-turn cross drill. Its existing suites ran in the quick gate.

Changelog: Drill reach, the cross-drill holder and part laws, and the touch probe's stylus reach judge a modelled tool body by its band stack, so a stepped body is no longer refused for a flange that never reaches the material (#842)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at v0.17.0.

Fixes #842

title: docs(process): add test-placement, crate-edge and app-scope rules
body:
## What changed

Process-only (docs). Three placement rules are added to AGENTS.md, named in the PR-reviewer checklist and the work-issue skill. PROCESS_VERSION 16 -> 17.

Quoted as added:

**AGENTS.md "Code shape"** (two bullets, after "One concern per subcrate"):

- **`app` holds the document, nothing else** (maintainer, 2026-11-11: "high cohesion, low coupling, because every gate is costly"). New code goes in `crates/app/src` only if it reads or writes the ECS world, the project file, a command, MCP or the CLI. Code that works only on domain values (cl, geometry, tools, post, sim, motion types) goes in the crate that owns them, and `app` re-exports it. A reviewer checks this from the new file's `use` lines: if none names one of those six things, the file is in the wrong crate.
- **No new dependency between our crates without a decision.** A `camcraft-*` entry added to `[dependencies]` or `[dev-dependencies]` in any `crates/*/Cargo.toml` needs a `docs/decisions/` entry in the same PR. The entry lists the imported items, says why the caller cannot pass the value in instead (a parameter, a closure, a recorded file), and names what now rebuilds when the dependency changes. An edge that would carry fewer than five items is not added: the caller passes the value in. (The wording of the five-item clause is the maintainer's to confirm.)

**AGENTS.md "Testing"** (the `crates/app/tests/` line is corrected, then one rule added):

- **A test lives with the code it tests.** A new test file goes in the lowest crate that provides everything it imports, and its Gate map names that crate (`camcraft_post::engine`, not `app::post`). A file in `crates/app/tests/` must import something `crates/app/src` defines; a test that uses only another crate's re-exports (`app::post`, `app::verify`, `app::machining2d`) belongs in that crate's `tests/`. A test that needs another crate's output reads a recorded file (`.cl`, `.cnc`) rather than importing that crate's generator.

Also: `.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md` law check gets a "Placement" item naming (a), (b), (c); `.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md` section 2 names the same three rules. `docs/decisions/920-placement-rules.md` records the decision.

## Decision on the fourth rule

The research proposed a fourth rule (a new test joins an existing suite). It is not in this PR: it waits for directory suites in xtask and for timings (#919 research, Q5).

## Maintainer to confirm

The "fewer than five items" wording of the crate-edge clause is as proposed in the #919 research. Its exact wording is the maintainer's to confirm on this PR.

## How tested

Docs and process only. No code changed, so no test was run for the change. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --dry-run` plans "nothing in crates/ changed: no tests to run". `git diff --stat`: 5 files (AGENTS.md, PR-reviewer.md, work-issue SKILL.md, PROCESS_VERSION, the decision file).

## Not exercised

No review by a second agent yet; the rules' effect on future PR reviews is untested.

## Process

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (PROCESS_VERSION 16 at the fork point). PR #963 also bumps PROCESS_VERSION to 17; whichever PR merges second takes 18 when it merges main.

On merge, announce on #681: `PROCESS_VERSION 17` · PR #<this PR> · AGENTS.md test-placement / crate-dependency / app-scope rules · forks: normal process sync.

Fixes #920

title: feat(turning): surface speed and feed per rev for lathe tools, G96 under a clamp
body:
## What changed

Lathe tools now have their own cutting-data model: surface speed (Vc) and feed per rev, with a max-rpm clamp. Turning ops suggest S/F from it and post G96 under that clamp.

- **Turning table** (`crates/tools/src/turning_data.rs`, new): Vc (m/min) and f (mm/rev) ranges for each work material, for HSS and carbide. These are our own conservative starting values, inside the ranges that Machinery's Handbook-style turning tables print (provenance comment). Grooving blades and form gauges take 0.4 x the feed. Boring bars take 0.8 x both Vc and feed.
- **`Tool::turning: Option<TurningData>`** `{ vc, feed_per_rev, max_rpm }`. It is checked by `Tool::is_sane`: values must be finite and in bounds, and the tool's constant rpm must not be above its own clamp. The project file and catalog key `turning` is additive and only written when stated, so old project and tool files load unchanged (pinned).
- **Suggestion** (`crates/app/src/cutting_turn.rs`, new, plus `cutting::suggest` handing off to it):
  - Covers every turning op except Threading, which keeps a constant rpm for the synchronized pass.
  - Vc and f/rev are the window middles.
  - The rpm is read at the stock's swing diameter about the spindle axis (program Z through the WCS origin, the lathe posts' meridian law). It is held to the tool's max rpm, then the machine's spindle max. If it falls under the machine's minimum the suggestion is refused, not raised.
  - Feed = f x rpm and plunge = f/2 x rpm (mm/min, not rounded), so the post's `F = feed / rpm` is exactly the table's f/rev.
- **`ApplyCuttingData`** writes the op's feed and plunge, and the tool's rpm and turning data, as one undo unit. The tool's own clamp is kept. This uses the existing `EditOperationParams` + `ChangeTool` composite, so there is no new command.
- **Posting**:
  - A CSS-eligible op whose tool states turning data puts `PARAM SurfaceSpeed <Vc>` on the stream, and also `PARAM MaxSpindleSpeed <rpm>` when the tool states a clamp (`post::Dump::css`).
  - `fanuc-lathe.cps` writes `G50 S<min(machine, tool)>` before the G96 when that clamp is not already in force. Before a later G97 section it lifts the clamp back to the machine's.
  - `tormach-lathe.cps` writes `G96 D<min(machine, tool)>`.
  - **Both posts now refuse, by name, a G96 when neither the machine nor the tool states a maximum rpm.** Before this PR, Tormach posted a G96 with no D and Fanuc posted one with no G50.
  - Tools without turning data post byte-identically (G97).
- **UI**:
  - New tool-editor rows (`tool_turning_row.rs`) for lathe steels: state turning data, Vc (m/min, or ft/min in an inch document), f/rev, and max rpm. The values ride the existing `ChangeTool` Apply.
  - The Feeds page readout shows "Vc · f/rev at Ø D" for a turning suggestion.

title: feat(post)!: the document's unit is the unit every post writes the program in
body:
Stacked on #961 (branch `issue/869-coolant-air`). Retarget/merge after #961.
Fork synced at v0.17.0.

## What changed

The document's Units choice (`SetUnits`, already undoable and saved as `units`) is now also the unit every post writes the program in. One setting: the machine file's `units.length` no longer chooses anything; it only says what unit the file's own numbers are in.

- **Seam.** The app adds `Units: "mm" | "inch"` to `postOptions` on every post path (whole program, per-operation files, per-mount files) via `posting::program_options`. The stream stays mm. `post.exe` takes `--units mm|inch`.
- **Manifest law (`post::units`).** A script that can write inch declares `programUnits = "mm inch"`. An inch document on a script that doesn't is refused by name before any hook runs. This includes a user's own pre-#902 script. An unknown unit word is refused too.
- **Posts that write inch:** Fanuc, Haas, Mazak and Doosan DNM (G20), and Siemens 840D (G700, the G710 twin). Lengths are written / 25.4 at four decimals and feeds in in/min at two. Angles, seconds and rpm are unchanged. The macro probe checks' band is one output step. The three Tormach posts now take the unit from the document instead of `machine.units`.
- **Posts that refuse inch by name:** Makera Carvera (its firmware is mm only), Heidenhain (#976) and Fanuc Lathe (#977). For Heidenhain and Fanuc Lathe, inch output needs verified dialect work, not a guess.
- **Old projects post byte-identical.** `PROJECT_VERSION` is now 59. A file at v58 or older opens on the unit its programs used to post in, taken from its machine files. If that differs from its saved display unit, a load note explains the change. A file whose setups posted in mixed units keeps its display unit, and a note names each setup whose unit changes.
- **UI.** The Post section (document/setup Post page) gets a "Program units" mm / inch row. It is the same `SetUnits` as the Stock page's Units row, now shared code. The post status line names the unit.
- **MCP.** New `set_units` tool (one undo step). `get_job` reports `units`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (the `Units` word, the `programUnits` manifest). Decisions: `docs/decisions/902-document-units.md`.

**Behaviour change / breaking:** a new document on an inch machine file now posts mm until the document is set to inch. This covers every shipped Tormach machine. Older builds refuse v59 project files.

## How tested

Pinning tests (new):
- `crates/app/tests/program_units.rs`
  - `every_inch_post_writes_the_mm_program_in_inches`: 6 posts × 8 mill goldens. Each inch program is checked word by word against the same post's mm program: the unit word swaps, lengths are / 25.4, feeds are / 25.4, and every other word is equal. The unit word comes before the first motion. `Units: "mm"` is byte-identical to no unit at all. Inch goldens are committed under `golden/nc/inch/<post>/` (contour_plate_with_hole, drill_peck).
  - `a_post_that_cannot_write_inch_refuses_the_document_by_name` (Carvera, Heidenhain, Fanuc Lathe)
  - `a_script_that_declares_no_units_refuses_inch_and_posts_mm`
  - `no_shipped_post_takes_the_program_unit_from_the_machine_file`
  - `an_inch_machine_file_no_longer_makes_an_inch_program`
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_units.rs::the_document_unit_is_the_posted_unit_through_undo_and_save` covers the end-to-end path over MCP: a Fanuc face job posts G21; `set_units` inch posts G20 with X / 25.4; Carvera refuses by name; save and reopen keep inch; undo gives back the identical mm program. Also `set_units_refuses_nonsense_and_no_ops`.
- `crates/app/tests/units_migrate.rs` (5 tests): the v58 → v59 rung in four cases (inch machine, inch display on a metric machine, matching display, mixed-unit setups), plus a v59 file that keeps its unit whatever the machine.
- `crates/post/src/post/units.rs` unit tests (unit word, manifest law).
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/program_units.rs::the_post_page_sets_the_program_unit_through_set_units`

Updated: the Tormach, plasma, microARC, probe and Carvera suites. Before this change, several of them used "an inch machine file" to mean "an inch program". Each now states an inch document instead: `SetUnits` in world tests, `Units` in engine tests. Their goldens are unchanged. `carvera_post::an_inch_machine_is_refused_by_name` became `an_inch_document_is_refused_by_name`. It now also pins that an inch machine file alone still posts G21.

**Goldens:** no existing golden moved; the mm output is byte-identical (conformance and every post suite green). New: 12 inch goldens under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/`.

Gate (Linux): `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/869-coolant-air` green: post, app (every app suite, since a shared test helper changed) and ui suites, 10.2 min, 0 failed. `.cps` changes are not gate-mapped (#923), but the whole app set ran, which covers every post suite (conformance, the per-post suites, post_unit_word). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

- No hand test on a real control in inch.
- Sinumerik G700 rests on the published G710/G700 pairing. It has not been run on an 840D.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool table (`.claude/skills/`, a process file) is not updated with `set_units`. That needs a PROCESS_VERSION bump, so it is left for the maintainer.
