title: fix(post): refuse a C-turning rapid when the machine states no C rate
body:
**Stacked on #964** (issue #906, branch `issue/906-c-unwind-rate-cap`). This PR is based on `main` because GitHub cannot base a cross-repo PR on a fork branch, so until #964 merges its diff also shows #964's two commits (`b21879ac`, `d1e1245a`). This PR's own commit is the last one; review it alone with its commit view. Merge #964 first.

## What changed

- `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`liveMove`): #964 refused a C-turning rapid in a C section when the machine states a C travel but no C rate. This PR drops the travel condition. A C-turning rapid on a machine that states **no C rate** is now refused by name whether a C travel is stated or not. The text names what is missing: "a C-axis rapid that turns C, but the machine file states no C rate - its feed would be uncapped; state the C axis's speeds". When a travel is stated it still reads "a C travel but no C rate", so #964's pinned text holds. Cut moves are unchanged, because their F is the planned feed along the part-frame chord.
- `crates/app/tests/c_axis_live.rs`: the `c_axis_live` bench (a test fixture, not a builder's data) now states a C rate: feed 6000 and rapid 12000 deg/min, the same figures as the shipped `millturn.mch`. Before this, its contour test posted C-turning link rapids on that bench at exactly the uncapped F this issue is about. The new test covers the no-rate case on an `unrated` copy of the same bench.
- `docs/decisions/966-lathe-c-no-rate.md`: why I chose a refusal over a no-F form (G00 with C follows no verified path; a G01 without F inherits an unrelated modal feed), why there is no generation gate, and why the bench changed.

## Readings

On the old bench (no C travel, no C rate), `a_rotary_contour_on_the_spindle_states_c_on_every_move_and_posts` posted its C-turning link rapids with no cap. With the fix and the old bench, that test fails with the new refusal, which confirms that the bench's contour did reach the uncapped branch. With the bench stating 6000 deg/min, every X Z C G01 of that program reads back inside 4000 mm/min linear and 6000 deg/min C.

## Pinning tests

- `c_axis_live::a_c_turning_rapid_without_a_stated_c_rate_is_refused_by_name` generates the bench's Rotary Contour and checks that it really does link by C-turning rapids. Posted through `fanuc-lathe.cps` on the bench with no C travel and no C rate, it is refused by name. On the rated bench it posts clean, and every F is checked against the stated linear and C rates.
- #964's `c_axis_unwind::the_lathe_post_refuses_a_c_turning_rapid_without_a_stated_c_rate` and `rotary_gate::a_rewind_without_a_stated_c_rate_is_refused_by_name` still pass unchanged.

## Moved goldens

None. `tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/c_axis_helix.nc` is unchanged: its rapids turn no C, and its cuts run well under 6000 deg/min. `c_axis_unwind`'s two-rings golden is unchanged too.

## Gates

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 1.8 min (app lib + `c_axis_fixture`, `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_unwind`); `cargo xtask gate test a_c_turning_rapid_without_a_stated_c_rate_is_refused_by_name --crate camcraft-app --binary c_axis_live` green; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test c_axis_live -- -D warnings` clean
- Extra suites: `lathe_post` 7, `lathe_post_refusals` 6, `lathe_post_g76` 8, `lathe_spindle_law` 8, `posting` 17, `golden_cl` 25, `conformance` 6, `program_entry` 9, `coolant_followups` 7 - all pass

## Not exercised

- The GUI and MCP paths. They post through the same engine and `.cps`, and no command or MCP surface changed.
- The release-tier heavy lanes.
- Other lathe posts (`tormach-lathe` and the rest) do not declare `liveTooling`. The engine refuses C sections for them, so they cannot reach this case.

Changelog: The Fanuc lathe post refuses by name a C-axis rapid that turns C on a machine that states no C rate, whether or not it states a C travel, instead of posting it at an uncapped feed (#966)

title: fix(sim): judge an upright tool within a stated tilt tolerance
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/upright.rs`: one predicate, `is_upright`, with one named tolerance `UPRIGHT_TILT_RAD = 1e-9` rad (~5.7e-8 deg). A pose within it is judged exactly as a vertical move (the prismatic branch, bit for bit); above it, downward, sideways, zero or non-finite reads tilted (the enclosing reading).
- Every verify law that branched on the exact `camcraft_cl::is_vertical` now reads `is_upright`: reach (c) and its mid-turn sweep (c3), fixture bands/rapids (c2)/(d2), posed steel, mesh steel, solid law, posed contact, posed-rapid second reading, all-air verdict.
- `camcraft_cl::is_vertical` itself stays exact, so CL dumps, posted G-code and goldens do not move.
- Law (c) no longer reports the same `ShankHit` twice for one move when both band groups (shank and holder) convict with the same verdict.
- Why 1e-9 rad is safe: at that tilt a 1 m stack moves 1e-6 mm sideways and a 100 mm holder disc dips 1e-7 mm, four orders below a 0.01 mm gouge tolerance. #938's 1e-10 deg (1.7e-12 rad) is three orders inside; a commanded 0.001 deg is four orders outside. The reasoning and the options I dropped are in `docs/decisions/938-tilt-tolerance.md`.

## How tested
- New `crates/sim/tests/tilt_tolerance.rs` (5 tests; 4 fail on upstream/main without the fix):
  - `a_wide_holder_reads_the_same_upright_and_at_a_rounding_error_of_tilt`: no pose, [0,0,1] and 1e-10 deg give the same clean verdict (before the fix, 1e-10 deg gave two false ShankHits).
  - `a_tilt_just_above_the_tolerance_is_still_judged_tilted`: 1.01e-9 rad and 0.001 deg still convict.
  - `a_noise_tilt_keeps_the_upright_conviction_exactly`
  - `a_leaning_shank_and_holder_report_one_shank_hit_per_move`
  - `the_fixture_band_law_reads_noise_as_upright_and_a_real_tilt_as_tilted` (law c2)
- Unit test `verify::upright::tests::rounding_noise_is_upright_and_a_real_tilt_is_not`, covering both sides plus down, sideways, zero, NaN and inf.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (sim, motion and app suites from the gate map). Also `posed_fixture` and `stock_posed` pass, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.
- One existing expectation changed: `tool_body_bands::a_raised_foot_over_a_fat_shank_is_judged_stricter_than_the_cylinder` had pinned the duplicate `[ShankHit{1,true}, ShankHit{1,true}]`. It now expects a single report. The conviction is the same. No goldens or snapshots moved.

## Not exercised
- Batch and release tiers were not run, so the heavy `--ignored` lanes did not run.
- `stock_sim` and the motion generators keep their exact upright tests (they shape geometry, not verdicts). I left them alone on purpose; see the decision file.

Changelog: The verifier treats a tool tilted by rounding noise (up to 1e-9 rad) as upright, so a holder wider than the cutter no longer raises a false collision on float noise, and a move reports a shank/holder hit once (#938)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #938

title: fix(sim): read XZ / YZ arcs on their XY footprint in Boundary gouge law
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed

Law (b)'s whole-move wall reading in Boundary mode (#43, XY arcs since #905) now covers XZ / YZ (G18 / G19) arcs too. Before, such an arc answered only at the union of its chord joints (#839).

- New `crates/sim/src/verify/arc_wall_plane.rs` gives a vertical arc's XY footprint:
  - **Planar** arc (normal coordinate equal at both ends): one exact segment along X (G18) or Y (G19), from the least to the greatest value the in-plane coordinate takes over the sweep. That is the endpoints, or `c +- r` where the sweep passes the coordinate's turn, read at the radius band's outer edge (`ARC_PAD`). It is read by the straight-move branch.
  - **Helical** arc: a polyline of at most `MAX_ARC_CHORDS` pieces (sagitta 1e-4 mm), each piece read `r d^2 / 8` plus the band width nearer than it stands, so it never reads farther than the truth.
  - Degenerate arcs (zero radius or sweep) read as the straight move, which is how `cl::arc_chords` cuts them. A non-finite centre or coordinate fails closed (`Trace::Unread`, a gouge). Nothing panics, and every loop is bounded.
- `arc_wall.rs`: `Trace::of` always returns a trace, and the new `Trace::Poly` variant is added. `XyArc::dist_seg` uses a fixed 4-slot buffer instead of a `Vec` per edge (review note on #942).
- `section.rs`: the wall reading runs for every non-rapid move in Boundary mode. Docs are updated.
- `crates/app/tests/boundary_arc_walls.rs` moves to `crates/sim/tests/` because it uses only `verify` re-exports (#921). It is unchanged apart from the crate path.

**Answer to the issue's P1 argument (it does not hold).** The footprint is a line, but the joints stand up to a chord length apart on it. On an r 200 arc at the 0.01 mm verdict tolerance, the pinned arc's joints (the union of both chord sets) are 1.92 mm apart in XY. A wall vertex 3.90 mm off the footprint, which is 90 um past a 4 mm cutter's 3.99 mm floor, read >= 4.016 mm from every joint, so the gouge passed. That is a real miss, and this PR fixes it.

## How tested

- `crates/sim/tests/boundary_arc_planes.rs` (new):
  - `a_vertex_between_a_vertical_arcs_joints_past_the_floor_is_a_gouge`: G18 and G19 arcs, planar and helical (rise 0.2), cut both ways. The vertex is on both sides of the footprint at 3.90 / 3.5 / 3.8 / 3.98 mm. The test asserts that the joints read it clear (>= floor) and that the verdict is `Gouge`. **It fails without the fix**: I checked by stubbing the new trace to read nothing, which got `left: []`.
  - `the_same_vertex_clear_of_the_floor_stays_clean`: the same cases at 3.995 / 4.0 / 4.5 mm (planar) and 4.0 / 4.5 / 6.0 mm (helical) give no warning. This checks for false refusals.
  - `a_model_corner_between_a_vertical_arcs_joints_is_judged`: a model-backed pin. A 45-degree block corner gives a gouge at 3.90 mm and is clean at 4.5 mm. title: fix(post): refuse a C rewind when the machine states a C travel but no C rate
body:
## What changed

A machine file whose rotary C states a travel but no rate (neither its feed nor its rapid, deg/min) had nothing to cap the C rewind orbit of #860 by. The lathe post scaled the machine's max linear feed by the C turn, about 57 x fmax / r (the F22954 of the #860 review, note 1). It now refuses by name, in two layers:

- **Generation** (`crates/app/src/operation/rotary_gate.rs`): when `unwind_c` inserts a rewind orbit (the path grows) and the machine's C states no rate, Rotary Contour is refused: "the path needs a C rewind, but the machine file states a C travel but no C rate - a rewind would post at an uncapped feed; state the C axis's feed or rapid rate". A shift of the opening stretch adds no move (the section's first G00 C positions it, at no F), so it is not refused. A path that fits the travel as stamped is not refused.
- **Lathe post** (`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`, `liveMove`): when the machine states a C travel and no C rate, a C-section rapid that turns C is refused ("a C-axis rapid that turns C, but the machine file states a C travel but no C rate - its feed would be uncapped; state the C axis's speeds"). This is the backstop for a stream that bypasses the gate, and it also covers C-turning link rapids that are not orbits, which had the same unbounded F. Cut moves are unchanged: they post at the planned feed.

Decision (named refusal over a stated default rate): `docs/decisions/906-c-unwind-rate-cap.md`.

## Readings

- A machine with C travel and no rate, Rotary Contour on the c_axis_unwind bar: refused at generation by name. The same machine with a travel wide enough for no rewind: generates.
- The unwound two-ring path posted on that machine: the lathe post refuses by name. The same path on the rated bench posts with no warnings (golden unchanged).

## Pinning tests

- `c_axis_unwind::a_stated_c_travel_without_a_c_rate_refuses_the_rewind_by_name` (generation, end to end through `operation::generate`)
- `c_axis_unwind::the_lathe_post_refuses_a_c_turning_rapid_without_a_stated_c_rate` (through the lathe post)
- `operation::rotary_gate::tests::a_rewind_without_a_stated_c_rate_is_refused_by_name` (gate unit: refused unrated, unwinds rated)

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (app lib, c_axis_fixture, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind). The first run failed on my own new unit test's fixture (its link chord crossed the spindle line); the fixture was fixed, second run green.
- Also run: app `lathe_post` 7/7, `lathe_post_refusals` 6/6, `posting` 17/17, `golden_cl` 25/25.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No NC golden, CL golden or snapshot PNG moved.

## Not exercised

- A machine that states no C travel and no C rate still posts C-turning rapids uncapped (the `c_axis_live` bench). That predates #860 and is outside this issue; noted in the decision file.
- `fanuc.cps` / `doosan-dnm.cps` carry no C-rate cap at all (already a known follow-up from #860).
- Batch and release tiers, ui suites, GUI.

Changelog: A machine file that states a C travel but no C rate now refuses the C rewind (and any C-turning rapid in the lathe post) by name, instead of posting an uncapped feed.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at v0.17.0.

Fixes #906

title: feat(post)!: Air coolant mode, machine default coolant, editor keeps coolant codes
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed

From the Makera Z1 user report: an Air M7 added in the machine editor was "ignored on save", the Carvera post emitted M8 from the seeded Flood, and an operation could not ask for air.

- **Air coolant mode.** `CoolantMode::Air` ("Air" in the op page's Coolant picker, `PARAM Coolant air` in the stream, `"air"` in project files). `COOLANT_KINDS` (the mounted-machine editor's pick list) gains `Air`.
- **Every post that reads the ask handles Air.** Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Haas, Siemens 840D, Heidenhain, Mazak, Doosan DNM and Tormach Lathe resolve `air` from the machine's `Air` / `Air blast` entry, or refuse it by name ("operation X: the machine states no air coolant code ..."). Tormach Plasma already refuses every ask but Off. The Tormach mill post does not read the ask, so the engine's existing `coolantModes` refusal covers it.
- **`carvera.cps` posts the coolant the op asked for.** It used to take "first Flood, else first coded entry", which posted M8 when the seeded Flood was kept. It now declares `coolantModes`. Air takes the `Air` entry. Flood takes the `Flood` entry, failing one a shop's own coded name. A missing match is a named refusal, never a wrong M-code.
- **The machine's default coolant.** `CoolantMode::machine_default(coolants)` is Flood when the machine can post a flood ask, otherwise the first coded entry's mode. `CreateOperation` starts each new op on its setup's machine's default. On the shipped Carvera (Air M7 only), a new op is Air and posts M7 / M9.
- **The machine file editor keeps the coolant.** "Add coolant" takes the name and the M code together and refuses an empty code by name. Each coolant row has a "Remove <coolant>" button, the seeded Flood included. A codeless coolant is a draft refusal that blocks Save and Save As. `save()` now checks the refusals itself, as `save_as()` already did.
- **`tormach.cps` flood law aligned** with the generic posts. On an Air-only (or Mist-only) list it refuses a flood op by name instead of posting the first coded entry (M7).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/869-coolant-air.md`.

**Behaviour change (heads-up for the release notes):** an op saved before this change on an Air-only Carvera is still Flood (the old default). It now gets a named refusal telling the user to pick Air, where it used to post M7. New ops on that machine start on Air. A generic post on a machine whose only coolant is named "Air" refuses a Flood op the same way; before, it treated "Air" as the shop's own flood.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/coolant_air.rs` (new)
  - `an_air_only_carvera_starts_a_default_op_on_air_and_posts_m7_m9`: the shipped Carvera, a default op is Air, posts one M7 and one M9, no M8, no warnings.
  - `an_air_op_posts_the_air_code_not_the_seeded_flood`: Flood M8 + Air M7 on every generic post and the Carvera. The default op is Flood. An Air op posts M7 and never M8. `air_blast` reads as Air.
  - `an_ask_the_machine_lacks_is_refused_by_name`: Air on a flood/mist machine is refused by name on every post. Flood on the Air-only Carvera is refused by name. The Tormach mill post refuses an Air op, and a Flood op on an Air-only list never posts M7.
  - `the_machine_default_coolant_reads_the_coded_list`
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/machines_edit.rs::a_blank_mill_swaps_its_flood_for_air_m7_and_keeps_it_through_save_and_reload`: through the real shell, a name-only add is refused by name; Air M7 is added; the seeded Flood is removed; Save As writes the file, which reads back as `[Air M7]` with an Air default.
- Updated: `machine_edit::a_coolant_code_must_be_a_well_formed_m_word` (an empty code is now refused by name), `coolant_followups::machine_coolant_names_read_through_spelling_variants` (`COOLANT_KINDS` pin), and `carvera_post` (the two-tool pocket stream asks `PARAM Coolant air`).

Gate (Linux): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green (post, app and ui suites; the ui lib holds the new editor test). The gate map does not pick the post-script suites for a `.cps` change, so these also ran green: 44 app suites touching coolant / posts / machines (`coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `coolant_air`, `carvera_post`, `carvera_machines`, `fanuc_post`, `doosan_dnm_post`, `lathe_post*`, `posting`, `conformance`, `smoothing`, `project_roundtrip`, `machine`, `machine_library`, the drilling / probe / mill2d suites, and others). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. First quick run failed on the new UI test: the old one-line "New coolant ... Add coolant" row was clipped in a narrow pane, so the click never landed. The add controls now sit on their own grid rows, and the removes are in a wrapped row.

**Goldens:** none moved. `nc/carvera/two_tool_pocket.nc` is byte-identical: its stream now asks for air, and still posts M7 / M9.

## Not exercised

- The mounted-machine editor window (Setup pane) beyond `COOLANT_KINDS` now listing Air; its "add coolant" still adds a codeless Flood row there (it only applies to the mounted machine, never writes a file).
- Hand test on a real Carvera / Z1.
- No MCP tool sets an op's coolant today (not added by this PR: it adds no command; `EditOperationParams::with_coolant` predates it). Follow-up filed: #954 ("MCP: set an operation's coolant", P1, effort:medium).

Changelog: Coolant: an operation can ask for Air (M7 air blast), resolved from the machine's list or refused by name; a new op starts on its machine's default coolant (Air on the Carvera); the Carvera post posts the op's coolant instead of the first Flood; the machine file editor adds a coolant with its code, can remove the seeded Flood, and never saves a codeless coolant.

Commit type: `feat(post)!` (the BREAKING CHANGE footer covers the Air-only Carvera Flood refusal; under 0.x it bumps MINOR like any feat).

title: feat(mcp): rename_operation and reorder_operation (closes #45)
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed

#45's GUI scope had already landed in earlier PRs: rename, saved order and drag and drop within a setup (PR #58, v0.12.0), the Setups ribbon cell and the always-present Setups browser row (#322, `fb957ec`), and each setup's operations grouped under its own browser node (#343). What was still owed was the agent surface: `RenameOperation` and `ReorderOperation` had no MCP tool (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool"). This PR adds them, which closes #45.

- `crates/app/src/mcp/order_tools.rs` (new):
  - `rename_operation {name, new_name}`: changes the display name only. The stable key and the program position stay the same, and renaming back to the key clears the label.
  - `reorder_operation {name, target, place: "before"|"after"}`: the drag and drop's own model. It moves an operation next to another one in the same setup, refuses a move to another setup, and answers with that setup's new order.
  - Both resolve operations by key or display name (`edit::find_op`) and run the existing undoable commands through the session History, so each is one undo step. Every construction-time refusal (a taken name, shadowing another op's key, another setup, already in place) comes back as a tool error.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/{mod,tools}.rs`: the module is registered and its table is chained into `tools::all()`.
- `docs/decisions/45-op-order-mcp.md`: the shape choices and what was dropped.

Posting, simulation and rest-machining order semantics do not change. The tools write the same `OperationMeta.order` the browser drag writes, and `setup::operation_order` still ranks setups first. There are no project-file or post-output changes.

## How tested

Pinning tests in the new binary `crates/app/tests/mcp_order.rs`:
- `rename_and_reorder_are_listed_with_their_schemas`
- `reorder_moves_within_its_setup_one_undo_step_and_refuses_another_setup`: two setups. A move within Setup1 keeps Setup2's op last, each move is one undo/redo step, and a cross-setup move, a no-op, a bad `place` and an unknown name are each refused with the order left as it was.
- `rename_keeps_the_key_and_the_order_and_round_trips`: the key and order are unchanged, other tools find the op by its new name, a duplicate label, another op's key and a blank name are refused, save -> open in a fresh session keeps the label and order, and undo restores the key as the name.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green - 19 app suites + lib (all `app::mcp` gate-mapped suites incl. the new `mcp_order`), 0 failed, 0.4 min; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test mcp_order -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- Pause / Home program entries (#155) can't be addressed by these tools, because the MCP surface does not expose entries yet.
- The camcraft-mcp skill's tool table is not updated. It is a process file and would bump PROCESS_VERSION in a feature PR; its SKILL.md names `tools::list()` as the live registry.
- No GUI change, so there are no UI or snapshot changes.

Changelog: MCP gains `rename_operation` and `reorder_operation`: rename an operation's display name and move it within its setup, each one undo step, over the same commands as the browser (#45)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #45

title: fix(sim): judge and draw a necked tool at its drawn neck
body:
## What changed

A necked tool was judged as its full shank cylinder by every stack law, so reach and fixture checks refused or warned about cuts the real tool makes. The drawn cutter outline (`ToolCutter`, #93 slice 2) now feeds the shank band of the stack laws and the simulated tool, **only where it is narrower than the stated shank, never wider**.

- **tools**: new `neck` module. `neck::neck_bands(tool, spun)` reads the outline's own conservative bands (`SpunProfile::bands`) over the shank span (flute top to stickout). Each band is capped at the stated shank radius, any gap is filled at that radius, and the bands are merged to `MAX_BANDS` (merging only grows a band). The result is empty when the outline no longer `agrees` with the numbers or narrows nowhere. `HolderStack` gains a `neck` field. `HolderStack::shank_bands(g)` returns the exact old `(flute_len, shank_len, shank_radius)` band unless a neck fits `g`: contiguous, finite, never wider than the shank, at most `MAX_BANDS` bands. Each neck band is widened to any holder-body band beside it.
- **sim**: the shank band in laws c/c3 (`reach`), c2 (`laws`), d2 (`stack_span::upper_bands`), the posed sweep (`posed_steel`), the mesh law (`mesh_steel::steel_stack`) and the solid law's atoms (`Cutter::atoms`) now comes from `shank_bands`. `Cutter` carries the neck as `NeckBands` (fixed capacity, so it stays `Copy`). `Cutter::judged` drops a neck that no longer fits the geometry.
- **app**: `tool_cutter::neck_of` computes the neck against the stored tool record. It feeds `tool_body::stack(..).with_neck(..)` at the three existing seams: generation (`GenJob.neck`), the post gate's `fixture_struck::op_hits`, and `sim_tool_body::for_operation`. The simulation's cutter meridian is drawn from those same bands. A drawn neck now enters the op stamp (`tool_cutter::digest`, which writes bytes only when a neck exists, so no other stamp moves). The doc comments and the MCP `set_tool_cutter_profile` description no longer call the drawn cutter "display only".

## Readings and safety

- A tool with no drawn cutter, or a drawn cutter with no neck, judges and draws bit-identically: the very same band tuple is produced.
- If a neck is absent, fails `agrees`, or is degenerate, the stated cylinder is used. The tool is never judged narrower than its drawn outline or a body standing beside the shank.
- Drill reach (`operation::drill_reach`, which reads the holder face, not the shank radius), the probe stylus (`probe_op::stylus_cutter`, its own single body band) and multi-axis tilt avoidance (`motion::multiaxis::avoid`, generator side) do not share this seam. They stay on the stated cylinder, which is conservative, and are left to #842.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/tool_neck_laws.rs` (new):
  - `a_necked_tool_clears_steel_its_shank_cylinder_strikes`: post gate fixture law, Ø8 neck vs Ø10 shank, 4.5 mm off; undo brings the strike back.
  - `a_drawn_cutter_with_no_neck_judges_bit_identically`: fixture verdicts and sim outline unchanged.
  - `the_reach_laws_cutter_carries_the_neck_and_no_neck_reads_the_cylinder`: `Cutter` used by laws c/c3 and the solid law; a misfitting neck is dropped.
  - `the_simulation_draws_the_neck`
- `crates/tools/src/neck_tests.rs` (new, 6 unit tests): neck bands, catalog tools carry no neck, a disagreeing outline is dropped, cylinder bit-for-bit, misfits fall back, a body beside the neck widens it.
- `tool_cutter_profile::a_drawn_cutter_lands_undoes_and_moves_the_stamp_only_by_its_neck`: renamed and updated. A drawn neck now moves the stamp; a drawn cutter with no neck still does not.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): green - tools, sim, motion, app and ui suites all ok (13.9 min wall); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No end-to-end generation test in which law (c) against rest material acquits a deep necked cut. The reach law reads the `Cutter` seam, which is pinned directly.
- No UI snapshot changes. The tool editor already draws the drawn outline; the simulation mesh change is covered structurally by `the_simulation_draws_the_neck`.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/852-necked-tool-envelope.md`.

Changelog: The collision/reach checks and the simulated tool now read a tool's drawn neck where it is narrower than the stated shank, so a necked tool is no longer refused for steel its neck clears (no drawn neck: unchanged).

Effort: high (no escalation). Fork synced at v0.17.0.

Fixes #852

title: fix(motion): adaptive growth overload fallback compares whole revolutions
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed

`Planner::step_search` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/grow.rs`): when no growth step holds the load, the fallback used to pick the least overload from the tries' readings. Those readings stop at the first point past the bound (`walk_until`). Where the overload comes before the step-dependent front, every try reads the same, the first and largest step wins the tie, and that step is then walked whole far past the reading it was picked on (#7 round 10, island NE corner: picked at 59.5 deg, cut at 125 deg).

Now the fallback keeps each overloaded try's ring and revolution, but drops its partial stock. `least_whole` walks each revolution whole again from the planner's stock, largest step first. A smaller step replaces the kept one only when its whole reading is more than 2 % lower (`SLACK`, the tie tolerance the old fallback already used). Each re-walk stops early once it can no longer win. The kept revolution reuses the stock and reading from its whole walk, so it is not walked a third time.

**#13 growth budget:** the re-walks are not charged as growth work, and `WORK_MAX`, `GEOM_MAX` and `GEOM_LEN` are unchanged. Each trial already charges its revolution's whole length (`add_len`) before its walk is cut short. The re-walk adds no new revolution and rebuilds no geometry: it reads revolutions already paid for in full, at most once each and usually only part way. The held fix e4039ef0 called the trial again instead, which rebuilt the offsets and charged length and vertices a second time; that is part of why its island run reached 61,971 r. The full reasoning is in `docs/decisions/845-adaptive-overload-fallback.md`.

## Readings

Release `hsm_one` over all six `adaptive_hsm` fixtures, run with this fix and with upstream's `grow.rs`:

| fixture | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| bore R12.5, rectangle 60x40, L-pocket, narrow slot 14x60, channel 22x60 | - | identical report lines (max deg, breaks, cut/air lengths, move counts, notes) |
| island 60x40, 12x12 | HSM refused by law 3 after 109 revolutions (~600.0 k vertices, ~9.4 k r); Offset rings | HSM refused by law 3 after 118 revolutions (~606.4 k vertices, ~9.5 k r); Offset rings - identical posted path |

On the island, the smaller steps now kept in the overloaded corners mean more revolutions before the existing geometry law refuses the plan (118 instead of 109). The refusal and the Offset-rings path it falls back to do not change. No other fixture's output moves.

**Goldens moved: none.** No committed CL/NC golden comes from the adaptive planner (`crates/app/tests/golden/` has no HSM/adaptive file), and no snapshot PNG is touched.

## How tested

- Pinning test: `machining2d::adaptive::grow::tests::the_overload_fallback_keeps_the_least_whole_reading_not_a_truncated_tie` (camcraft-motion lib). Two overloaded revolutions share a 3 mm side-cut start past the bound. Walked to the bound, their readings are exactly equal (the old tie, which the larger step won). Walked whole, the larger step turns into fresh stock and reads much more, so the test asserts the smaller step is kept with its whole reading. Plus `a_near_tie_keeps_the_larger_step_and_nothing_tried_keeps_nothing`.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: motion lib + adaptive_band + adaptive_hsm + pocket3d_hsm, all green (33 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Release heavy lanes: `adaptive_hsm --ignored` (full-resolution report, island refused in seconds, channel trochoid fallback, small-helix rectangle) and the lib's `budget::fixtures::the_fixtures_that_grow_today_stay_under_the_geometry_budget`: green.
- Debug camcraft-app adaptive suites (pocket3d_hsm, roughing2d, shoulder_adaptive, pocket_overhead, whole_model_pocket): all green (18 passed; 1 was already ignored).

## Not exercised

- The island fixture with the budget lifted (the issue's evidence run): the island is still refused by law 3 before its NE corner is grown, so the 125 deg corner overload no longer shows up in any posted path on main. The pinning test covers the mechanism directly.
- The batch and release tiers.

Changelog: Adaptive clearing's growth spiral, where no step holds the load, now cuts the step whose whole revolution overloads least, not the largest step on a tie read before the overload (#845)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #845

title: fix(post): cap a feed that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rates
body:
**Changes posted G-code: waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.**

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a). Effort: high (safety floor: posted G-code; no escalation).

## What changed
- **One shared rule** - `crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs` (new, appended to the prelude every `.cps` sees): `rotaryRate(letter)` (stated feed speed, else rapid, deg/min), `rotaryFeedCap(f, lin, turns, mode)`, `rotaryFeed(p, prev, letters, mode, arc)` and `rotaryFeedWord(v)`. It caps F so no rotary runs past its stated rate and no linear part past `feedRateMax`, read the way the control reads F:
  - **path** - `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` under G43.4. F is the tool tip's speed relative to the work, with the rotaries carried along (FANUC 30i-B operator's manual, tool center point control): F <= rate x tip / |d|. With the tip still, F <= the rate.
  - **composite** - `doosan-dnm.cps` on a 4th axis without TCP, and `fanuc-lathe.cps` C-axis live tooling (#860). The control times the block over sqrt(lin^2 + sum d^2), counting degrees as mm (FANUC 0i-F operator's manual, feedrate for rotation axes). `fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove` now calls the shared rule instead of its own copy.
  - **Arcs** that turn a rotary use the path rule over the chord in the arc's plane. That chord is never longer than any reading of an arc's F, so the cap is never too loose.
- A capped F is floored to 0.1 mm/min. A cap under 0.1 mm/min is refused by name.
- The post now tracks the angles the control holds (`rotAt`), taken only from the A/B/C words it actually wrote. If a feed turns a rotary from an angle the post never wrote, and that rotary states a rate, the post refuses it by name: `a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held`. Each rate refusal is counted once per program.
- An unstated rate caps nothing (the unstated-limit law).
- `tormach.cps` needs no cap: it writes A only on a G0 index and refuses an A that changes inside an operation (#785). haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain and carvera refuse every tilted record.
- The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/885-rotary-feed-cap.md`.

## How tested
New pinning suite `crates/app/tests/rotary_feed_cap.rs`. It reads every posted motion block back, keeps the axes modal, and checks every feed block that turns A against the stated rates under that dialect's reading:
- `fanuc_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (pins `A30 F3.3`, `A60 F1000` and the uncapped `A61 F2000`)
- `doosan_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate`
- `doosan_fourth_axis_composite_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (also pins the refusal when no A word was ever written)
- `an_unstated_rate_caps_nothing`
- `a_feed_turning_from_an_unknown_angle_is_refused_by_name`

The lathe stays pinned by `c_axis_unwind::a_lower_stated_rate_posts_a_lower_feed` and its golden, which did not change.

Gate (local, macOS, debug):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all suites green.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` plus the 44 post-touching binaries: all green, 377 tests. The binaries are arc_planes, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind, comment_escape, conformance, control_comp, coolant_followups, doosan_dnm_post, drill_prior, drill_rplane, fanuc_post, fourth_axis_pose, heidenhain_cycles, inverted_equivalence/post/probe, lathe_*, machine_library, plasma_*, post_unit_word, probe_*, program_comments, program_entry, rotary_feed_cap, turning_face_approach, vertical_arc_entry, wear_comp, tilt, rotary_verify, tormach_fourth_axis, microarc_test_part, tormach_machines and posting.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved
**None.** No committed golden states a rotary rate on a tilted feed. The lathe's C-axis goldens (`c_axis_unwind.nc`, `c_axis_helix.nc`) are byte-identical through the shared rule.

## Test fixture changed
`fourth_axis_pose.rs` `tilted()` now opens with a rapid at the pose before its two feeds. Under the new refusal, its feeds would otherwise turn the shipped DNM 5700's rated A from an angle the post never placed. The tests' own assertions are unchanged.

## Not exercised
- No Hub run or machine cut yet.
- G93 inverse time is not implemented (see the decision file).
- Under G43.4 the machine's linear axes also make a compensating move that depends on the pivot length. No machine file states that length, so the control's own per-axis clamp covers it. The post caps the tip at `feedRateMax`.

Found while working this: #950 (P0). doosan-dnm without TCP assumes A0 at program start and after a tool change, so an A0 section after an A30 section posts no A word. This PR does not fix that output. With a rated A, it now refuses such a feed by name.

Changelog: Posts cap the feed of a block that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rotary rate and linear feed (fanuc, doosan-dnm, fanuc-lathe through one shared rule), refusing by name when the starting angle is unknown (#885)

Fixes #885

title: fix(verify): law (b) reads a Boundary-mode arc on its true circle against the walls
body:
#905: outside Area mode, law (b) read an arc move only at its chord joints. A sharp wall or island corner between two joints was never measured against the cutter. The issue's case: a 4 mm cutter on an r 200 arc sweeping 0.048 rad, with the corner midway between joints, passed a 90 um gouge on main (after #839's union of both joint sets).

Fork synced at v0.17.0, PROCESS_VERSION 14; merged with upstream main at bac4d015 (head 8207e79e).

## What changed

- **New `sim::verify::arc_wall`** (`crates/sim/src/verify/arc_wall.rs`): the XY trace of a move (`Trace::Seg`, `Trace::Arc`, `Trace::Unread`) and the exact least distance from a wall edge to an arc.
  - For each piece of the edge inside the arc's wedge, the distance is radial. `|CP|` is convex along a segment, so it is the gap between that piece's radius range and the circle.
  - Outside the wedge, the nearest arc point is an endpoint.
  - The radius is a band, `[min, max]` of the two endpoint radii, widened by `ARC_PAD` (1 um, the centre lattice). The reading is never farther than the truth.
- **`section::tangency`**: in `Mode::Boundary` an XY arc (a helix included) now joins the whole-move wall reading (`wall_gouge`) that straight moves have had since #43. Edge classification is unchanged:
  - section edges are walls;
  - with a model, the probe picks the walls;
  - without one, a move that properly crosses a region edge is over an open rim. For an arc, the crossing is computed on the true circle.

  A straight move keeps the same squared comparison, float for float.
- **Unchanged:** Area mode, which already reads every chord whole. XZ/YZ arcs, whose XY trace is not a circle, keep the joint reading. The #689 joint union also stays, since it still judges the section's containment and the non-wall edges.
- A centre or radius that is not a number fails closed (a gouge). A zero-radius or zero-sweep arc is read as its straight chord, as `cl::arc_chords` cuts it.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/905-arc-corner-gouge.md`.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/boundary_arc_walls.rs`, the issue's Done-means. Each case runs the arc ccw and cw, with the vertex outside and inside the circle.
  - `a_corner_between_an_arcs_joints_past_the_floor_is_a_gouge`: the corner sits midway between the joints at 3.5, 3.8, 3.90 and 3.98 mm (floor 3.99). The test asserts that the joints of both tolerances read the 3.90 corner clear, so the old reading passed it. Every case is now a gouge.
  - `the_same_corner_just_inside_the_floor_stays_clean`: 3.995, 4.0 and 4.5 mm pass.
  - `area_mode_verdicts_on_the_corner_are_unchanged`.
- `sim::verify::arc_wall::tests::the_exact_distance_matches_a_dense_sampling`: 800 random segments against four arcs (ccw and cw, under and over a half turn). The exact distance is never farther than a dense sampling and stays within its spacing.

Checked against the old code: with the arc kept out of the wall reading, `a_corner_between_an_arcs_joints_past_the_floor_is_a_gouge` fails at the 3.90 mm case. With the fix, it passes.

Gates:
- On the final head 8207e79e (after merging upstream main at bac4d015):
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green.
  - The Boundary-mode suites listed below: green.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
  - `headless_bin`: green now that #936 is fixed upstream.

Earlier runs, on the tree before that merge:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (before the clippy respelling): green (sim, motion and app suites, `verify_arc_reading` among them).
- The quick gate's maps don't name the Boundary-mode suites, so these were also run by hand, all green:
  - `boundary_walls`, `wall_arc_entry`, `corner_blend`, `verify`
  - `blind_floor`, `real_tip_contour`, `solid_law`, `solid_law_goldens`, `vertical_arc_entry`
- `cargo xtask gate batch` (24.8 min): this PR's suites are green, but the batch was not green overall. Results by step:
  - geometry, tools, post, sim, motion (slow ones included) and app (center_cut_multiaxis included): green.
  - clippy failed on two `!(x >= y)` NaN guards in `arc_wall.rs`. They were respelled (3ad9b07f), and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is now clean.
  - The first ui run failed to compile on a stale build cache (`ash` rlib missing); a rerun built. Of 17 ui test binaries, 16 pass. The one failure is `theme_files::the_shipped_example_parses` (cell_h 35 -> 40), red on upstream main already (#932). This PR touches no ui code.
  - cl: `headless_bin::cl_bin_prints_move_stats` fails. Upstream main is red there too (#936: #839's golden regeneration made `contour_disc_hole.cl` 33 arcs, the test still expects 30). This PR touches no cl code or golden.
- No snapshot PNG touched.

## Not exercised

- A model-backed Boundary case (a section edge, or a region edge classified as a wall by the probe) has no new test of its own. That classification code is unchanged, and the model-backed suites above pass.
- XZ/YZ arcs are not read on their true trace (unchanged, see above).

Changelog: Gouge check: in Boundary mode (contour, trace, face) an arc move is checked along its whole length against wall corners, not only at sample points, so a gouge between two samples is caught (#905)

Effort: high (the issue's label). Not escalated.

Fixes #905

title: feat(kernel): STEP import through solidcore-step behind the seam, benched against truck
body:
M12.1 stage 4 (#916): a STEP importer on the solidcore side of the kernel seam, and the dual-importer bench against truck-stepio. **Bench only** - `crates/app` still imports STEP through truck; truck and ruststep stay. Everything is inside `crates/kernel`; no other workspace crate gains a dependency.

## What changed

- **Pin.** `crates/kernel` takes `solidcore`, `solidcore-step` and `solidcore-convert` from `https://github.com/NeoTech/solidcore` at `rev = "55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda"` (the fork's tag `camcraft-pin-2026-11-11`) in place of crates.io `solidcore = "=1.0.1"`. `solidcore-ops` and `solidcore-record` come with them; `solidcore-tess` at the same rev is a dev-dependency. `Cargo.lock`: 6 git packages (`solidcore`, `-convert`, `-ops`, `-record`, `-step`, `-tess`) replace the 1 registry package (552 -> 557), no new crates.io package (an earlier version of this text said 5 and 556: counted before the dev-dependency was added). The lock diff touches only those packages and camcraft-kernel's own dependency list.
- **Against 1.0.1** (the pin is 2973 commits past the `solidcore-v1.0.1` tag; the seam's library code compiled unchanged): `Brep` is no longer `Clone` (two test helpers now copy with `brep_copy` or measure in place); the port now refuses a NaN offset distance; the native reader now refuses blank, foreign, noise and header-only files itself. Five pinned port verdicts re-triaged - all were findings against the port, now closed by it.
- **Importer** (`camcraft_kernel::solidcore_step`): `read_step` (every solid item, refused ones with stage and reason, the file's length units, notes) and `import_step` (a model only when every solid item came through). 64 MiB size bound; the caller's `CancelToken` is the time bound (new `KernelError::TimedOut`), polled by the parser, between solids and inside the kernel's loops; panics caught. The stage-3 laws apply unchanged (integrity, closed manifold solid, vertex gap <= 1e-3 mm). A length unit the reader cannot convert is refused by the seam (the reader alone reads it as millimetres, silently).
- **Bench** (`tests/step_agreement.rs`): every `.step` under `testdata/models` through both importers; verdicts pinned; a fixture with no row fails.
- **Corrupt corpus** (`tests/step_import.rs`): 19 files made from box.step through both importers, each under a 60 s bound that cancels the import.

## Readings

| File | Unit (mm) | Importers | solidcore-tess mesh |
|---|---|---|---|
| box.step, empty_list.step (#887), tool_csys_box_iso13399.step | 1 | agree | watertight, within tolerance |
| sample_ap214.step (metre, 3 solids) | 1000 | agree | watertight, within tolerance |
| Milling-test.step, Milling-test-inch.step | 1 / 25.4 | **disagree: bounding box** | watertight, within tolerance |
| tool_csys_none / _iso13399 / _degenerate (no solid) | 1 | both refuse by name | - |

The disagreement: the port's "tight" box of Milling-test is Y -30..30; the part is a disc with a flat at Y = 19.719 (file vertices, truck's mesh and solidcore's own mesh all agree). Volume and area agree to 1.2e-4. solidcore is the wrong side - filed as #939.

Corrupt corpus: no panic, no hang. solidcore refuses 17 of 19 by name and imports 2 that are whole. truck-stepio, as the bench reads it, refuses the 10 that break the Part 21 syntax and answers `Ok` for the other 9, five of them with an open mesh.

Tessellation (point 4): `solidcore-tess` at the app's 0.005 mm chord has 0 open triangle sides on every fixture (truck: 854 on Milling-test, 3196 on sample_ap214) and is closer to the exact volume (5.6e-5 against 1.2e-4 relative on Milling-test), with more triangles (6228 against 952). What a machining mesh still owes is #940.

wasm32 (point 5): `cargo check -p camcraft-kernel --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes.

## How tested

Run in release, `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel --no-fail-fast`: 25 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (heavy lane); the 2 heavy-lane tests also pass with `--ignored`. `cargo clippy --release -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Pinning tests (new): `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name`, `importer_hands_out_closed_forms_and_units`, `corrupt_step_files_never_panic_or_hang`, `importer_keeps_its_size_and_time_bounds`. Re-pinned: `port_degenerate_inputs_never_panic_and_match_pinned_verdicts`, `corrupt_native_files_never_panic_or_hang`.

## Gate results after the first push

**Batch gate on head 10fabe16 merged with an older main** (run by the main session, not by the author): all green except one UI theme test that was red on main itself at the time (fixed on main since); `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel` passed there too (25 passed).

**This round - head ef65c32e, which is 10fabe16 + `git merge origin/main` (e0cb0049, v0.18.0) + a one-line count correction in the decision file.** The merge had no conflict; `Cargo.lock` merged by itself and `cargo metadata --locked` accepts it. Against main's lock, package by package: the registry `solidcore` 1.0.1 is replaced by the git one, five `solidcore-*` git packages are added, and `camcraft-kernel`'s dependency list gains them plus `ruststep` and `truck-stepio` (dev-dependencies, already locked). No other package differs; `flecs_ecs`, `flecs_ecs_sys` and the `ruststep` git source are identical to main's.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel --no-fail-fast` | 25 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (heavy lane) |
| `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel --test agreement -- --ignored` | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo check -p camcraft-kernel --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` | ok |
| `cargo check -p camcraft-app` | ok |

The tests and the checks ran on the merged tree before the count correction was committed; that commit changes only `docs/decisions/916-solidcore-step-bench.md`.

## What was not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate quick` was not run by the author: its plan falls back to the batch tier because `Cargo.lock` changed. The batch tier was run by the main session instead (below). App's and ui's suites were not re-run on the head merged with v0.18.0 main; `cargo check -p camcraft-app` was.
- The largest mesh-to-surface distance is not measured; the mesh is judged on volume, area, box and watertightness (#940).
- No wasm32 test run, only the check; `solidcore-tess` was not checked for wasm32.
- No STEP file larger than 100 KB and no third-party corpus: the fixtures are the repo's nine.
- The time bound cannot stop the reader's topology pass (no hook upstream, #939); it is bounded by caps.

Follow-ups filed: #939 (bounding box and two smaller port findings), #940 (machining mesh). Both gate #917.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/916-solidcore-step-bench.md`. Notices: `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`.

title: fix(sim,app): flag a STEP model imported coarser than promised; tighten its gouge verdicts, refuse past that
body:
Base is `main` (v0.18.0, e0cb0049, merged into this branch). #839, which this was stacked on, has merged.

## What changed

A STEP model whose kept mesh is coarser than the importer's 0.005 mm promise used to import with only a line on stderr. Its facets stand inside the true surface on a convex wall, so a real gouge up to the mesh's error could pass. Following the maintainer's decision on #864:

1. **Flagged.** The import records the error of the mesh it kept (held work on this branch: `step_refine`, `step::parse_with_chord`; a refinement pass that is thrown away no longer lends its tolerance to the coarser mesh that is kept). Above the cap, the model carries `schema::ReducedFidelity { chord_mm }`. It is set by `ImportModel`, `UpdateModel`, `ImportFixture` and `AddFixtureModel`, kept by a repair, restored by undo and by undoing a delete, and saved as `coarse_mm` on that entity only.
2. **Tightened while honest.** `VerifyContext::model_excess` (achieved error less the cap) is a separate field, not mixed into `gouge_tol`. The gouge laws subtract it from their tolerance while a positive tolerance is left.
3. **Refused past that.** Once the excess uses a whole tolerance, the laws read untightened and the program gate refuses each operation judged against that model, by name. The program sim does not judge either, so no gouge line is read off such a mesh.

With no flag (every model that fits the budget, STL, OBJ, every older project) `model_excess` is 0 and every law, golden and saved byte is as before.

### Laws that read the excess

| Law | Where |
|---|---|
| (b) section / tangency floor - the joints and the whole-move wall reading (#942) share it | `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:104` |
| (b2) solid law `allow` | `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs:283` |
| (f) finish envelope, gouge half | `crates/sim/src/verify/finish.rs:104` |
| containment kinds' solid law (`contain_into`) | `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:3203` |
| lathe axial hole verdict (`drilling::axial_warnings`) | `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs:2944` |
| program sim verdict (`deviate`) | `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` (`simulate_document`), `crates/app/src/stock_sim_carry.rs:268` (`judge`), through `model_fidelity::verdict_tol` |

The one test both the laws and the gate read is `verify::excess_floor` (`crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs`).

### Laws that do not (said, not hidden)

- **Refused on any reduced-fidelity model** (`operation::fidelity_law::excess_aware`), because their gouge laws are not threaded yet: 2D chamfer, deburr, trace, engrave, probe, the cross drill, every multi-axis and rotary kind, turning, plasma.
- **Collision laws, not tightened:** shank and holder reach (c, c3), rapids in stock (d), the turning rapid, bar-feed and holder scans. While an operation still posts the excess is under 0.01 mm.
- **Display only, unchanged:** the machined-surface classes and the viewport deviation preview still colour at 0.01 mm.
- **Fixtures** that came through the same importer: judged by their bounding box grown by the error on every side, and their mesh is not offered to the mesh law, which only ever acquits. Stock: a stock copied from a model reads that model's excess.

All of the above is filed as #904.

### A metre-unit STEP file

Since #839 it stops at the kernel's least tolerance, 0.01 mm, above the cap. It now gets the same flag and the same treatment: 0.005 mm of tolerance is left, so its mill verdicts are tightened and it still posts; the kinds listed above are refused. Scaling to millimetres before meshing was not attempted (it means transforming the kernel's shell before tessellation); it is in #904. An inch file meets the promise and is not flagged (pinned).

## What the user sees

- Model page: `Reduced fidelity: surfaces are approximated to within 0.012 mm`, with a hint: "This model was too large to import at full detail. Gouge checks against it are stricter to make up for that; when it is too coarse to check at all, its operations are refused at the post. Re-import with a larger budget to clear this."
- Import status line: `imported part - Reduced fidelity: surfaces are approximated to within 0.012 mm`.
- Post refusal: `OP: model 'part' was imported too coarsely to verify; re-import with a larger budget (surfaces are approximated to within 0.030 mm)`.
- For a kind that cannot be judged yet: `OP: model 'part' was imported at reduced fidelity (surfaces are approximated to within 0.012 mm) and this kind of operation cannot be verified against it; re-import with a larger budget`.
- The stock sim line: `stock sim did not judge this program: model 'part' was imported too coarsely to verify; re-import with a larger budget (...)`.

"Re-import with a larger budget" is the maintainer's wording; the facet budget is not a user setting yet (#904).

## MCP

- `import_model` adds `reduced_fidelity: { approximation_mm, promised_mm, note }` for such a model, and nothing for a normal one.
- `get_job` carries the same object on that model's entry only.
- Both tool descriptions say so. The `camcraft-mcp` skill text is a process file and was not edited.

## Pins

- `crates/sim/tests/model_excess.rs`: a cut 0.006 mm into a convex wall (less than the 0.0122 mm mesh error) passes at full fidelity and is convicted with the excess; a nominal ring is clean both ways; an exactly finished flat face is never a gouge at any excess; past the tolerance the law reads exactly as at full fidelity; `excess_floor` only tightens.
- `crates/app/tests/model_fidelity.rs`: an over-budget import is flagged with its own error and one that fits is not (through undo, redo, update, repair-style update, delete and undo, stock copy); the inch fixture is not flagged and the metre sample is, at 0.01 mm with 0.005 mm left; a project keeps the flag, and one without it saves back byte for byte; the program verdict convicts a floor cut 0.006 mm deep on the reduced model and passes it at full fidelity, while an exact flat face posts on both; a model at 0.03 mm is refused by name, with no gouge line even for a path sunk 1 mm, and does not post; a 2D chamfer is refused on any reduced model; a coarse fixture's box grows and its mesh is withheld; MCP `import_model` and `get_job` facts.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/model_fidelity.rs`: the model page shows the flag and the achieved error for a reduced model and nothing for a normal one (AccessKit labels).
- Held from the earlier worker: `step_refine::tests::*`, `crates/app/tests/step_fidelity.rs`.

## Gate

On the final head `6a40e3b6` (four merges of `origin/main`, the last at e0cb0049 = v0.18.0, + two test commits):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green, 4 steps, 0 failed, 21.3 min. sim suites (18 binaries), motion suites (16), app suites (211), ui suites (12, the lib with `model_fidelity` included).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --tests`: green, 53 test binaries, 432 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Merges of `main`:

- v0.18.0 (e0cb0049, with #942 and #1003): **no conflict**. `section.rs` merged clean; #942's whole-arc wall reading takes the same `floor` variable as the joints, so it already reads against the tightened floor. Pinned: `boundary_arc_walls::the_whole_arc_reading_answers_to_a_coarse_models_tightened_floor` (a corner between an arc's joints is convicted between the plain and the tightened floor on a coarse model, clean at full fidelity and outside the tightened floor). `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock` are main's 0.18.0; `docs/decisions/864-reduced-fidelity.md` stays in `docs/decisions/`. The `boundary_arc_walls` context (new on main) takes `..Default::default()`.
- Earlier: `crates/app/src/commands/update_model.rs` (#826's plate snapshot and this PR's fidelity fields were both added to `UpdateModel`; both kept) and the two `contain_into` calls in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` (#843's `cutter` argument and this PR's trailing `material.excess`; both kept).
- The joint reading with the excess is pinned by `verify_arc_reading::boundary_mode_judges_the_union_joints_against_the_tightened_floor`; #839's `boundary_mode_keeps_the_old_joints_so_a_sharp_vertex_on_one_stays_convicted` still passes.

The diff touches 43 existing test files with one line each (`..Default::default()` on their `VerifyContext` literal); no golden, snapshot or expected value changed.

## Not exercised

- The envelope law (f) and the containment solid law are tightened through the same helper as (b), but have no fixture-level pin on a reduced-fidelity model (#904).
- No real over-budget model (30 M facets) was imported; the pins force the small fixture over a test-only budget.
- The GUI was not launched; the page is pinned structurally only. Snapshot PNGs are untouched.
- The release tier and the heavy `--ignored` lanes were not run.

Changelog: A STEP model imported coarser than 0.005 mm is flagged as reduced fidelity (model page, MCP, project file); gouge checks against it are tightened by the excess, and its operations are refused at the post once it is too coarse to verify
Effort: max (escalated once, from high)

Fixes #864

title: feat(ui): two orientation dropdowns, one section everywhere
body:
## What changed

The setup orientation UI is two dropdowns, one section everywhere
(#771, stacked on #770):

- **Plane orientation** - Axes (#769, the default), Points (#555),
  Face (#330), Manual (the preset/angles picker), and the new
  **Cylinder angle**: one pick on a bore's or cylinder's curved wall
  names its axis from the wall's own facet normals (any two
  non-parallel wall normals cross exactly along it; every other
  normal is verified - a mixed patch is refused by name, never
  misread). The axis lands on a chosen world axis (+X/+Y/+Z), turned
  by an angle about it, the part turning about its bounds centre.
- **Orientation point** - the parts' bounds or the setup's stock
  (corner or centre), or a picked vertex. The WCS's rotation is kept:
  the frame comes from the plane side; each setup places its own WCS
  (`SetWcsOrigin::for_setup`), never the active one's.
- The section is ONE component (`setup_orient_pick::section`) mounted
  on the Setups overview AND each setup's Settings page - same
  dropdowns, same options, same look (the user's law). The old rows
  keep their own entry points and draw verbatim as the expanded
  content.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/orient_dropdowns.rs` (9 tests): a tilted
  cylinder's wall lands its axis on Z (end to end: every wall normal
  in the setup frame perpendicular to it); a 90-degree angle swings
  the wall about the landed axis and keeps the axis put; X and Y
  landings; a flat face, an edge and a NaN angle refused by name; the
  model box corner/centre places the setup's WCS (undo removes it);
  the stock box corner/centre; placing the origin keeps a pre-set
  rotation; each setup places its own WCS (Setup1 untouched); the
  missing model and stock refused by name.
- UI: the structural twin `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure`
  rewritten for the dropdowns (two combos, axes rows expanded by
  default, the other methods behind their entries, the origin side's
  box reading); `setup_picks_disarm` switches the dropdown before
  clicking the plane/points rows (switch_plane_method) - all 8 green
  again. Battery green: ui 37 (setup_axis, structural, disarm,
  one_pick_rule, plane, points, align), orient_dropdowns 9,
  align_axes 9, axis_align 10, plane_align 9, points_align 8,
  turn_pivot 5; clippy clean on camcraft-app and camcraft-ui.

## What was not exercised

- The dropdown's method selection persists per egui session only (a
  page reopen resets to the defaults); the picks themselves follow
  the #664 pause law as before.
- The vertex origin pick needs a model with vertices in the viewport -
  pinned at the app layer (`place_setup_origin`'s Vertex arm reads
  the same `vertex` the 3-2-1 flow uses); the full viewport click
  path is covered by the disarm suites' click plumbing, not a new
  end-to-end vertex case.

Changelog: feat(ui): two orientation dropdowns on the Setups pages - plane method (axes/points/face/manual/cylinder angle) and origin point (model box/stock box/vertex), one section everywhere (#771, PR)

title: feat(align): part alignment from two perpendicular edge picks (full 3D frame)
body:
## What changed

Part alignment from two perpendicular edge picks (#769): the picks
define the full 3D frame.

- `pick::align_from_axes` (`crates/app/src/pick/axis.rs`): with both
  +Y and +X picked, their directions - read through the setup's held
  alignment, so it composes after a face lay - define the frame: the
  primary axis lands exactly, the secondary is orthogonalized against
  it (landing within the skew it came with), and +Z lands on the
  picks' cross, the right-hand rule. The part turns about the centre
  of its bounds; the origin is NOT set (the work offset stays where
  it is placed). A left-handed pair is honoured literally (the part
  lands as picked) instead of refused; only (nearly) parallel picks
  refuse, by name. The landing is proved before the command stores
  anything.
- `AlignPartToSetup::align_from_axes` / `check_align`
  (`commands/setup_align.rs`): the command constructors, same
  refusals by name.
- The UI axis panel (`egui_app/setup_axis_pick.rs`, the `CommandKind`
  renamed `TurnPartInPlane` -> `AlignPartFromAxes`): same rows, same
  picks, same flip toggles - the meaning grew. One picked axis keeps
  the in-plane turn (#557 unchanged, `turn_in_plane` kept for its
  callers); the words under Apply say which case applies.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/align_axes.rs` (9 tests): the user's exact
  case (a down-Z edge picked +Y, a -X edge picked +X - full 3D
  landing, the picks' cross up, centre unmoved); a vertical edge as +Y
  lays the part on its side; in-plane picks subsume `turn_in_plane`
  exactly (positions and rotation, pinned); one axis alone keeps the
  in-plane turn; a skewed secondary lands within its own skew;
  parallel picks refused by name; a left-handed pair honoured
  literally (pinned as deliberate); picks compose after a held
  alignment; a face pick still refuses by name.
- New UI pin `two_picks_with_an_upright_edge_align_the_part_in_full_3d`
  (setup_axis_tests): the round that #557 refused - upright edge +
  top edge - leaves Apply on, applies, lands the picks on their axes
  with +Z on their cross, never touches the work offset, and one undo
  restores. Existing surface pins updated for the renamed command and
  the new status words.
- Battery green: align_axes 9, axis_align 10, plane_align 9,
  points_align 8, turn_pivot 5, ui setup_axis 9; clippy clean on
  camcraft-app and camcraft-ui.

## What was not exercised

- The origin is untouched by design (the work-offset flows own it).
- `turn_in_plane` and `in_plane_turn_deg` are unchanged; their callers
  (single-pick panel round, MCP align tools) keep their behavior -
  the MCP surface exposing `turn_in_plane` still turns in-plane only.

Changelog: feat(align): part alignment from two perpendicular edge picks - the picks define the full 3D frame, +Z by the right-hand rule (#769, PR #770)

Fixes #769

body:
**Stacked on #715** (grblHAL post, not merged yet): this branch is #715's head plus one commit, so the diff shows #715's files too until it merges. Only commit `feat(machines): Sienci AltMill ...` is this PR. Fork synced at v0.16.0 (via #715's base).

## What changed

Three built-in machines for Sienci's AltMill routers, which run grblHAL on the SLB-EXT controller. They post through the existing `grblhal.cps`; there is no AltMill post file.

- `assets/machines/sienci-altmill-2x4.mch`, `-4x4.mch` and `-4x8.mch`, registered in `posting::MACHINES` as "Sienci AltMill 2x4", "4x4" and "4x8".
- **Units mm, 3 axes.** The Vortex rotary waits on #714.
- **`safe_retract: 0.0`.** The AltMill homes (`$22=79`: homing on, required at startup, machine origin 0 at home; Z homes up; soft limits on). So every tool change lifts `G53 G0 Z0`, then `T<n> M6` stands alone. gSender and ncSender take over on `T<n> M6` (manual change, RapidChange or Sienci ATC), so the post needs no ATC or manual mode and no rack list.
- **Figures** from Sienci's spec pages. The 4x4's travel (1260 x 1248 x 170 mm soft limits), axis rates and spindle range (1200-24000 rpm) are read from a 4x4's own `$$`. Every figure and its source is in `docs/decisions/728-altmill.md`.

## How tested

- New `altmill_machines.rs` (4 tests): each file's figures; the `G53 G0 Z0` lift before each `T<n> M6` and no G43/G43.1/G49; a spindle speed past 24000 refused; the 4x4 two-tool program locked byte-exact in mm and inch (`golden/nc/grblhal/altmill_4x4_two_tool{,_inch}.nc`).
- Green on macOS: `altmill_machines`, `machine` (the library list now pins the three), `machine_library`, `machine_edit`, `conformance`, `grblhal_post`, `tormach_machines`. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test altmill_machines -- -D warnings` is clean.

- **Machine run:** the 4x4 golden air-cut on an AltMill 4x4 (SLB-EXT) with ncSender and an 8-pocket RapidChange ATC; the `T3 M6` and `T4 M6` changes ran cleanly (comment below).

## Not exercised

- The 2x4 and 4x8 figures come from Sienci's pages only; an owner's `$$` would confirm them.
- Full workspace gate not run (disk-limited machine); the suites above are the ones that touch the machine registry and the grblHAL post.

title: feat(app,ui): set the WCS from any set of feature picks (#701)
body:
You can select edges, vertices, faces and cylinder walls and say which axis each one sets (#701) - the WCS lands on the fitted frame, undoable like any other placement.

## The change

**App lane** - `pick::roles.rs`: `Role` (`Origin | X | Y | Z`) and `align_roles(world, picks) -> Result<Alignment, String>`, returning the same `Alignment` `pick::align`'s 3-2-1 fit already returns, so one fit law answers both. Frame law: among the axis picks present, read in the priority order Z, X, Y - first exact, second projected perpendicular, third derived to close the right-handed frame (a third axis pick is overridden wholesale, not blended). An origin pick anchors on the feature's natural centre; without one, the origin falls on the second axis pick's anchor (an edge's start, a face's centroid, a wall's centre), projected onto the first pick's plane when that pick is a face. Refusals come back as words, in order: too few picks, a duplicated role, fewer than two axes, an unresolvable datum, an unsupportable tilt, a stale feature id. Cylinder walls fit by covariance null-space (Jacobi) plus a Kasa circle, on the wall's local facets transformed by the feature's `setup_align::view_pose` - the same law the plane fit already uses.

**UI lane** - the Setups page grows a "Set WCS from features" row (`egui_app::wcs_pick_row.rs`) over a draft module (`wcs_pick.rs`): arming it keeps the toolbar's pick mode (faces, edges, corners and walls all feed the one draft), the role box says what the next pick sets, and each viewport pick is stamped into that role's slot - re-picking a role replaces its pick in place. One draft at a time: arming this row disarms the plane-pick and axis-pick drafts and vice versa, and the wcs draft pauses while its setup row is hidden (the #664 law). Apply is gated live by `align_roles` itself - the refusal words ride the row inline and on the disabled button, so the UI's why is the command's own words - and only answers on the ACTIVE setup's row: `SetWcs` places the active setup's WCS, so a greyed Apply on another setup's row says to make that row's setup active first. Apply queues the existing undoable `CommandKind::SetWcs`; the same command the WCS pane's anchor grid already sends. No new command kind, no world writes outside commands. Rationale in `docs/decisions/701-wcs-from-features.md`.

## Pins (red before the fix, green with it)

- `wcs_roles::z_face_x_edge_and_origin_corner_reproduce_the_3_2_1_frame` - a Z face, X edge and origin corner digit-for-digit reproduce `align_321`.
- `wcs_roles::the_third_axis_role_is_derived_right_handed_never_read` - three axis picks: the third is overridden wholesale and the frame is right-handed.
- `wcs_roles::the_origin_projects_onto_a_z_face_and_anchors_on_its_centroid` - an origin vertex pick anchors on the face's centroid, projected onto its plane.
- `wcs_roles::a_tilted_bore_wall_fits_its_real_axis_and_centre` / `a_bore_wall_picked_as_z_stands_upright_with_a_pinned_sign` - the wall fit, both flat and tilted, sign pinned by the axis role.
- `wcs_roles::every_degenerate_role_set_is_refused_by_name` - each refusal sentence, pinned.
- `wcs_roles::an_edge_as_the_first_axis_reads_unit_on_a_part_tipped_off_the_table` - the first-axis edge is normalised right after reading: unit length and square axes on a tipped part, origin on the block.
- `egui_app::wcs_pick_tests::*` - five kittest tests on the live row: arming keeps the pick mode and stops the other drafts; an incomplete set greys Apply and shows the app's own words; role picks land in the draft (never in the open operation) and Apply queues one undoable `SetWcs` that undo/redo round-trips; re-picking replaces only that role's pick; and with two setups, the row on the inactive one greys Apply, queues nothing, says to make that setup active, and once active the same frame moves that setup's own WCS while the other setup's work zero stays put.
- `wcs_pick::tests::*` - three draft-module tests: role default and mutual disarm, replace-in-place, a paused draft takes nothing.

## Tested

- The pin commit alone is red: at `35f399d1` the `wcs_roles` binary does not compile (no `pick::Role`/`align_roles` on main) and the ui lib does not compile (no `crate::wcs_pick`, row unwired) - the API and surface the pins demand did not exist.
- Green at head `d2663a3f`, merged with current `origin/main` (`f490458a`): `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` - 7 passed. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` - 110 passed. Full `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (state.rs and interact.rs touched) - 538 passed, 5 ignored. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` - clean.

## Follow-ups

- MCP parity: the agent surface still takes only an absolute origin/quaternion (`set_wcs`); filed as #937 to add a feature-pick version over the same `align_roles` law.
- Arc/circle centre picks (#705/#692) as the Origin role, now that `feature_arc` has landed - not wired here (`PickKinds.centres: false` in the wcs mode).
- A wall picked as an axis takes its sign from the hemisphere rule, not from the origin pick as an edge does (review round 3): deterministic, but siding it by the origin pick would match what a user expects.

Changelog: the Setups page can set the WCS from feature picks - click faces, edges, corners and walls in the viewport, say what each one sets, and Apply places the work zero on the fitted frame, undo and redo included (#701)

Fixes #701

title: feat(ui): viewport origin gizmos wear their names (#727)
body:
With several setups on screen, every origin triad looks alike - nothing in the viewport says whose zero is whose (#727).

## The change

Every origin gizmo now labels itself at its origin. Each work-offset triad draws the entity name the Setup pane already uses (`G54` for the first setup, `Setup2/WCS` for the second) in bright triad blue at the ordinary overlay-label size; the dimmed world axes draw `World` in neutral gray dimmed by `WORLD_DIM`, like the lines under them. `Gizmo` (`interact.rs`) grows one `name` field, filled in `gizmos()` - which already honors the Models pane's eye (`hidden_offsets`) and the `show_world_axes` gate, so a hidden offset loses its name with its lines for free. `overlay_labels` places each name just below the projected origin (`NAME_DROP_UV = 0.02`, same currency as `axis_note::NOTE_DROP_UV`), emitted before the gizmo's `X`/`Y`/`Z` tips. Only the letters keep the big `is_axis_label` font. Rationale in `docs/decisions/727-viewport-gizmo-labels.md`.

## The switch (#645)

On top of the names, the review on #645 asked for a user switch, so the browser pane grows a `Show origin names` checkbox next to `Show world origin axes`. It gates only the name rows: the big `X`/`Y`/`Z` letters and the triad's strokes ignore it. The choice is a per-user preference, not document state - nothing touches the world or the command history - and it persists in `view.json` in the OS config folder next to the recents file (`recent`'s resolver, #662, so `CAMCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the folder), written at once on the flip and read back at startup. The default is ON, the #727 decision: shipping the switch changes no existing viewport. A missing, unreadable or corrupt file - or a foreign one, the `camcraft-view/1` format tag says - starts at the defaults with a logged reason, never a crash, and unknown keys stay ignored so newer builds keep working.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `gizmo_tests::the_dimmed_world_axes_are_labelled_world` - the fresh world's set carries `World`, neutral gray (equal channels) and dimmed like the axes.
- `gizmo_tests::each_triad_is_labelled_with_its_own_offset_name` - two setups: both `G54` and `Setup2/WCS` label their own origins, bright against the letters.
- `gizmo_tests::an_offset_name_stands_at_its_origin_not_its_axis_tips` - the name rides the projected origin horizontally, a small uv drop below it, not crowded onto the tips.
- `gizmo_tests::a_hidden_work_offset_drops_its_name_with_its_gizmo` - the pane's eye and the label agree.
- `gizmo_tests::gizmo_names_are_not_the_big_axis_letters` - `is_axis_label` still answers only X/Y/Z.
- Re-pins: label counts 3→4 (fresh world), 6→8 (two gizmos), 3→4 (moved origin); `axis_note_tests`' fresh-world set pins exactly `["World", "X", "Y", "Z"]`, which fixes each gizmo's emission order name-first.
- `setup_chip_tests`' no-G54-on-Setup2's-op clause narrows to plane chips (`" · "`): the `G54` origin name is Setup1's own, legitimately - the law was about op chips, and it still holds there.
- `structural::origin_names_paint_on_and_quiet_off_letters_and_lines_always` - the re-review's both-states shell check: with the switch on the seeded document's `G54` name row paints inside the viewport (the properties pane also reads `G54`, so the probe sits between the pane anchors, as the view-cube check does); the checkbox click drops it from the painted frame while the `X`/`Y`/`Z` letters and the triad's strokes come through untouched. The test redirects `view_store` to a temp folder so the flip never writes the real user's `view.json`.
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs` (new integration suite) - the persistence law: a flipped choice round-trips through the file across a "restart", a missing file is a quiet default start, a corrupt or foreign-format file starts at the defaults with a reason and never crashes, unknown keys stay ignored, and a `CAMCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` override is the folder the choice round-trips through (`recent::config_dir_for` with a fake getter, as `recent_files` does).

## Tested

- Red first: with only the pins committed, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests` ran 8 failed / 7 passed, exactly the new and re-pinned label tests - e.g. the fresh world's labels were `["X", "Y", "Z"]` with no name.
- Green: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests setup_chip_tests` - 17 passed, 0 failed.
- Full lib: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` - 490 passed, 0 failed (5 ignored). An earlier run of the same command failed only on `structural::shell_structure_light`, a theme-sync test this change never touches; it passes in isolation and on re-run - pre-existing parallel global-theme-state flakiness, already noted on #638.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test view_prefs` - 5 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` - clean.
- Not exercised: the on-screen labels themselves - the producers are pinned instead.

Changelog: viewport origin gizmos now wear their names - each work-offset triad shows its Setup-pane name at its origin, the neutral world axes show World (#727) - and a persisted "Show origin names" checkbox in the browser pane turns the name rows on and off, kept in the per-user `view.json` (#645)

Fixes #727

title: feat(post): EDM condition table as user data in the .mch edm section
body:
**Stacked on #551** (EDM machine kinds). Its commits show here until #551 merges; this PR adds one commit on top.

## What changed

`edm.conditions[]` in the `.mch` `edm` section (#531, part of #290, design D4):
- Each condition is `{ id, name, gap, wire_diameter | undersize, role: rough|skim|finish, notes }`. It holds only the geometry a toolpath needs. Power and flushing stay the control's, selected by `id`.
- `id` is the control's own selector, required and unique; a numeric id reads as its word. Lengths scale with the file's unit. Gap and undersize may be 0; a wire diameter must be positive.
- A garbled entry refuses the file, naming its id, and `is_sane` restates the law for project files.
- `Edm::condition(machine, id, need)` is the door the first EDM op (#532) calls at command creation. A missing condition, or an unstated field the op needs (gap, wire diameter, undersize), is refused by name before any generator runs.
- No conditions ship. Tests use an explicitly synthetic table.

## How tested

- New `edm_conditions`, 6/6:
  - a stated table reads, and the template states none;
  - an inch file's gap reads in mm;
  - the lookup refuses a missing condition or field by name;
  - eight garbled tables each refuse the file;
  - a hand-edited project machine with duplicate ids or a NaN gap is not sane;
  - the table rides the project file.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`, escalated to batch: geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app are green, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on all 8 crates. ui: only the five known reds that are also red on main.
- Named: `edm_machine` 7, `machine` 32, `machine_library` 11, and `camcraft-post` all pass.

## Not exercised

- An EDM op using the door; that is #532.
- A real control's condition numbers; the data is the user's.

Changelog: EDM machine files can state the generator conditions (spark gap, wire diameter, undersize) an EDM operation selects by id (#531)

Fixes #531

title: feat(post): wire_edm and sinker_edm machine kinds and the .mch edm section
body:
## What changed

The first EDM sub-issue of #290 (design D1):
- **Machine kinds.** `Kind::WireEdm` / `Kind::SinkerEdm`, declared only (`wire_edm`, `sinker_edm`, plus synonyms such as `wedm` and `die-sinker`). No axis inventory infers an EDM. The required axes are X+Y for wire and Z for sinker. A blank EDM machine has no spindle or coolant.
- **`.mch` `edm` section** (`crates/post/src/machine/edm.rs`). Wire: lower and upper guide planes, max taper, wire diameters, AWT. Sinker: orbit patterns (CamCraft's geometry name plus the control's word), max orbit radius, pickup. Every key is optional and absent means not stated. Lengths scale with the file's unit. A garbled value refuses the file by name, and the same law is restated in `is_sane` for project files.
- **No current op family admits an EDM**, so every op is refused at the door on an EDM setup.
- **Post-time family gate (safety).** `op_streams` now re-checks every op's family against its own setup's machine and refuses by name. Before this, an op made on a mill still posted in a milling dialect after its setup was remounted onto a lathe or an EDM; the door only guarded creation.
- **No EDM post serves yet** (`post_serves` is false for both kinds).
- **Templates are test fixtures for now.** The empty wire/sinker templates live in `crates/app/tests/edm/` because every library machine must have a post. They join the library with #533 / #542.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the kinds and the section.

## How tested

- New `edm_machine`, 7/7: templates parse and declare their kinds; a filled section reads and inch-scales; nine garbled values each refuse by name; the kind words round-trip and unknown kinds still refuse; no milling op enters an EDM setup; **a milling op remounted onto an EDM is refused at post, and undo restores the post**; a project round-trips the section.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick`, escalated to batch, 913 s:
  - geometry, cl, tools, post, sim and motion are green, and clippy `-D warnings` is clean on all 8 crates.
  - app: green apart from `machine_library`, fixed by the follow-up commit that moved the templates to fixtures. The lathe, turning, mill-turn, drilling, c-axis, program-entry and conformance suites all ran, and the new gate's message appears in none of their logs, so it refused nothing outside its own test.
  - ui: only the five known reds that are also red on main.
- After the follow-up: `machine_library` 11/11, `machine` 32/32, `edm_machine` 7/7.

## Not exercised

- Any real EDM control. No EDM op or post exists yet; this is the schema seam only.
- The UI machine editor's kind picker still lists only mill, lathe and mill-turn (EDM setup pages are #535).

Changelog: Machine files can declare wire_edm and sinker_edm machines with an edm section; a program whose operation its setup's machine cannot run is refused at post (#530)

Fixes #530
